The proposed termwise validity record is deferred as duplication of the general convex-disjunctive-hull theorem. Multi-term selector sparsity, general support duality, and split lattice geometry are excluded as sibling scopes.

children.title: Split Disjunction Geometry
children.top_down_role: Convexification structure induced by complementary split regions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Maximal Lattice-Free Geometry of a Split Slab
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Maximality of the open slab associated with a primitive split normal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\pi\in\mathbb Z^p\) be primitive and \(\pi_0\in\mathbb Z\). The open convex set \[S=\{(x_I,x_C):\pi_0<\pi^{\mathsf T}x_I<\pi_0+1\}\] contains no point of \(\mathbb Z^p\times\mathbb R^q\), and it is maximal among open convex subsets of \(\mathbb R^{p+q}\) with this property. Its two boundary hyperplanes contain mixed-integer points because \(\pi^{\mathsf T}\mathbb Z^p=\mathbb Z\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primitive split defines a maximal lattice-free slab between two consecutive integer hyperplanes.
assumptions_latex: \(\pi\in\mathbb Z^p\) is primitive.
\(\pi_0\in\mathbb Z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S\) is a maximal lattice-free open convex set for \(\mathbb Z^p\times\mathbb R^q\).
knowledge_statements.title: Maximal Lattice-Free Geometry of a Split Slab
Split Disjunction Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lattice-free slab geometry underlying a split disjunction in mixed-integer space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x=(x_I,x_C)\in\mathbb R^{p+q}\), where \(x_I\) is constrained to be integral. For a primitive vector \(\pi\in\mathbb Z^p\) and \(\pi_0\in\mathbb Z\), the split disjunction is
\[\pi^{\mathsf T}x_I\le\pi_0\quad\vee\quad \pi^{\mathsf T}x_I\ge\pi_0+1.\]
Its excluded open slab is \(S=\{x:\pi_0<\pi^{\mathsf T}x_I<\pi_0+1\}\). The slab contains no point with integral \(x_I\); hence every mixed-integer point satisfies one of the two closed halfspaces. Intersecting both terms with a relaxation \(P\) yields the split set used for convexification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A split divides mixed-integer space into two parallel closed halfspaces and excludes an open unit-width slab containing no admissible integer point.
assumptions_latex: \(x_I\in\mathbb Z^p\) at every admissible mixed-integer point.
\(\pi\in\mathbb Z^p\) is primitive and \(\pi_0\in\mathbb Z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every admissible mixed-integer point lies in \(\{\pi^{\mathsf T}x_I\le\pi_0\}\cup\{\pi^{\mathsf T}x_I\ge\pi_0+1\}\).

notation.meaning: integer normal defining the split direction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The mathematical definition of the split disjunction and its lattice-free open slab is correct, and the definition kind fits the leaf. The phrase unit-width in the plain statement should be understood as unit lattice width rather than Euclidean width. A mixed-integer convexification source with a specific locator is required.

children.title: Two-Term–Split Equivalence Regimes
children.top_down_role: Settings where the two families coincide or yield comparable hull structure.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Relative-to-P Equivalence Does Not Imply Global Split Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes equality after restriction to a relaxation from equality of defining halfspaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Equality of two disjunctions after intersection with a common set \(P\) does not imply that their defining halfspaces have split geometry. For example, in \(\mathbb R^2\), let \(P=\{(0,0)\}\), \[H_1=\{x:x_1\le0\},\qquad H_2=\{x:x_2\ge1\}.\] Then \(P\cap(H_1\cup H_2)=P\), which also equals \[P\cap\bigl(\{x:x_1\le0\}\cup\{x:x_1\ge1\}\bigr),\] although \(H_1,H_2\) have nonparallel boundaries and therefore are not themselves a split pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A restricted relaxation may make a nonsplit two-term disjunction trace-equivalent to a split even though their ambient halfspaces differ.
assumptions_latex: \(P,H_1,H_2\) are the displayed sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Trace equivalence on \(P\) is strictly weaker than global split equivalence.
knowledge_statements.title: Relative-to-P Equivalence Does Not Imply Global Split Geometry
Two-Term–Split Equivalence Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact criterion for a two-term halfspace disjunction to be a mixed-integer split.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider a two-term disjunction whose terms are \(P\cap H_1\) and \(P\cap H_2\), where \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^{p+q}\). It is a split disjunction for the lattice restriction \(x_I\in\mathbb Z^p\) exactly when, after multiplication of each defining inequality by a positive scalar, there exist a primitive \(\pi\in\mathbb Z^p\) and \(\pi_0\in\mathbb Z\) such that
\[H_1=\{x:\pi^{\mathsf T}x_I\le\pi_0\},\qquad H_2=\{x:\pi^{\mathsf T}x_I\ge\pi_0+1\}.\]
Thus every split is two-term, but a two-term disjunction with nonparallel boundaries, continuous-variable coefficients, or a non-unit lattice gap need not be a split.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A two-term halfspace disjunction is a split precisely when its parallel boundaries have a primitive integer normal and bound consecutive integer levels.
assumptions_latex: The two alternatives are intersections of a common set \(P\) with closed halfspaces.
Integrality is imposed only on \(x_I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Two-term and split geometry coincide exactly under the displayed consecutive-lattice-hyperplane condition.

notation.meaning: common continuous relaxation intersected with each term

review_flags: standard_field_rationale:criterion follows from the standard definition of a split disjunction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed consecutive-lattice-hyperplane condition is the standard geometric form of a split and the condition content kind fits the leaf. However, a source is needed to resolve whether equivalence is meant for the defining halfspaces themselves or only for their intersections with P, since those notions can differ on a restricted P.

children.title: Multi-Term Disjunctions
children.top_down_role: Convexification of unions containing several alternatives.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sparse Activity in a Multi-Term Disjunctive Hull
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Carathéodory sparsity of active alternatives in a finite convex disjunction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty convex sets. Every \(x\in\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_{k=1}^m C_k)\) admits \[x=\sum_{k=1}^m\lambda_kc_k,\qquad c_k\in C_k,\quad \lambda\in\Delta_m,\] with at most \(\min\{m,n+1\}\) positive components of \(\lambda\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every point in a multi-term disjunctive hull needs positive weight on at most n+1 alternatives.
assumptions_latex: \(m<\infty\).
Each \(C_k\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty and convex.

notation.meaning: Simplex of nonnegative m-vectors whose components sum to one.

knowledge_statements.title: Sparse Activity in a Multi-Term Disjunctive Hull
Multi-Term Disjunctions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact lifted convex-hull representation for finitely many compact convex alternatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C_k\subset\mathbb R^n\), \(k=1,\ldots,m\), be nonempty compact convex sets. Then
\[\operatorname{conv}\!\left(\bigcup_{k=1}^m C_k\right)=\left\{x:x=\sum_{k=1}^m x^k,\ x^k\in\lambda_kC_k,\ \lambda_k\ge0,\ \sum_{k=1}^m\lambda_k=1\right\}.\]
At an integral selector vector with one component equal to one, the lifting represents a single alternative; allowing the selector vector in the simplex produces its convex hull. Compactness ensures that a zero multiplier contributes only \(x^k=0\), avoiding recession-direction qualifications required for general unbounded alternatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The hull of finitely many compact convex alternatives uses one scaled variable block per term and simplex weights summing to one.
assumptions_latex: Every \(C_k\) is a nonempty compact convex subset of \(\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Projection of the displayed simplex-scaled formulation equals \(\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_{k=1}^m C_k)\).

notation.meaning: scaled contribution associated with alternative k

review_flags: standard_field_rationale:finite convex-union hull obtained by simplex-weighted perspective lifting

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite simplex-scaled formulation is correct for nonempty compact convex alternatives, including the treatment of zero multipliers. The representation content kind matches the multi-term disjunction leaf. No authoritative source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Convex Disjunctive Hulls
children.top_down_role: Hull representations for unions whose individual terms are convex sets.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Closed Convex Alternatives Can Have a Nonclosed Hull
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp closedness boundary for unbounded convex disjunctive hulls.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In \(\mathbb R^2\), let \(C_1=\{(x,y):x>0,\ y\ge 1/x\}\) and \(C_2=\{(0,0)\}\). Both sets are nonempty, closed, and convex, but \[\operatorname{conv}(C_1\cup C_2)=\{(u,v):u>0,\ v>0\}\cup\{(0,0)\},\] which is not closed, and \(\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(C_1\cup C_2)=\mathbb R_+^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even two closed convex alternatives can have a nonclosed convex hull when unbounded recession behavior is not suitably controlled.
assumptions_latex: \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) are the displayed subsets of \(\mathbb R^2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{conv}(C_1\cup C_2)\) is not closed and has closure \(\mathbb R_+^2\).
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Closed Convex Alternatives Can Have a Nonclosed Hull

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Support-Function Characterization of a Convex Disjunctive Hull
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual halfspace characterization of the hull of finitely many alternatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty and let \(D=\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_{i=1}^m C_i)\). Then, for every \(a\in\mathbb R^n\), \[\sigma_D(a)=\max_{1\le i\le m}\sigma_{C_i}(a).\] Consequently, \[\operatorname{cl}D=\bigcap_{a\in\mathbb R^n}\left\{x:a^{\mathsf T}x\le\max_i\sigma_{C_i}(a)\right\}.\] In particular, an affine inequality is valid for \(D\) exactly when it is valid for every alternative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The support function of a finite disjunctive hull is the maximum of the alternatives' support functions, so affine validity can be checked term by term.
assumptions_latex: \(m<\infty\).
Each \(C_i\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sigma_D=\max_i\sigma_{C_i}\), and the displayed intersection represents \(\operatorname{cl}D\).

notation.meaning: Support function of the set C.
Convex hull of the union of the alternatives.

knowledge_statements.title: Support-Function Characterization of a Convex Disjunctive Hull
Convex Disjunctive Hulls
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-union homogenized representation of a convex disjunctive hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty convex sets and define \(K_i=\operatorname{cone}(\{(1,x):x\in C_i\})\). Then
\[
\operatorname{conv}\!\left(\bigcup_{i=1}^m C_i\right)=\left\{x:\ x=\sum_{i=1}^m y_i,\ \sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i=1,\ (\lambda_i,y_i)\in K_i\ \text{for every }i\right\}.
\]
Thus each hull point is assembled from alternative-specific scaled points, with nonnegative weights encoded by the homogenization cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The convex hull of finitely many convex alternatives is the projection of a homogenized system combining scaled alternative-specific points with weights summing to one.
assumptions_latex: \(m\in\mathbb{N}\) is finite.
\(C_i\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty and convex for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_i C_i)\) equals the displayed projection.

notation.meaning: Weight and scaled point for alternative i.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation and content kind fit the node, but the cited general convex-hull section does not specifically establish the homogenized-cone formulation. A disjunctive-programming or perspective-formulation locator is required.

children.title: Activation-Logic Representation Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Alternative representations of logical activation and disjunctive structure.

children.title: Big-M Formulations
children.top_down_role: Compact activation formulations whose validity and strength depend on finite bounds.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bound-generation procedure for a fixed reference domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each activated row, solve \[v=\sup\{a^{\mathsf T}x-b:x\in X\}\] and set \(M^*=\max\{0,v\}\). Thus a system of activated affine inequalities is tightened by one support-optimization problem per row over the applicable inactive reference domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compute each tight big-M value by maximizing that row's inactive violation over its reference domain.
assumptions_latex: The row support problem has finite value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M^*=\max\{0,\sup_{x\in X}(a^{\mathsf T}x-b)\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Row-Wise Tight Big-M Computation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polyhedral Dual Certificate for a Big-M Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Verifiable multiplier certificate for a polyhedral reference domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\{x:Cx\le d\}\) be nonempty. Any \(\lambda\ge0\) satisfying \(C^{\mathsf T}\lambda=a\) certifies \[a^{\mathsf T}x-b\le d^{\mathsf T}\lambda-b\quad\text{for every }x\in X.\] Hence \(M=\max\{0,d^{\mathsf T}\lambda-b\}\) is valid. If the support problem is finite, linear-programming duality gives \[\sup_{x\in X}(a^{\mathsf T}x-b)=\min_{\lambda\ge0}\{d^{\mathsf T}\lambda-b:C^{\mathsf T}\lambda=a\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative multiplier representing the activated row certifies a valid big-M bound; an optimal multiplier yields the tight polyhedral value.
assumptions_latex: \(X=\{x:Cx\le d\}\) is nonempty.
For equality with the dual minimum, the support value is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C^{\mathsf T}\lambda=a,\ \lambda\ge0\implies \max\{0,d^{\mathsf T}\lambda-b\}\text{ is valid}.
knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Dual Certificate for a Big-M Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity boundary for the standard one-row template.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A finite \(M\) in \[a^{\mathsf T}x\le b+M(1-z)\] represents \(z=1\Rightarrow a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\) on \(X\times\{0,1\}\) if and only if \(\sup_{x\in X}(a^{\mathsf T}x-b)<+\infty\). If this supremum is infinite, every finite \(M\) excludes an inactive point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The standard big-M row has a finite valid constant exactly when inactive violation is uniformly bounded.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists M<\infty\text{ valid}\iff \sup_{x\in X}(a^{\mathsf T}x-b)<+\infty.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Bound Requirement

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Big-M Encoding of a Binary-Activated Inequality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-row linear big-M encoding over a reference domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty and consider \(z=1\Rightarrow a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\). If \[M\ge\max\{0,\sup_{x\in X}(a^{\mathsf T}x-b)\}<+\infty,\] then \[a^{\mathsf T}x\le b+M(1-z)\] represents the implication exactly on \(X\times\{0,1\}\). The smallest valid nonnegative constant is \[M^*=\max\{0,\sup_{x\in X}(a^{\mathsf T}x-b)\}.\] Larger valid constants preserve the binary feasible set but can weaken the relaxation with \(z\in[0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite bound on inactive violation gives an exact binary implication, and the smallest nonnegative bound is strongest within this row template.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty.
\(\sup_{x\in X}(a^{\mathsf T}x-b)<+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: a^{\mathsf T}x\le b+M(1-z)\text{ exactly represents the implication on }X\times\{0,1\}.

notation.meaning: nonnegative bound on inactive constraint violation

knowledge_statements.title: Big-M Encoding of a Binary-Activated Inequality
Big-M Formulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear big-M encoding of one binary-activated inequality over a bounded reference domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, let \(a\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}\), and \(z\in\{0,1\}\). Consider the implication \(z=1\Rightarrow a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\). If \(M\ge0\) and
\[
M\ge \sup_{x\in X}\bigl(a^{\mathsf T}x-b\bigr)<+\infty,
\]
then
\[
a^{\mathsf T}x\le b+M(1-z)
\]
represents that implication exactly on \(X\times\{0,1\}\). Among nonnegative constants, the smallest valid value is
\[
M^*=\max\left\{0,\sup_{x\in X}\bigl(a^{\mathsf T}x-b\bigr)\right\}.
\]
Larger valid constants preserve the binary feasible set but can weaken the relaxation obtained by replacing \(z\in\{0,1\}\) with \(z\in[0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite upper bound on inactive constraint violation gives an exact binary implication. Under the standard nonnegative-M convention, the smallest such bound is strongest within this template.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty.
\(a\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(b\in\mathbb{R}\).
\(\sup_{x\in X}(a^{\mathsf T}x-b)<+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le b+M(1-z)\) represents \(z=1\Rightarrow a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\) on \(X\times\{0,1\}\).

notation.meaning: Nonnegative bound on inactive constraint violation.

children.title: Indicator-Constraint Formulations
children.top_down_role: Native implication representations and their reformulation interfaces.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: An Indicator Is Not a Biconditional
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary preventing reversal of the implication.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The implication \(z=1\Rightarrow g(x)\le0\) is satisfied whenever \(z=0\), independently of \(g(x)\). It is not equivalent to \(z=1\Longleftrightarrow g(x)\le0\), and it does not imply \(z=0\Rightarrow g(x)>0\). Either converse must be modeled separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inactivity removes the predicate; it does not force the predicate to be violated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (z=1\Rightarrow g(x)\le0)\not\Rightarrow(z=0\Rightarrow g(x)>0).
knowledge_statements.title: An Indicator Is Not a Biconditional

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Indicator Semantics Do Not Determine a Continuous Relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes binary semantics from solver-specific reformulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The binary set \[S=\{(x,z)\in X\times\{0,1\}:z=0\text{ or }g(x)\le0\}\] does not uniquely specify constraints for \(0<z<1\). Different valid big-M, perspective, branching, or disaggregated implementations can induce different continuous relaxations. Relaxation strength is therefore a property of the chosen reformulation, not of the logical implication alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A native indicator fixes binary semantics but has no unique fractional relaxation; strength depends on its implementation.
assumptions_latex: \(z\) is binary in the indicator semantics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Indicator semantics alone do not specify a unique relaxation for }z\in[0,1].
knowledge_statements.title: Indicator Semantics Do Not Determine a Continuous Relaxation
Indicator-Constraint Formulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Native logical constraint activated by a specified binary value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), a binary variable \(z\), and a predicate \(g(x)\le0\), the indicator constraint
\[
z=1\ \Longrightarrow\ g(x)\le0
\]
defines
\[
S=\{(x,z)\in X\times\{0,1\}:z=0\ \text{or}\ g(x)\le0\}.
\]
It imposes no additional restriction from \(g\) when \(z=0\). A solver reformulation must preserve this set, possibly using finite bounds, branching, or a disjunctive extended formulation; the logical statement itself requires no chosen big-M constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An indicator constraint activates a predicate at one binary value and leaves that predicate inactive at the other value.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\).
\(g:X\to\mathbb{R}\) is well defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The feasible set is \(S=\{(x,z)\in X\times\{0,1\}:z=0\text{ or }g(x)\le0\}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically precise, agrees with the plain statement, and fits the indicator-constraint container, but no source supports either the native implication semantics or the reformulation-interface claims.

children.title: Disaggregated Hull Formulations
children.top_down_role: Extended formulations based on alternative-specific variable copies and convex combination structure.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Size of the Standard Disaggregated Lift
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formulation-size cost of alternative-specific copies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(m\) alternatives in \(\mathbb R^n\), the standard construction introduces \(m\) vectors \(y_i\in\mathbb R^n\), \(m\) scalar weights, the linking equation \(x=\sum_i y_i\), the simplex equation \(\sum_i\lambda_i=1\), and one scaled constraint block per alternative. Its explicit size is therefore linear in the total sizes of the alternative descriptions and in \(mn\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The hull lift uses one variable copy, one weight, and one scaled constraint block per alternative.
assumptions_latex: The alternatives have finite explicit inequality descriptions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The explicit lift size is }O(mn+\sum_i\operatorname{size}(A_i,b_i)).
knowledge_statements.title: Size of the Standard Disaggregated Lift

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Continuous Weights Recover the Hull, Not Generally the Union
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between one-hot selection and convexification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under \(\lambda\ge0\) and \(\sum_i\lambda_i=1\), fractional weights combine several alternatives and can project outside \(\bigcup_iP_i\). Recovery of the original union requires one-hot weights, for example \(\lambda\in\{0,1\}^m\). Continuous weights project to the union itself only when the union already equals its convex hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fractional alternative weights describe the hull rather than the original disjunction; one-hot weights select a single alternative.
assumptions_latex: The disaggregated formulation uses simplex weights.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lambda\in\{0,1\}^m,\ \mathbf1^{\mathsf T}\lambda=1\text{ selects one alternative; continuous }\lambda\text{ generally does not}.
knowledge_statements.title: Continuous Weights Recover the Hull, Not Generally the Union

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Disaggregated Hull Formulation for Bounded Polyhedra
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact extended hull representation for a finite union of nonempty bounded polyhedra.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_i=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:A_i x\le b_i\}\) be nonempty bounded polyhedra for \(i=1,\ldots,m\). Then \(\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_iP_i)\) is the projection onto \(x\) of \[x=\sum_{i=1}^m y_i,\qquad \sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i=1,\qquad A_i y_i\le b_i\lambda_i,\qquad \lambda_i\ge0.\] Requiring \(\lambda_i\in\{0,1\}\) selects one alternative and projects to \(\bigcup_iP_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternative-specific variable copies and convex weights give an extended formulation whose continuous projection is exactly the hull of bounded polyhedral alternatives.
assumptions_latex: There are finitely many alternatives.
Each \(P_i=\{x:A_i x\le b_i\}\) is nonempty and bounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{proj}_x(Q)=\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_iP_i).

notation.meaning: scaled copy of the original variable for alternative i

knowledge_statements.title: Disaggregated Hull Formulation for Bounded Polyhedra
Disaggregated Hull Formulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact extended hull formulation for a finite union of bounded polyhedra.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P_i=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:A_i x\le b_i\}\) be nonempty bounded polyhedra. Then \(\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_{i=1}^mP_i)\) is the projection onto \(x\) of
\[
x=\sum_{i=1}^m y_i,\qquad \sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i=1,\qquad A_i y_i\le b_i\lambda_i,\qquad \lambda_i\ge0.
\]
Requiring \(\lambda_i\in\{0,1\}\) selects one alternative and recovers the original union; allowing \(\lambda_i\ge0\) gives its convex hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternative-specific variable copies and convex weights form an extended formulation whose continuous projection is exactly the hull of bounded polyhedral alternatives.
assumptions_latex: \(m\in\mathbb{N}\) is finite.
Each \(P_i=\{x:A_i x\le b_i\}\) is nonempty and bounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed continuous formulation projects to \(\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_iP_i)\).

notation.meaning: Scaled copy of the original variable for alternative i.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bounded-polyhedral disaggregated formulation and representation content kind fit the node. A specific source is required for exact projection to the hull and recovery of the union under binary weights.

children.title: Product-Lift Spaces
children.top_down_role: Auxiliary spaces formed from lifted variable products.

knowledge_statements.title: Product-Lift Spaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cartesian lift carrying separate coordinate blocks for multiple factors or alternatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given finite-dimensional real vector spaces \(E_1,\ldots,E_m\), their product-lift space is
\[
\mathcal{E}=E_1\times\cdots\times E_m.
\]
A lifted point is \(y=(y_1,\ldots,y_m)\), where \(y_i\in E_i\). Given linear maps \(T_i:E_i\to\mathbb{R}^n\), define the aggregation map \(\pi:\mathcal{E}\to\mathbb{R}^n\) by
\[
\pi(y)=\sum_{i=1}^m T_i y_i.
\]
A product-lift formulation places factor-specific constraints on the blocks and recovers the original-space variable through \(x=\pi(y)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A product lift stores factor-specific variables in a Cartesian product and maps their aggregate back to the original variable space.
assumptions_latex: \(m\in\mathbb{N}\) is finite.
Each \(E_i\) is a finite-dimensional real vector space.
Each \(T_i:E_i\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is linear.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal{E}=\prod_{i=1}^mE_i\) is the lifted space, and \(x=\sum_{i=1}^mT_i y_i\) is its aggregation interface.

notation.meaning: Linear aggregation map to the original space.

source_refs.locator: 1.9 Cartesian Product of Vector Spaces p. 7

source_witnesses.locator: 1.9 Cartesian Product of Vector Spaces p. 7

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometry induced by independent feasible blocks and linear aggregation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_i\subseteq E_i\) be nonempty sets and let \(T_i:E_i\to\mathbb R^n\) be linear. For \(C=\prod_{i=1}^mC_i\) and \(\pi(y)=\sum_iT_iy_i\), \[\pi(C)=\sum_{i=1}^mT_iC_i,\qquad \sigma_{\pi(C)}(u)=\sum_{i=1}^m\sigma_{C_i}(T_i^*u),\] with equality in the extended-real sense. Thus linear optimization over independent blocks separates additively.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A product lift projects to the Minkowski sum of its block images, and its support function separates across blocks.
assumptions_latex: Each \(C_i\subseteq E_i\) is nonempty.
Each \(T_i:E_i\to\mathbb R^n\) is linear.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\pi(\prod_iC_i)=\sum_iT_iC_i\) and \(\sigma_{\pi(C)}(u)=\sum_i\sigma_{C_i}(T_i^*u)\).

notation.meaning: Adjoint of the block aggregation map.

children.title: Disjunctive-Lift Spaces
children.top_down_role: Auxiliary spaces formed from disjunct-specific variables or components.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact extended representation of a finite compact-convex disjunction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_1,\ldots,P_m\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty compact convex sets. Then \[\operatorname{conv}\Bigl(\bigcup_{i=1}^mP_i\Bigr)=\left\{x:\ x=\sum_{i=1}^m y_i,\ \lambda\ge0,\ \sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i=1,\ y_i\in\lambda_iP_i\ (i=1,\ldots,m)\right\}.\] At an integral label \(\lambda=e_i\), the formulation selects \(P_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Disaggregated copies and simplex weights exactly represent the convex hull of a finite union of compact convex sets.
assumptions_latex: \(m\in\mathbb N\) is finite.
Each \(P_i\) is nonempty, compact, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The projection onto \(x\) equals \(\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_iP_i)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Disaggregated Convex-Hull Lift
Disjunctive-Lift Spaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Alternative-labeled embedding of a finite disjunction into an extended space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P_1,\ldots,P_m\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) and let \(e_i\) denote the \(i\)-th unit vector of \(\mathbb{R}^m\). The disjunctive-lift set is
\[
D=\bigcup_{i=1}^m\bigl(P_i\times\{e_i\}\bigr)\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^m.
\]
The label coordinate records the selected alternative. Its original-space projection satisfies \(\operatorname{proj}_x(D)=\bigcup_iP_i\), while convexification commutes with this linear projection:
\[
\operatorname{proj}_x(\operatorname{conv}D)=\operatorname{conv}\!\left(\bigcup_iP_i\right).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A disjunctive lift attaches a unit-vector label to each alternative; projecting its convex hull yields the convex hull of the original union.
assumptions_latex: \(m\in\mathbb{N}\) is finite.
\(P_i\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_x(D)=\bigcup_iP_i\) and \(\operatorname{proj}_x(\operatorname{conv}D)=\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_iP_i)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The labeled lift and its projection identities are correct and fit a definition of disjunctive-lift spaces, but no inspectable source locator is supplied.

children.title: Activation-Variable Coupling
children.top_down_role: Structural links between lifted quantities and activation variables.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of zero-forcing at the closed-hull boundary for an unbounded active set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonempty closed convex set \(C\), \[\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}\bigl(\{(0,0)\}\cup(C\times\{1\})\bigr)=\{(y,z):0<z\le1,\ y\in zC\}\cup\bigl(\operatorname{rec}(C)\times\{0\}\bigr).\] Thus zero activation need not force \(y=0\). For \(C=[1,\infty)\), the closed hull contains every \((y,0)\) with \(y\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Closing an on-off hull for an unbounded active set introduces its recession directions at zero activation.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rec}(C)\times\{0\}\subseteq\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(\{(0,0)\}\cup(C\times\{1\}))\).

notation.meaning: Recession cone of the active set.

knowledge_statements.title: Recession Boundary at Zero Activation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact activation coupling for a compact convex active set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, compact, and convex. Then \[\operatorname{conv}\bigl(\{(0,0)\}\cup(C\times\{1\})\bigr)=\{(y,z):0\le z\le1,\ y\in zC\},\] where \(0C=\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scaling a compact convex active set by a relaxed activation variable gives the exact convex hull of its inactive and active states.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, compact, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{conv}(\{(0,0)\}\cup(C\times\{1\}))=\{(y,z):0\le z\le1,\ y\in zC\}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Compact Convex On-Off Hull
Activation-Variable Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bound-based constraints coupling an alternative-specific variable block to its activation weight.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(z_i\in[0,1]\), let \(y_i\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and let finite vectors \(\ell_i,u_i\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfy \(\ell_i\le u_i\) componentwise. The activation coupling
\[
\ell_i z_i\le y_i\le u_i z_i
\]
is interpreted componentwise. It forces \(y_i=0\) when \(z_i=0\), and it permits exactly \(y_i\in[\ell_i,u_i]\) when \(z_i=1\). Thus, for binary \(z_i\), it exactly describes the bounded on-off block; for fractional \(z_i\), it permits the scaled box \(y_i\in z_i[\ell_i,u_i]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiplying finite componentwise bounds by an activation weight forces an inactive copied block to zero and scales its permitted box under fractional activation.
assumptions_latex: \(y_i\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
\(\ell_i,u_i\in\mathbb{R}^n\) are finite and satisfy \(\ell_i\le u_i\) componentwise.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\ell_i z_i\le y_i\le u_i z_i\), and \(z_i=0\Rightarrow y_i=0\).

notation.meaning: Componentwise finite lower and upper bounds.

children.title: Projection-Based Strengthening
children.top_down_role: Recovery of strengthened original-space descriptions from lifted systems.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact elimination algorithm for finite polyhedral lifted systems and its output-size boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: To eliminate a scalar \(y\) from a finite linear-inequality system, retain inequalities having zero \(y\)-coefficient and combine every positive-coefficient inequality with every negative-coefficient inequality after nonnegative scaling that cancels \(y\). Repeating this operation yields an exact inequality description of the projection. If an elimination step has \(p\) positive and \(q\) negative inequalities, it may create \(pq\) pairwise inequalities before redundancy removal; repeated elimination can therefore have exponential intermediate and output size.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fourier–Motzkin elimination exactly projects a polyhedron but can suffer exponential inequality growth.
assumptions_latex: The lifted system contains finitely many linear inequalities.
Only finitely many real variables are eliminated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The resulting system describes the exact projection, and one elimination step may generate \(pq\) inequalities.

notation.meaning: Numbers of positive- and negative-coefficient inequalities for the eliminated variable.

knowledge_statements.title: Fourier–Motzkin Projection

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Farkas Characterization of a Polyhedral Projection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact original-space inequalities obtained by eliminating continuous lifted variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q=\{(x,y):Ax+By\le b\}\). Then \[\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)=\bigcap_{\lambda\ge0:\,B^T\lambda=0}\{x:\lambda^TAx\le\lambda^Tb\}.\] Consequently, if \(\bar x\notin\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)\), some \(\lambda\ge0\) with \(B^T\lambda=0\) satisfies \(\lambda^TA\bar x>\lambda^Tb\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative Farkas multipliers that cancel all eliminated-variable coefficients exactly characterize a polyhedral projection.
assumptions_latex: \(A,B,b\) are finite-dimensional real matrices and vectors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)\iff \lambda^TAx\le\lambda^Tb\) for every \(\lambda\ge0\) satisfying \(B^T\lambda=0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Farkas Characterization of a Polyhedral Projection
Projection-Based Strengthening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Original-space strengthening obtained by projecting a tighter valid lifted relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), and let \(Q_0,Q_1\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n+p}\) be lifted relaxations. Assume
\[
S\subseteq\operatorname{proj}_x(Q_1)
\quad\text{and}\quad
Q_1\subseteq Q_0.
\]
Then
\[
S\subseteq\operatorname{proj}_x(Q_1)\subseteq\operatorname{proj}_x(Q_0).
\]
Hence projecting the tighter lifted relaxation cannot enlarge the original-space relaxation. Strict strengthening occurs when \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q_1)\subsetneq\operatorname{proj}_x(Q_0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tightening a valid lifted relaxation and projecting it cannot enlarge the original-space relaxation; strict projected containment yields genuine strengthening.
assumptions_latex: \(S\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\).
\(Q_0,Q_1\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n+p}\).
\(S\subseteq\operatorname{proj}_x(Q_1)\).
\(Q_1\subseteq Q_0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S\subseteq\operatorname{proj}_x(Q_1)\subseteq\operatorname{proj}_x(Q_0)\).

children.title: Lift-Project Closure Family
children.top_down_role: Closure families induced by complete lift-and-project separation systems.

children.title: Product-Lift Closures
children.top_down_role: Closures induced through product-variable lifting systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Product-Lift Closures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closure obtained by imposing a specified valid-cut family in a product lift and projecting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S\subseteq R\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\). Let \(F_{\mathrm{prod}}\subseteq Q_{\mathrm{prod}}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n+p}\) satisfy
\[
\operatorname{proj}_x(F_{\mathrm{prod}})=S
\quad\text{and}\quad
\operatorname{proj}_x(Q_{\mathrm{prod}})\subseteq R.
\]
Let \(\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{prod}}\) be a specified family of closed halfspaces such that \(F_{\mathrm{prod}}\subseteq H\) for every \(H\in\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{prod}}\). Define
\[
\operatorname{cl}_{\mathrm{prod}}(R)=
\operatorname{proj}_x\!\left(Q_{\mathrm{prod}}\cap
\bigcap_{H\in\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{prod}}}H\right).
\]
Then
\[
S\subseteq\operatorname{cl}_{\mathrm{prod}}(R)
\subseteq\operatorname{proj}_x(Q_{\mathrm{prod}})\subseteq R.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relative to a specified product lift and valid-cut family, the product-lift closure imposes those lifted halfspaces and projects the intersection back to the original variables.
assumptions_latex: \(S\subseteq R\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\).
\(F_{\mathrm{prod}}\subseteq Q_{\mathrm{prod}}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n+p}\).
\(\operatorname{proj}_x(F_{\mathrm{prod}})=S\) and \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q_{\mathrm{prod}})\subseteq R\).
Every \(H\in\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{prod}}\) contains \(F_{\mathrm{prod}}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S\subseteq\operatorname{cl}_{\mathrm{prod}}(R)\subseteq\operatorname{proj}_x(Q_{\mathrm{prod}})\subseteq R\).

notation.meaning: Lifted feasible set whose original-space projection is S.
Specified family of halfspaces valid for the lifted feasible set.

children.title: Disjunctive-Lift Closures
children.top_down_role: Closures induced through disjunctive lifting systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Disjunctive-Lift Closures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closure obtained by cutting an alternative-labeled lift and projecting to original space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S\subseteq R\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\). Let \(F_{\mathrm{disj}}\subseteq Q_{\mathrm{disj}}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n+p}\) satisfy
\[
\operatorname{proj}_x(F_{\mathrm{disj}})=S
\quad\text{and}\quad
\operatorname{proj}_x(Q_{\mathrm{disj}})\subseteq R.
\]
Let \(\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{disj}}\) be a specified family of closed halfspaces such that \(F_{\mathrm{disj}}\subseteq H\) for every \(H\in\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{disj}}\). Define
\[
\operatorname{cl}_{\mathrm{disj}}(R)=
\operatorname{proj}_x\!\left(Q_{\mathrm{disj}}\cap
\bigcap_{H\in\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{disj}}}H\right).
\]
Then
\[
S\subseteq\operatorname{cl}_{\mathrm{disj}}(R)
\subseteq\operatorname{proj}_x(Q_{\mathrm{disj}})\subseteq R.
\]
The resulting closure depends on the chosen disjunctive lift and halfspace family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relative to a specified labeled disjunctive lift and valid-cut family, the closure intersects the lift with those cuts and projects the result to the original variables.
assumptions_latex: \(S\subseteq R\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\).
\(F_{\mathrm{disj}}\subseteq Q_{\mathrm{disj}}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n+p}\).
\(\operatorname{proj}_x(F_{\mathrm{disj}})=S\) and \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q_{\mathrm{disj}})\subseteq R\).
Every \(H\in\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{disj}}\) contains \(F_{\mathrm{disj}}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S\subseteq\operatorname{cl}_{\mathrm{disj}}(R)\subseteq\operatorname{proj}_x(Q_{\mathrm{disj}})\subseteq R\).

notation.meaning: Lifted disjunctive feasible set whose original-space projection is S.
Specified family of halfspaces valid for the lifted disjunctive feasible set.

children.title: Closure Strength Ordering
children.top_down_role: Relative strength of closure families after projection.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonnested Lifted Cut Families Can Produce Incomparable Closures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp boundary of set-inclusion strength ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q=[0,1]^2\), let projection be the identity, and let the intended lifted set be \(F=\{(0,0)\}\). The valid halfspaces \(H_x=\{(x,y):x\le1/2\}\) and \(H_y=\{(x,y):y\le1/2\}\) define \[C_x=Q\cap H_x=[0,1/2]\times[0,1],\qquad C_y=Q\cap H_y=[0,1]\times[0,1/2].\] Neither \(C_x\subseteq C_y\) nor \(C_y\subseteq C_x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two valid but nonnested lifted cut families may yield incomparable projected closures.
assumptions_latex: \(Q,F,H_x,H_y\) are the displayed sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_x\) and \(C_y\) are incomparable by inclusion.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonnested Lifted Cut Families Can Produce Incomparable Closures
Closure Strength Ordering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-inclusion ordering of closures induced by nested lifted feasible regions or cut families.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a fixed lifted relaxation \(Q\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n+p}\), define
\[
C_k=\operatorname{proj}_x\!\left(Q\cap
\bigcap_{H\in\mathcal{H}_k}H\right),
\qquad k\in\{1,2\}.
\]
If every halfspace in \(\mathcal{H}_2\) is valid for the lifted feasible set and \(\mathcal{H}_1\subseteq\mathcal{H}_2\), then
\[
C_2\subseteq C_1.
\]
Thus the closure using the larger valid-cut family is at least as strong. More generally, inclusion of cut lifted regions before projection implies the same inclusion after projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding valid lifted cuts can only shrink the projected closure, so the larger cut family produces an equally strong or stronger relaxation.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n+p}\).
\(\mathcal{H}_1\subseteq\mathcal{H}_2\).
Every halfspace in \(\mathcal{H}_2\) is valid for the lifted feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_2\subseteq C_1\).

notation.meaning: Valid lifted halfspace family defining closure k.
Projected closure generated by the corresponding family.

children.title: Reformulation–Linearization Technique
children.top_down_role: Product-based lifting and linearization for bounded discrete, continuous, and mixed nonlinear models.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Sherali and Adams, A Reformulation-Linearization Technique for Solving Discrete and Continuous Nonconvex Problems
top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Discrete, continuous, and mixed reformulation-linearization systems

children.title: Binary Reformulation–Linearization
children.top_down_role: RLT families exploiting binary identities and bounded products.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Binary-Product Ideality Does Not Imply Global Ideality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of assembling exact binary-product hulls in a coupled model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Replacing every equation \(z_{ij}=x_ix_j\) by its exact individual product hull preserves validity, but intersection with shared constraints need not equal the convex hull of the full binary model. In general, \[\operatorname{conv}\!\left(\bigcap_kG_k\right)\subsetneq\bigcap_k\operatorname{conv}(G_k)\] can occur, so additional RLT products or globally valid inequalities may be necessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact individual binary-product linearizations can still yield a nonideal relaxation when products interact through shared constraints.
assumptions_latex: The model contains interacting product blocks or additional coupling constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{conv}(\bigcap_kG_k)\subsetneq\bigcap_k\operatorname{conv}(G_k)\text{ can occur}.
knowledge_statements.title: Local Binary-Product Ideality Does Not Imply Global Ideality

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex hull of one product of two binary variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x_i,x_j\in\{0,1\}\) and \(z=x_ix_j\), \[\operatorname{conv}\{(x_i,x_j,z):z=x_ix_j\}=\{(x_i,x_j,z)\in[0,1]^3:z\le x_i,\ z\le x_j,\ z\ge x_i+x_j-1\}.\] Thus these inequalities and bounds form an ideal linearization of one binary product.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A product of two binary variables has an exact three-inequality convex-hull linearization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: z\le x_i,\quad z\le x_j,\quad z\ge x_i+x_j-1\text{ describe the binary-product hull with }(x_i,x_j,z)\in[0,1]^3.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Binary-Product Linearization
Binary Reformulation–Linearization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-round RLT construction for a linear system with binary variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input \(Ax\le b\), where \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\). For each \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), define the nonnegative slack
\[
g_i(x)=b_i-a_i^{\mathsf T}x.
\]
For every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\) and \(j\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\), generate
\[
x_jg_i(x)\ge0,
\qquad
(1-x_j)g_i(x)\ge0.
\]
Introduce variables \(X_{jk}\) for the products \(x_jx_k\), replace each quadratic product by \(X_{jk}\), and impose
\[
X_{jj}=x_j,
\qquad
X_{jk}=X_{kj}
\]
for all applicable indices. After processing all row-index pairs, output the resulting linear system in \((x,X)\), or its projection onto \(x\). Every feasible binary point has the lift \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\), so the output is a valid relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One-round binary RLT multiplies every linear slack by each binary variable and its complement, linearizes the resulting products, and returns a valid lifted linear relaxation.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\).
\(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\) and \(j,k\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every feasible binary \(x\) admits the lift \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\) satisfying the generated linear system.

notation.meaning: Lifted variable replacing the product of binary coordinates j and k.

children.title: Continuous Reformulation–Linearization
children.top_down_role: RLT families for bounded continuous polynomial and multilinear structure.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Termwise McCormick Exactness Does Not Imply Joint Exactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary for continuous models with interacting products.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For several bilinear or multilinear terms sharing variables, intersecting the exact McCormick hull of each individual bilinear graph with the remaining constraints need not equal the convex hull of the joint nonlinear graph. Products of constraints, domain partitioning, or higher-order lifted consistency inequalities can strengthen the termwise relaxation strictly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: McCormick is exact for one bilinear graph over a rectangle, but independently enveloping interacting products need not convexify their joint graph.
assumptions_latex: The model contains interacting products or shared coupling constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{conv}(\bigcap_kG_k)\subsetneq\bigcap_k\operatorname{conv}(G_k)\text{ can occur}.

notation.meaning: graph constraint for one nonlinear product

knowledge_statements.title: Termwise McCormick Exactness Does Not Imply Joint Exactness

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependence of continuous RLT strength on the variable box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B'\subseteq B\) be finite rectangles for \((x_i,x_j)\), and let \(M(B)\) and \(M(B')\) be their McCormick lifted polyhedra. Then \[M(B')\subseteq M(B)\cap(B'\times\mathbb R).\] Therefore replacing bounds by tighter valid bounds cannot weaken the bilinear relaxation and may strengthen it strictly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tighter valid variable bounds produce McCormick envelopes at least as strong as those derived from a larger box.
assumptions_latex: \(B'\subseteq B\) are finite rectangles.
Both rectangles contain the relevant feasible projection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M(B')\subseteq M(B)\cap(B'\times\mathbb R).

notation.meaning: McCormick polyhedron generated from box B

knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Tightening Monotonicity of Bilinear Envelopes
Continuous Reformulation–Linearization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Level-one RLT for bounded continuous bilinear terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For bounded variables \(l_i\le x_i\le u_i\) and \(l_j\le x_j\le u_j\), introduce \(X_{ij}\) to represent \(x_i x_j\). Linearizing the four nonnegative products of bound factors yields \[X_{ij}\ge l_i x_j+l_j x_i-l_i l_j,\qquad X_{ij}\ge u_i x_j+u_j x_i-u_i u_j,\] \[X_{ij}\le u_i x_j+l_j x_i-u_i l_j,\qquad X_{ij}\le l_i x_j+u_j x_i-l_i u_j.\] These inequalities define the convex hull of the graph \(X_{ij}=x_i x_j\) over the rectangle. Continuous RLT applies the same multiply-and-linearize operation to bounded polynomial constraints, retaining the resulting linear inequalities in lifted monomial variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Continuous RLT replaces bounded products by lifted variables and linearizes products of bound factors. For one bilinear term, the four resulting inequalities give its exact convex hull.
assumptions_latex: \(l_i<u_i\) and \(l_j<u_j\).
All multiplied polynomial expressions have finite bounds on the prescribed box.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{conv}\{(x_i,x_j,X_{ij}):X_{ij}=x_i x_j\}\) is described by the variable bounds and the four displayed inequalities.

notation.meaning: lifted variable representing the product of two continuous variables

children.title: Mixed Binary–Continuous Reformulation–Linearization
children.top_down_role: RLT families coupling discrete and continuous product structure.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-Bound Requirement for Mixed Product Hulls
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Applicability boundary of the standard binary–continuous RLT block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The standard four-inequality convex-hull formulation for \(y=bx\) requires finite valid bounds \(l\le x\le u\). If either bound is infinite, the corresponding finite-coefficient inequalities are unavailable; alternative valid bounds or another disjunctive or conic representation is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The exact standard binary–continuous product linearization depends essentially on finite valid bounds for the continuous factor.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: l,u\in\mathbb R\text{ are required for the standard four-inequality hull block}.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Bound Requirement for Mixed Product Hulls

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Componentwise Mixed Hulls Need Not Be Globally Ideal
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of assembling exact mixed-product blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Replacing every selected equation \(y_k=b_kx_k\) by its exact bounded mixed-product hull preserves validity, but intersection with coupling constraints need not equal the convex hull of the full mixed-integer nonlinear set. Additional constraint products, disjunctive inequalities, or shared-variable consistency constraints may be required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact hulls for individual binary–continuous products do not guarantee an ideal formulation of a coupled mixed model.
assumptions_latex: The model contains coupling constraints or interacting products.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{conv}(\bigcap_kG_k)\subsetneq\bigcap_k\operatorname{conv}(G_k)\text{ can occur}.

notation.meaning: graph set for one mixed product

knowledge_statements.title: Componentwise Mixed Hulls Need Not Be Globally Ideal

assumptions_latex: \(-\infty<l\le u<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed polyhedron is the exact convex hull of \(y=bx\) on \(b\in\{0,1\}\) and \(x\in[l,u]\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact mixed RLT block for one binary–continuous product.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(b\in\{0,1\}\), \(l\le x\le u\), and introduce \(y=bx\). The convex hull of this mixed product graph is \[\operatorname{conv}\{(b,x,y):b\in\{0,1\},\ l\le x\le u,\ y=bx\}\] \[=\{(b,x,y):0\le b\le1,\ l\le x\le u,\ lb\le y\le ub,\ x-u(1-b)\le y\le x-l(1-b)\}.\] Mixed binary–continuous RLT uses these inequalities for every selected binary–continuous product and linearizes higher products after multiplying valid constraints by \(b\) or \(1-b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A binary–continuous product has an exact four-inequality linear formulation after lifting. Mixed RLT combines these blocks with linearized products of constraints and binary factors.
knowledge_statements.title: Mixed Binary–Continuous Reformulation–Linearization

children.title: Polyhedral Lifting Hierarchies
children.top_down_role: Sherali–Adams and related bounded-discrete lifting interfaces.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent marginal-consistency interpretation of bounded-binary Sherali–Adams levels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under a fixed level convention, a level-\(r\) Sherali\text{--}Adams solution can be represented by distributions \(\mu_S\) on \(\{0,1\}^S\) for the required subsets \(S\), with consistent marginals on intersections. For every original slack \(g_i(x)=b_i-a_i^{\mathsf T}x\) and every partial-assignment indicator \(\chi\) allowed at level \(r\), the lifted moments satisfy \(\mathbb E_{\mu}[\chi g_i]\ge0\). Singleton marginals give \(x_i=\mu_{\{i\}}(1)\). Every distribution supported on the binary feasible set induces such marginals, but a feasible low-level family need not extend to a global supported distribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sherali–Adams is equivalently a system of consistent local distributions satisfying localized versions of the original inequalities; low-level consistency need not imply a global feasible distribution.
assumptions_latex: The subset sizes and multiplier degrees follow one fixed Sherali–Adams indexing convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{conv}(F)\subseteq P_r^{\mathrm{SA}},\quad\text{while local extendability can fail below an exact level}.

notation.meaning: local distribution on coordinates in S
indicator of a permitted partial binary assignment

knowledge_statements.title: Local-Distribution Form of Sherali–Adams
Polyhedral Lifting Hierarchies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sherali–Adams hierarchy for a bounded binary linear system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x\in[0,1]^n:Ax\le b\}\) and \(F=P\cap\{0,1\}^n\). At level \(r\), multiply every defining inequality of \(P\) by each factor \(\prod_{i\in S}x_i\prod_{j\in T}(1-x_j)\), where \(S\cap T=\varnothing\) and \(|S|+|T|\le r\); expand, replace \(x_i^2\) by \(x_i\), and assign a lifted variable to every remaining square-free monomial. Projection onto the original variables gives \(P_r^{\mathrm{SA}}\). The projections are nested, \(P_{r+1}^{\mathrm{SA}}\subseteq P_r^{\mathrm{SA}}\), contain \(\operatorname{conv}(F)\), and satisfy \(P_n^{\mathrm{SA}}=\operatorname{conv}(F)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sherali–Adams multiplies valid inequalities by bounded binary factors and linearizes square-free monomials. Its projections tighten monotonically and recover the binary hull by level n.
assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq[0,1]^n\) is described by finitely many linear inequalities.
The identities \(x_i^2=x_i\) are imposed during multilinearization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{conv}(F)\subseteq P_{r+1}^{\mathrm{SA}}\subseteq P_r^{\mathrm{SA}}\) and \(P_n^{\mathrm{SA}}=\operatorname{conv}(F)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record fits the polyhedral hierarchy container and correctly states nesting, containment, and finite exactness under a conventional Sherali–Adams level indexing. Because level conventions and the precise multiplier construction vary across sources, the absent citation makes the stated formulation and level-n claim insufficiently supported.

children.title: Semidefinite Lifting Hierarchies
children.top_down_role: Lovász–Schrijver, moment–sums-of-squares, and theta-body interfaces.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite exactness and optimizer extraction from a flat feasible moment solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y\) satisfy the moment and localizing constraints of an order-\(d\) relaxation, and let \(d_K\) cover the half-degrees of the support polynomials. Under the standard flat-extension hypotheses, if \(\operatorname{rank}M_d(y)=\operatorname{rank}M_{d-d_K}(y)\), then \(y\) has a finitely atomic representing measure supported on the feasible set, with at most \(\operatorname{rank}M_d(y)\) atoms. If \(y\) is relaxation-optimal, exactness follows and every positive-weight atom is a global optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A flat feasible moment matrix certifies a finitely atomic feasible measure and permits extraction of global optimizers from an optimal relaxation solution.
assumptions_latex: The applicable moment and localizing matrices are feasible.
The standard flat-extension and support hypotheses hold.
\(y\) is optimal for the extraction conclusion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: y\text{ has a feasible finitely atomic representing measure; optimal flat }y\text{ certifies exactness}.

notation.meaning: degree offset determined by the support polynomials

knowledge_statements.title: Flat Moment-Matrix Extraction Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Theta-body interface for real polynomial ideals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an ideal \(I\subseteq\mathbb R[x]\), a linear polynomial \(\ell\) is \(k\)-SOS modulo \(I\) if \(\ell-\sum_jq_j^2\in I\) for polynomials \(q_j\) of degree at most \(k\). Define \[\operatorname{TH}_k(I)=\{x:\ell(x)\ge0\text{ for every linear }\ell\text{ that is }k\text{-SOS modulo }I\}.\] Then \(\operatorname{TH}_k(I)\) is a convex semidefinite-representable outer approximation of \(\operatorname{conv}(V_{\mathbb R}(I))\), and \(\operatorname{TH}_{k+1}(I)\subseteq\operatorname{TH}_k(I)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A theta body imposes all linear inequalities having bounded-degree sums-of-squares proofs modulo an ideal.
assumptions_latex: \(I\subseteq\mathbb R[x]\) is an ideal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{conv}(V_{\mathbb R}(I))\subseteq\operatorname{TH}_{k+1}(I)\subseteq\operatorname{TH}_k(I).
knowledge_statements.title: Theta-Body Relaxations

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One round of the positive-semidefinite Lovász–Schrijver operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq[0,1]^n\) be convex and let \(C_K=\operatorname{cone}\{(1,x):x\in K\}\). The set \(N_+(K)\) consists of those \(x\) admitting \(Y\succeq0\) with \(Ye_0=\operatorname{diag}(Y)=(1,x)\) and \(Ye_i,Y(e_0-e_i)\in C_K\) for every \(i\). Then \[\operatorname{conv}(K\cap\{0,1\}^n)\subseteq N_+(K)\subseteq K,\] and iteration produces nested semidefinite strengthenings.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Lovász–Schrijver N-plus operator uses a positive-semidefinite consistency matrix whose binary-conditioned columns remain in the homogenized relaxation.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq[0,1]^n\) is convex.
Coordinate zero is the homogenizing coordinate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{conv}(K\cap\{0,1\}^n)\subseteq N_+(K)\subseteq K.
knowledge_statements.title: Lovász–Schrijver Positive-Semidefinite Lift
Semidefinite Lifting Hierarchies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Moment–sums-of-squares semidefinite hierarchy for polynomial optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_j(x)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\), the order-\(d\) moment relaxation replaces a probability measure on \(K\) by a truncated sequence \(y=(y_\alpha)_{|\alpha|\le2d}\) satisfying \(y_0=1\), \(M_d(y)\succeq0\), and \(M_{d-\lceil\deg(g_j)/2\rceil}(g_jy)\succeq0\) whenever the indicated order is nonnegative. Linear objectives are evaluated through their moments. The dual relaxation represents an objective gap by a degree-bounded sum of squares plus sum-of-squares multiples of the \(g_j\). Increasing \(d\) enlarges the moment and localizing matrices and tightens the projected relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Moment–SOS hierarchies encode truncated moments using positive-semidefinite moment and localizing matrices; their duals use bounded-degree sums-of-squares certificates.
assumptions_latex: \(g_1,\ldots,g_m\in\mathbb R[x]\).
The relaxation order is large enough to contain the objective and required localizing matrices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each order \(d\) produces a semidefinite relaxation, and increasing \(d\) yields a nested tightening of its projection.

notation.meaning: truncated moment indexed by a multi-index

children.title: Lifted-Dimension Growth
children.top_down_role: Expansion of auxiliary spaces across hierarchy levels.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Scalar Size of Dense Semidefinite Blocks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Translation from hierarchy block order to raw symmetric-matrix storage dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A symmetric positive-semidefinite matrix variable of order \(s\) has \(s(s+1)/2\) independent scalar entries. Consequently, a dense order-\(d\) moment matrix indexed by \(s=\binom{n+d}{d}\) monomials has \[\frac12\binom{n+d}{d}\left(\binom{n+d}{d}+1\right)\] symmetric entries before moment-identification equalities are imposed. Matrix order, raw symmetric entries, and distinct moment coordinates are therefore different size measures.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dense semidefinite block of order s has s(s+1)/2 symmetric entries, although moment identifications reduce the number of distinct lifted coordinates.
assumptions_latex: The semidefinite block is represented densely as a symmetric matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The raw number of independent symmetric matrix entries is \(s(s+1)/2\).
knowledge_statements.title: Scalar Size of Dense Semidefinite Blocks
Lifted-Dimension Growth
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combinatorial size growth of dense polyhedral and moment lifts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A dense square-free level-\(r\) lift in \(n\) binary variables has \(\sum_{k=0}^r\binom nk\) monomial coordinates, which is \(O(n^r)\) for fixed \(r\). A dense order-\(d\) moment lift in \(n\) real variables has \(\binom{n+2d}{2d}\) truncated-moment coordinates and a moment matrix indexed by \(\binom{n+d}{d}\) monomials. Thus fixed-order lifts are polynomial in \(n\), whereas orders proportional to \(n\) generally produce exponentially many coordinates or exponentially large semidefinite blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dense hierarchy size is polynomial in dimension at fixed order but becomes combinatorial as the order grows; moment lifts also create rapidly growing semidefinite blocks.
assumptions_latex: The lift retains every monomial permitted by its degree or square-free order.
No sparsity, symmetry, or quotient-basis reduction is applied.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The coordinate counts are \(\sum_{k=0}^r\binom nk\) and \(\binom{n+2d}{2d}\), with moment-matrix order \(\binom{n+d}{d}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The monomial counts are correct for the explicitly dense, unreduced constructions, and complexity_bound is the correct role for this terminal container. No source with a section, theorem, or page locator is supplied for the counts or scaling conclusion.

children.title: Finite-Exactness Regimes
children.top_down_role: Problem classes reaching the target hull at a finite level.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank certificate for finite atomic recovery at a moment-relaxation level.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y\) be feasible for an order-\(d\) moment relaxation over \(K\), and let \(d_K\) be the maximum degree offset required by its localizing constraints. Under the standard flat-extension hypotheses, if \[\operatorname{rank}M_d(y)=\operatorname{rank}M_{d-d_K}(y)=r,\] then \(y\) has a representing measure on \(K\) supported on \(r\) points. If \(y\) is relaxation-optimal, the support points are global minimizers and the relaxation is exact in value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A standard flat-rank condition certifies an atomic representing measure and enables recovery of global minimizers.
assumptions_latex: \(y\) satisfies the order-d moment and localizing constraints.
The standard flat-extension hypotheses and displayed rank condition hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An \(r\)-atomic representing measure on \(K\) exists; for an optimal \(y\), its atoms are global minimizers.

notation.meaning: Flat rank and number of recovered atoms.

knowledge_statements.title: Flat Moment-Matrix Extraction Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Truncated SOS Certificate of Value Exactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-order certificate for exact objective value in a polynomial optimization hierarchy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K=\{x:g_j(x)\ge0\}\), let \(M_d(g)\) be the degree-\(2d\) truncated quadratic module. If the attained true minimum is \(f^*\) and \[f-f^*\in M_d(g),\] then the order-\(d\) SOS lower bound equals \(f^*\). Conversely, if the order-\(d\) SOS dual is attained with no duality gap and its value is \(f^*\), such a degree-bounded representation exists. This is objective-value exactness, not equality of an entire projected relaxation with a convex hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A degree-bounded SOS representation of the optimality gap certifies finite value exactness for the selected objective.
assumptions_latex: \(f,g_j\in\mathbb R[x]\).
The true minimum \(f^*\) is attained.
The converse assumes attainment of the order-d SOS dual and zero duality gap.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f-f^*\in M_d(g)\Rightarrow p_d=f^*\).
knowledge_statements.title: Truncated SOS Certificate of Value Exactness
Finite-Exactness Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite convergence of bounded-discrete lifting hierarchies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F=\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:Ax\le b\}\), the Sherali–Adams hierarchy is finitely exact: its level-\(n\) projection equals \(\operatorname{conv}(F)\). More generally, a relaxation hierarchy \((R_r)_{r\ge0}\) is exact at finite level \(r_*\) when its projection onto the original variables satisfies \(\pi_x(R_{r_*})=\operatorname{conv}(F)\); nesting then gives \(\pi_x(R_r)=\operatorname{conv}(F)\) for every \(r\ge r_*\). Finite exactness concerns equality of feasible-set projections, not merely equality of one selected objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sherali–Adams reaches the binary convex hull by level n. In general, finite exactness means an entire projected relaxation equals the target convex hull at some finite level.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite binary feasible set.
The hierarchy is nested and every relaxation contains the lifted image of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\pi_x(R_{r_*})=\operatorname{conv}(F)\) implies \(\pi_x(R_r)=\operatorname{conv}(F)\) for all \(r\ge r_*\); for Sherali–Adams one may take \(r_*=n\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition of finite exactness and the Sherali–Adams level-n example match the container, and property is an appropriate content kind. The hierarchy-specific exactness assertion lacks an authoritative citation and depends on the adopted level convention.

children.title: Asymptotic-Convergence Regimes
children.top_down_role: Hierarchy behavior when strength improves only across increasing levels.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: General set-theoretic regime for asymptotic convergence of hierarchy values and minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_1\supseteq R_2\supseteq\cdots\) be nonempty compact subsets of a common finite-dimensional space, let \(F=\bigcap_{d\ge1}R_d\), and let \(f\) be continuous. Then \[p_d:=\min_{x\in R_d}f(x)\uparrow\min_{x\in F}f(x)=:p^*.\] Every cluster point of minimizers \(x_d\in\arg\min_{R_d}f\) is in \(\arg\min_Ff\). Nesting alone does not imply convergence to an intended target larger or smaller than \(\bigcap_dR_d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested compact relaxations converge in value and in optimizer cluster points when their intersection is exactly the target set.
assumptions_latex: Each \(R_d\) is nonempty and compact.
\(R_{d+1}\subseteq R_d\).
\(F=\bigcap_dR_d\).
\(f\) is continuous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_d\uparrow p^*\), and every cluster point of level minimizers is target-optimal.

notation.meaning: Target feasible set and exact limiting intersection.

knowledge_statements.title: Nested Compact Relaxation Convergence
Asymptotic-Convergence Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Archimedean convergence of the moment–SOS hierarchy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_j(x)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\), and minimize \(f\in\mathbb R[x]\) over \(K\). Suppose the quadratic module generated by \(g_1,\ldots,g_m\) is Archimedean: for some \(R>0\), the polynomial \(R-\|x\|_2^2\) belongs to that module. Then \(K\) is compact, the order-\(d\) moment–SOS optimal values \(p_d\) are nondecreasing lower bounds on the true optimum \(p^*\), and \(p_d\uparrow p^*\) as \(d\to\infty\). This conclusion does not assert finite convergence at any prescribed order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under an Archimedean compactness certificate, moment–SOS lower bounds increase monotonically to the polynomial optimization optimum, though finite convergence need not occur.
assumptions_latex: \(f,g_1,\ldots,g_m\in\mathbb R[x]\).
The feasible set is nonempty.
The quadratic module generated by the constraints is Archimedean.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_d\le p_{d+1}\le p^*\) for all admissible \(d\), and \(\lim_{d\to\infty}p_d=p^*\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Archimedean hypothesis and monotone convergence conclusion form an appropriate theorem for the asymptotic-convergence container. This nontrivial convergence theorem has no source reference or inspectable Putinar/Lasserre locator.

children.title: Structure-Aware Scaling
children.top_down_role: Dimension control through sparsity, symmetry, or decomposable structure.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pairwise Consistency Does Not Imply Global Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of local sparse gluing on a cyclic clique system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X_1,X_2,X_3\in\{0,1\}\). On each edge \(\{1,2\},\{2,3\},\{1,3\}\), assign probability \(1/2\) to \((0,1)\), probability \(1/2\) to \((1,0)\), and zero otherwise. The three pair distributions have identical uniform one-variable marginals on their overlaps, but no joint distribution exists because their support would require \(X_1
e X_2\), \(X_2
e X_3\), and \(X_1
e X_3\) simultaneously.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pairwise-consistent local marginals on a triangle need not extend globally, demonstrating the need for an acyclic gluing condition.
assumptions_latex: The clique system is the three-edge cycle.
Only equality of shared one-variable marginals is imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The locally consistent edge marginals admit no global joint distribution.
knowledge_statements.title: Pairwise Consistency Does Not Imply Global Consistency

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-point and orbit reduction of an invariant convex hierarchy level.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a finite group \(G\) act linearly on a convex relaxation \(R\), and suppose \(R\) and the linear objective \(c^Tx\) are \(G\)-invariant. For every \(x\in R\), its Reynolds average \[\bar x=\frac1{|G|}\sum_{g\in G}gx\] is feasible, fixed by \(G\), and has the same objective value. Hence \[\min_{x\in R}c^Tx=\min_{x\in R\cap\operatorname{Fix}(G)}c^Tx.\] Under a permutation action on monomial coordinates, invariant coordinates may be indexed by monomial orbits.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Averaging over a finite symmetry group preserves feasibility and objective value, allowing restriction to fixed-point or orbit variables.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is finite and acts linearly.
\(R\) is convex and \(G\)-invariant.
The linear objective is \(G\)-invariant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{x\in R}c^Tx=\min_{x\in R\cap\operatorname{Fix}(G)}c^Tx\).

notation.meaning: Subspace fixed by every element of G.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Group Symmetry Reduction
Structure-Aware Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sparse moment lifting over bounded-size variable cliques.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose polynomial objectives and constraints are assigned to \(q\) variable cliques \(C_1,\ldots,C_q\), each of cardinality at most \(w\). An order-\(d\) clique-sparse moment construction uses, per clique, at most \(\binom{w+2d}{2d}\) moment coordinates and a positive-semidefinite block of order at most \(\binom{w+d}{d}\). Hence its aggregate coordinate count is at most \(q\binom{w+2d}{2d}\), before identifying moments shared by overlapping cliques. For fixed \(w\) and \(d\), this size is linear in \(q\); convergence claims additionally require compatibility conditions such as running intersection and consistent overlap moments.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clique-sparse moment lifts replace one dimension-dependent block by local blocks governed by clique width. At fixed width and order, representation size grows linearly with the number of cliques.
assumptions_latex: Each polynomial is supported within at least one clique.
The maximal clique cardinality is \(w\).
Shared moments are constrained consistently on clique overlaps.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The lift uses at most \(q\binom{w+2d}{2d}\) local coordinates and positive-semidefinite blocks of order at most \(\binom{w+d}{d}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The local coordinate and PSD-block counts follow from dense degree indexing within each clique, and complexity_bound fits the structure-aware scaling leaf. An authoritative sparse moment hierarchy source is required, particularly for the stated overlap and running-intersection qualifications.

knowledge_statements.title: Norm-Cone Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Epigraph cone and dual cone of a finite-dimensional norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a norm \(\|\cdot\|\) on \(\mathbb R^n\), define its epigraph cone by \[K_{\|\cdot\|}=\{(x,t)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R:\|x\|\le t\}.\] This is a closed convex pointed cone with nonempty interior. Under the pairing \(\langle(y,s),(x,t)\rangle=y^\top x+st\), its dual cone is \[K_{\|\cdot\|}^*=\{(y,s):\|y\|_*\le s\},\] where \(\|\cdot\|_*\) is the dual norm. For the Euclidean norm, this cone is the Lorentz cone and is self-dual under the standard inner product.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every norm inequality is membership in its epigraph cone. The dual cone is the epigraph cone of the dual norm; the Euclidean case is the self-dual Lorentz cone.
assumptions_latex: \(\|\cdot\|\) is a norm on finite-dimensional \(\mathbb R^n\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The norm epigraph cone, dual-cone identity, and Euclidean self-duality statement are correct in finite dimensions, and representation fits the leaf. The record has no source. A supporting locator should also preserve the distinction between general norm cones and the narrower class admitting finite SOC representations.

children.title: Convex-Epigraph Cone Representations
children.top_down_role: SOC-compatible representations of convex epigraph structure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact lifted product-cone definition for an SOC-compatible convex epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A proper closed convex function \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) has an SOC-representable epigraph if there exist auxiliary variables \(y\), affine maps \(L_j\), and Lorentz or rotated-Lorentz cones \(\mathcal Q_j\) such that \[\operatorname{epi}f=\{(x,t):\exists y,\ L_j(x,t,y)\in\mathcal Q_j\ \text{for every }j\}.\] Exactness requires equality after projection, not merely containment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex epigraph is SOC representable when it is exactly the projection of finitely many affine Lorentz- or rotated-Lorentz-cone constraints.
assumptions_latex: Only finitely many finite-dimensional Lorentz or rotated-Lorentz cones are used
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The projected product-cone system is an exact SOC lift of \(\operatorname{epi}f\).
knowledge_statements.title: SOC-Representable Convex Epigraph
Convex-Epigraph Cone Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Homogenized cone representation of a closed convex epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper, closed, and convex. Its homogenized epigraph cone is \[K_f=\operatorname{cl}\{(x,t,s)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\times\mathbb R:s>0,\ t\ge s f(x/s)\}.\] The set \(K_f\) is a closed convex cone, and its affine slice at \(s=1\) recovers the epigraph exactly: \[\operatorname{epi}f=\{(x,t):(x,t,1)\in K_f\}.\] Consequently, any tractable conic representation of \(K_f\), including a second-order-cone lift when one exists, gives a conic representation of the original epigraph constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proper closed convex epigraph can be homogenized into a closed convex cone. Slicing that cone at the homogenizing coordinate one recovers the original epigraph.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, lower-semicontinuous, and convex.
The closure includes recession directions at homogenizing coordinate zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K_f\) is a closed convex cone and \(\operatorname{epi}f=\{(x,t):(x,t,1)\in K_f\}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The closure of the perspective epigraph gives the stated homogenized cone and its unit slice recovers the epigraph, so the mathematics and representation content kind fit the container. No authoritative source or specific locator is supplied.

children.title: SOC Representability Limits
