knowledge_statements.statement_title: Semialgebraicity Necessary for Finite SOC Lifts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General obstruction to exact finite second-order-cone representability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Every set representable as the projection of an affine slice of a finite product of Lorentz cones is semialgebraic. Consequently, a convex set or epigraph that is not semialgebraic has no exact finite SOC lift. In particular, for irrational \(p>1\), \[E_p=\{(x,t)\in\mathbb R^2:x\ge0,\ t\ge x^p\}\] is a closed convex nonsemialgebraic epigraph and therefore has no exact finite SOC lift.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite SOC lifts are necessarily semialgebraic, so nonsemialgebraic convex epigraphs such as an irrational-power epigraph cannot have exact finite SOC representations.
assumptions_latex: Only finitely many finite-dimensional Lorentz cones and auxiliary variables are allowed
\(p>1\) is irrational
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E_p\) has no exact finite SOC lift.

knowledge_statements.title: Semialgebraicity Necessary for Finite SOC Lifts
SOC Representability Limits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A basic semidefinite cone that admits no finite SOC lift.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Call a closed convex cone second-order-cone representable when it is the linear image of an affine slice of a finite Cartesian product of Lorentz cones. The positive-semidefinite cone \(\mathbb S_+^3\) is not second-order-cone representable in this sense: no finite number of auxiliary variables and Lorentz-cone constraints has projection exactly equal to \(\mathbb S_+^3\). Thus second-order-cone lifting does not subsume semidefinite lifting, even for matrices of fixed order three. This boundary concerns exact representation and does not preclude outer or inner SOC approximations of \(\mathbb S_+^3\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The cone of three-by-three positive-semidefinite matrices has no exact finite second-order-cone lift, although it can still be approximated by SOC formulations.
assumptions_latex: Only finite products of finite-dimensional Lorentz cones are permitted.
Representability requires exact equality after affine slicing and linear projection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb S_+^3\) has no finite second-order-cone lift.

notation.meaning: cone of three-by-three real symmetric positive-semidefinite matrices

children.title: Rotated-Cone Product Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Rotated-SOC representations for convex product and quadratic-over-linear structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Rotated-Cone Product Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rotated-SOC encoding of product and quadratic-over-linear inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the rotated second-order cone \[\mathcal Q_{r}^{n+2}=\{(u,v,w)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^n:2uv\ge\|w\|_2^2,\ u\ge0,\ v\ge0\}.\] For \(s,t\ge0\), the convex quadratic-over-linear inequality \(\|x\|_2^2\le st\) is equivalent to \((s,t,\sqrt2 x)\in\mathcal Q_r^{n+2}\). Likewise, for \(u,v\ge0\), the product hypograph inequality \(z^2\le uv\) is equivalent to \((u,v,\sqrt2 z)\in\mathcal Q_r^3\). Dropping an equality such as \(z^2=uv\) to this cone constraint therefore gives a convex product relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The rotated second-order cone exactly represents quadratic-over-linear inequalities and product hypographs. Replacing a nonconvex product equality by this membership condition gives a convex relaxation.
assumptions_latex: The two scalar factors in each product inequality are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|x\|_2^2\le st\iff(s,t,\sqrt2x)\in\mathcal Q_r^{n+2}\), and \(z^2\le uv\iff(u,v,\sqrt2z)\in\mathcal Q_r^3\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: With the stated normalization of the rotated cone, both equivalences and the relaxation interpretation are correct, and representation is the proper content kind. The record supplies no authoritative source with a specific locator for the cone normalization and equivalences.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed extended-value formulation duplicates the dedicated quadratic-over-linear epigraph leaf.

\(s,t\in\mathbb R\)

children.title: Structured Quadratic SOC Relaxations

knowledge_statements.title: Structured Quadratic SOC Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact SOC representation of convex quadratic inequalities used inside structured quadratic relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x,q\in\mathbb R^n\), \(r\in\mathbb R\), and \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\). Choose an integer \(p\ge1\) and \(A\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\) satisfying \(Q=A^{\mathsf T}A\), and define \(t=-2q^{\mathsf T}x-r\). Then \[x^{\mathsf T}Qx+2q^{\mathsf T}x+r\le0\] is equivalent to \[\bigl(t,\tfrac12,Ax\bigr)\in\mathcal Q_r^{p+2},\qquad \mathcal Q_r^{p+2}:=\{(u,v,w)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^p:2uv\ge\lVert w\rVert_2^2,\ u\ge0,\ v\ge0\}.\] Consequently, retained quadratic inequalities with positive-semidefinite quadratic parts have exact rotated-SOC representations; relaxing other nonconvex constraints produces an SOC relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every quadratic inequality with a positive-semidefinite quadratic part has an exact rotated second-order-cone representation. Retaining these representations while relaxing other nonconvex constraints yields a structured SOC relaxation.
assumptions_latex: \(x,q\in\mathbb R^n\), \(r\in\mathbb R\)
\(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\)
\(A\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\) and \(Q=A^{\mathsf T}A\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^{\mathsf T}Qx+2q^{\mathsf T}x+r\le0\iff(-2q^{\mathsf T}x-r,\tfrac12,Ax)\in\mathcal Q_r^{p+2}\).

notation.meaning: Cone of real symmetric positive-semidefinite matrices

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Positive-Semidefinite Cone Obstruction to SOC Lifts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite SOC lifts do not capture general positive-semidefinite matrix structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: There are no finite-dimensional affine subspace \(L\), finite Cartesian product \(K\) of Lorentz cones, and linear map \(\pi\) such that \[\mathbb S_+^3=\pi(K\cap L).\] Consequently, the class of general linear matrix inequalities of order at least three cannot be represented exactly using only finitely many SOC constraints and auxiliary variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The three-by-three positive-semidefinite cone has no finite SOC lift, so general matrix positivity genuinely exceeds SOC representability.
assumptions_latex: Extended formulations use finitely many finite-dimensional Lorentz cones and auxiliary variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb S_+^3\) has no finite second-order-cone lift.

notation.meaning: Cone of real three-by-three positive-semidefinite matrices
Linear projection from an extended formulation

knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Semidefinite Cone Obstruction to SOC Lifts
SOC Representability Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pairwise SOC-representable matrix conditions do not enforce general positive semidefiniteness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\rho\in(\tfrac12,1)\), let \[M_\rho=\begin{pmatrix}1&-\rho&-\rho\\-\rho&1&-\rho\\-\rho&-\rho&1\end{pmatrix}.\] Every principal \(2\times2\) submatrix is positive semidefinite because its eigenvalues are \(1-\rho\) and \(1+\rho\); each such condition is rotated-SOC representable. However, \(M_\rho\) has eigenvalue \(1-2\rho<0\) in the all-ones direction, so \(M_\rho\notin\mathbb S_+^3\). Thus replacing a matrix PSD constraint by all pairwise \(2\times2\) PSD constraints is generally only an SOC relaxation, not an exact representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matrix can satisfy every pairwise PSD, hence SOC-representable, condition while remaining indefinite. General semidefinite consistency therefore exceeds this pairwise SOC relaxation.
assumptions_latex: \(\tfrac12<\rho<1\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_\rho[\{i,j\}]\succeq0\) for every pair \(i,j\), but \(M_\rho\not\succeq0\).

notation.meaning: Principal submatrix indexed by i and j

children.title: Shor Relaxation Family
children.top_down_role: First-level matrix-lifting relaxations for continuous, binary, and mixed-integer quadratic models.

knowledge_statements.title: Shor Relaxation Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-level semidefinite lifting of continuous, binary, or mixed-integer QCQPs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m,n\in\mathbb N\), \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(q_k(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Q_kx+2c_k^{\mathsf T}x+d_k\) for \(k=0,\ldots,m\), where \(Q_k\in\mathbb S^n\), \(c_k\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(d_k\in\mathbb R\). Introduce \(X\in\mathbb S^n\) and \[Y:=\begin{pmatrix}1&x^{\mathsf T}\\x&X\end{pmatrix}.\] The Shor relaxation of \(\min\{q_0(x):q_k(x)\le0,\ k=1,\ldots,m\}\) is \[\min_{x,X}\ \langle Q_0,X\rangle+2c_0^{\mathsf T}x+d_0\quad\text{subject to}\quad \langle Q_k,X\rangle+2c_k^{\mathsf T}x+d_k\le0\ \ (k=1,\ldots,m),\quad Y\succeq0.\] Every feasible original point has the feasible lift \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\), so this SDP gives a lower bound. If \(B\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) indexes binary coordinates, one additionally imposes \(X_{jj}=x_j\) for \(j\in B\); one may relax \(x_j\in\{0,1\}\) to \(x_j\in[0,1]\), or retain integrality in a mixed-integer SDP relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Shor relaxation replaces quadratic products by entries of a symmetric matrix and replaces rank-one consistency by a positive-semidefinite block constraint. Diagonal equations represent binary squares, with binary integrality either relaxed or retained.
assumptions_latex: \(m,n\in\mathbb N\)
\(Q_k\in\mathbb S^n\), \(c_k\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(d_k\in\mathbb R\) for \(k=0,\ldots,m\)
The original QCQP is a minimization problem
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every feasible \(x\) has a feasible lift \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\), so the Shor relaxation gives a lower bound.

notation.meaning: Lifted surrogate for the product matrix xx-transpose

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lagrangian-Dual Interpretation of the Shor Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between the continuous Shor SDP dual and the scalar-multiplier Lagrangian bound for a QCQP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(q_k(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Q_kx+2c_k^{\mathsf T}x+d_k\), define \[\theta(\lambda)=\inf_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\left(q_0(x)+\sum_{k=1}^m\lambda_kq_k(x)\right),\qquad \lambda\ge0.\] The dual of the continuous Shor SDP is \(\sup_{\lambda\ge0}\theta(\lambda)\). Moreover, \(\theta(\lambda)\ge\gamma\) exactly when \[\begin{pmatrix}d_0+\sum_k\lambda_kd_k-\gamma&(c_0+\sum_k\lambda_kc_k)^{\mathsf T}\\c_0+\sum_k\lambda_kc_k&Q_0+\sum_k\lambda_kQ_k\end{pmatrix}\succeq0.\] If the continuous Shor SDP is strictly feasible and has finite optimum, its value equals this dual bound and the dual optimum is attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The continuous Shor bound is dual to the best global quadratic Lagrangian lower bound; strict SDP feasibility and finiteness give equality and dual attainment.
assumptions_latex: The QCQP constraints have the form \(q_k(x)\le0\).
The duality statement concerns the continuous SDP relaxation, not a mixed-integer SDP.
Strong duality assumes strict feasibility of the Shor SDP and a finite primal optimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: v_{\mathrm{Shor}}=\sup_{\lambda\ge0}\inf_x\left(q_0(x)+\sum_k\lambda_kq_k(x)\right)\text{ under the stated regularity assumptions}.
knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian-Dual Interpretation of the Shor Bound

children.title: Rank-Relaxation Mechanism
children.top_down_role: Convexification by retaining semidefinite consistency while relaxing rank-one or low-rank structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Relaxation Mechanism
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dropping rank while retaining semidefinite consistency produces a convex outer approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), \(X\in\mathbb S^n\), and \[Y:=\begin{pmatrix}1&x^{\mathsf T}\\x&X\end{pmatrix}.\] Then \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\) holds if and only if \[Y=\begin{pmatrix}1\\x\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}1\\x\end{pmatrix}^{\mathsf T},\] equivalently, \(Y\succeq0\), \(Y_{00}=1\), and \(\operatorname{rank}Y=1\). Dropping only the rank constraint leaves the convex spectrahedron \[Y\succeq0,\qquad Y_{00}=1,\] which contains every exact lift. Suppose all other lifted constraints and the objective are affine in \((x,X)\), and their restriction to \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\) is equivalent to the original model. Then the relaxation gives a lower bound for minimization, and any rank-one relaxed optimizer recovers a globally optimal feasible point of the original model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact product lifting is characterized by a rank-one positive-semidefinite block matrix. Dropping rank gives a convex outer relaxation; under exact correspondence of the remaining lifted model, a rank-one relaxed optimizer recovers a global original optimizer.
assumptions_latex: \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(X\in\mathbb S^n\)
All remaining lifted constraints and the objective are affine in \((x,X)\)
Restricting the lifted model to \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\) is equivalent to the original model
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dropping \(\operatorname{rank}Y=1\) yields an outer SDP relaxation, while a rank-one relaxed optimizer certifies exact recovery under the stated equivalence assumption.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent description of the semidefinite consistency retained after deleting rank one.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(X\in\mathbb S^n\), \[\begin{pmatrix}1&x^{\mathsf T}\\x&X\end{pmatrix}\succeq0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad X-xx^{\mathsf T}\succeq0.\] Thus the rank-relaxed lift permits exactly a positive-semidefinite slack \(W=X-xx^{\mathsf T}\), and exact rank-one consistency holds exactly when \(W=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The bordered PSD constraint allows a PSD slack above the exact product matrix; the lift is rank-one consistent exactly when that slack vanishes.
assumptions_latex: \(x\in\mathbb R^n\)
\(X\in\mathbb S^n\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Y\succeq0\iff X-xx^{\mathsf T}\succeq0,\qquad \operatorname{rank}Y=1\iff X-xx^{\mathsf T}=0.
knowledge_statements.title: Schur-Complement Form of Rank-Relaxation Slack

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed certificate duplicates a dedicated exactness-regime record outside this mechanism leaf.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonzero complementary primal matrix is rank one when the dual slack has a one-dimensional kernel.

Projected Spectrahedral Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semidefinite extended formulations whose projections contain the original feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A set \(R\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a projected spectrahedron, or spectrahedral shadow, if there exist symmetric matrices \(A_0,A_1,\ldots,A_n,B_1,\ldots,B_m\) of a common size such that \[R=\left\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\exists y\in\mathbb R^m,\ A_0+\sum_{i=1}^n x_iA_i+\sum_{j=1}^m y_jB_j\succeq0\right\}.\] For a feasible set \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), such an \(R\) is a projected spectrahedral relaxation when \(F\subseteq R\). Linear optimization over \(R\) is then an SDP in the extended variables \((x,y)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A projected spectrahedron is the projection of an affine semidefinite slice. It relaxes a feasible set when that projection contains every original feasible point.
assumptions_latex: All coefficient matrices are real and symmetric of one fixed size
\(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\subseteq R=\operatorname{proj}_x\{(x,y):A_0+\sum_i x_iA_i+\sum_j y_jB_j\succeq0\}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Optimizer Recovery from a CP Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery of original simplex optimizers from a decomposed optimum of the exact completely positive reformulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X^*\) solve \[\min\{\langle Q,X\rangle:\langle ee^{\mathsf T},X\rangle=1,\ X\in\mathcal{CP}^n\}\] and let \(X^*=\sum_{k=1}^{r}v_kv_k^{\mathsf T}\) with nonzero \(v_k\ge0\). Define \(\alpha_k=e^{\mathsf T}v_k\) and \(x_k=v_k/\alpha_k\). Then every \(x_k\) is feasible for \(\min\{x^{\mathsf T}Qx:x\ge0,\ e^{\mathsf T}x=1\}\), and every component having positive weight \(\alpha_k^2\) is globally optimal for that original problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every nonzero normalized factor in a completely positive decomposition of an optimal lifted matrix is a global optimizer of the original simplex quadratic problem.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\).
\(X^*\) is optimal for the stated completely positive program.
A completely positive decomposition of \(X^*\) is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_k\in\arg\min\{x^{\mathsf T}Qx:x\ge0,\ e^{\mathsf T}x=1\}\quad\text{for every nonzero decomposition term}.

notation.meaning: sum of the entries of the kth nonnegative factor

knowledge_statements.title: Optimizer Recovery from a CP Decomposition

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite nonnegative rank-one representation of completely positive matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Every \(X\in\mathcal{CP}^n\) admits a decomposition \[X=\sum_{k=1}^{r}v_kv_k^{\mathsf T},\qquad v_k\in\mathbb R_+^n,\qquad r\le \frac{n(n+1)}2.\] The least possible number of summands is the cp-rank of \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every completely positive matrix has a nonnegative rank-one decomposition with at most n(n+1)/2 terms; the minimum number of terms is its cp-rank.
assumptions_latex: \(X\in\mathcal{CP}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: X=\sum_{k=1}^{r}v_kv_k^{\mathsf T}\text{ for some }v_k\ge0\text{ and }r\le n(n+1)/2.

notation.meaning: minimum number of terms in a completely positive decomposition

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Completely Positive Decompositions
Exact Completely Positive Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact completely positive formulation of standard quadratic optimization over the simplex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(\mathcal{CP}^n:=\{\sum_{k=1}^N v_kv_k^{\mathsf T}:N<\infty,\ v_k\in\mathbb R_+^n\}\), and let \(e\) be the all-ones vector. For every \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\), the standard quadratic program satisfies \[\min\{x^{\mathsf T}Qx:x\ge0,\ e^{\mathsf T}x=1\}=\min\{\langle Q,X\rangle:\langle ee^{\mathsf T},X\rangle=1,\ X\in\mathcal{CP}^n\}.\] Thus lifting \(xx^{\mathsf T}\) into the completely positive cone convexifies the feasible rank-one matrices without changing the optimal value; an optimal rank-one \(X\) directly recovers an optimizer \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic program over the simplex equals a linear conic program over the completely positive cone, so the lift is convex and value-exact.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\)
The feasible region is \(\{x\ge0:e^{\mathsf T}x=1\}\)

children.title: Copositive Dual Representations
children.top_down_role: Dual cone representations associated with completely positive reformulations.

knowledge_statements.title: Copositive Dual Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual-cone and conic-program duality for completely positive formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The dual of the completely positive cone under the trace inner product is the copositive cone: \[(\mathcal{CP}^n)^*=\mathcal{COP}^n:=\{M\in\mathbb S^n:z^{\mathsf T}Mz\ge0\ \text{for every }z\in\mathbb R_+^n\}.\] Accordingly, the conic dual of \[\min\{\langle Q,X\rangle:\langle ee^{\mathsf T},X\rangle=1,\ X\in\mathcal{CP}^n\}\] is \[\max\{\gamma:Q-\gamma ee^{\mathsf T}\in\mathcal{COP}^n\}.\] Weak duality always holds, and equality follows whenever an applicable conic strong-duality qualification is satisfied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The copositive cone is dual to the completely positive cone. This turns a completely positive minimization formulation into a copositive maximization dual.
assumptions_latex: The pairing is \(\langle A,B\rangle=\operatorname{tr}(AB)\)
Primal and dual values use the stated minimization-maximization convention
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\mathcal{CP}^n)^*=\mathcal{COP}^n\) and the displayed conic programs are a primal-dual pair.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The CP-COP dual-cone identity and displayed conic dual are correct, but neither claim has a cited source with an inspectable locator.

children.title: Tractable Cone Approximations
children.top_down_role: Polyhedral and semidefinite approximations replacing computationally difficult matrix cones.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nested semidefinite-representable sufficient conditions converging over the interior of the copositive cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(M\in\mathbb S^n\), set \(p_M(y)=\sum_{i,j=1}^nM_{ij}y_i^2y_j^2\), and for \(r\in\mathbb Z_+\) define \[\mathcal K_r=\left\{M:\left(\sum_{i=1}^ny_i^2\right)^r p_M(y)\text{ is a sum-of-squares polynomial}\right\}.\] Each \(\mathcal K_r\) is semidefinite representable and \[\mathcal K_r\subseteq\mathcal K_{r+1}\subseteq\mathcal{COP}^n.\] Every strictly copositive matrix belongs to \(\mathcal K_r\) for some finite \(r\), so \(\operatorname{int}\mathcal{COP}^n\subseteq\bigcup_{r\ge0}\mathcal K_r\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Norm-multiplied sum-of-squares tests form nested SDP inner approximations of the copositive cone, and every strictly copositive matrix enters at a finite level.
assumptions_latex: \(M\in\mathbb S^n\).
\(r\in\mathbb Z_+\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal K_r\subseteq\mathcal K_{r+1}\subseteq\mathcal{COP}^n,\qquad \operatorname{int}\mathcal{COP}^n\subseteq\bigcup_{r\ge0}\mathcal K_r.

notation.meaning: even biquadratic form associated with M
level-r SOS inner approximation of the copositive cone

knowledge_statements.title: SOS Inner Hierarchy for Copositivity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp dimensions in which the basic doubly nonnegative approximation is exact.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(n\le4\), \[\mathcal{CP}^n=\mathcal{DNN}^n,\qquad \mathcal{COP}^n=\mathbb S_+^n+\mathbb N^n.\] For every \(n\ge5\), \[\mathcal{CP}^n\subsetneq\mathcal{DNN}^n,\qquad \mathbb S_+^n+\mathbb N^n\subsetneq\mathcal{COP}^n.\] Thus the basic SDP approximation is exact at the cone level through dimension four and can be strictly weaker from dimension five onward.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The DNN and PSD-plus-nonnegative approximations equal the exact CP and COP cones through dimension four, while both inclusions are strict from dimension five onward.
assumptions_latex: All cones are taken in \(\mathbb S^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: n\le4\Rightarrow\mathcal{CP}^n=\mathcal{DNN}^n;\qquad n\ge5\Rightarrow\mathcal{CP}^n\subsetneq\mathcal{DNN}^n,\text{ with the displayed dual equality or strictness}.
knowledge_statements.title: Low-Dimensional DNN Exactness Boundary
Tractable Cone Approximations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Doubly nonnegative outer approximation and its dual inner approximation for difficult matrix cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal{DNN}^n:=\mathbb S_+^n\cap\mathbb N^n\), where \(\mathbb N^n\) is the cone of entrywise nonnegative symmetric matrices. Then \[\mathcal{CP}^n\subseteq\mathcal{DNN}^n,\qquad (\mathcal{DNN}^n)^*=\mathbb S_+^n+\mathbb N^n\subseteq\mathcal{COP}^n.\] Therefore replacing \(X\in\mathcal{CP}^n\) by \(X\in\mathcal{DNN}^n\) gives a tractable SDP outer relaxation and a lower bound for completely positive minimization. Dually, requiring a copositive matrix to lie in \(\mathbb S_+^n+\mathbb N^n\) gives a tractable inner approximation and a valid, possibly weaker, dual bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Doubly nonnegative matrices outer-approximate completely positive matrices. The dual PSD-plus-nonnegative cone inner-approximates the copositive cone, producing tractable SDP bounds.
assumptions_latex: All matrix cones lie in \(\mathbb S^n\)
Bounds refer to minimization over the primal cone
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal{CP}^n\subseteq\mathcal{DNN}^n\) and \(\mathbb S_+^n+\mathbb N^n\subseteq\mathcal{COP}^n\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cone inclusions and primal-dual approximation directions are correct and fit the approximation container, but an authoritative source locator is required.

children.title: S-Lemma-S-Procedure Correspondence

children.title: S-Lemma Exactness Regime
children.top_down_role: Quadratic implication settings supporting exact semidefinite representation.

knowledge_statements.title: S-Lemma Exactness Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inhomogeneous real S-lemma with one quadratic constraint and strict feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(i\in\{0,1\}\), let \(A_i\in\mathbb S^n\), \(b_i\in\mathbb R^n\), \(c_i\in\mathbb R\), and define \(q_i:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) by \(q_i(x)=x^{\mathsf T}A_ix+2b_i^{\mathsf T}x+c_i\). Suppose there exists \(\bar x\in\mathbb R^n\) such that \(q_1(\bar x)<0\). Then \[q_1(x)\le0\ \Longrightarrow\ q_0(x)\ge0\qquad\text{for every }x\in\mathbb R^n\] holds if and only if there exists \(\lambda\ge0\) such that \[q_0(x)+\lambda q_1(x)\ge0\qquad\text{for every }x\in\mathbb R^n.\] Equivalently, the augmented symmetric matrix representing \(q_0+\lambda q_1\) is positive semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For two real inhomogeneous quadratic functions, strict feasibility of the single premise inequality makes the implication equivalent to a global quadratic certificate with one nonnegative multiplier.
assumptions_latex: \(A_i\in\mathbb S^n\), \(b_i\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(c_i\in\mathbb R\) for \(i\in\{0,1\}\)
There exists \(\bar x\in\mathbb R^n\) with \(q_1(\bar x)<0\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \([q_1\le0\Rightarrow q_0\ge0]\iff[\exists\lambda\ge0:\ q_0+\lambda q_1\ge0\text{ on }\mathbb R^n]\).

notation.meaning: Real inhomogeneous quadratic function from R^n to R

review_flags: locator support for the S-lemma remains provisional

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degenerate single-premise implication for which no S-lemma multiplier exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(\mathbb R\), let \(q_1(x)=x^2\) and \(q_0(x)=x\). Since \(q_1(x)\le0\) forces \(x=0\), the implication \(q_1(x)\le0\Rightarrow q_0(x)\ge0\) is valid. Nevertheless, for every \(\lambda\ge0\), \(x+\lambda x^2\) is negative at some sufficiently small \(x<0\). Thus the multiplier conclusion can fail when the premise has no strictly feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without strict feasibility, a valid implication with one quadratic premise need not admit an S-lemma multiplier.
assumptions_latex: No \(x\) satisfies \(q_1(x)<0\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \([q_1\le0\Rightarrow q_0\ge0]\) holds, but \(\nexists\lambda\ge0\) such that \(q_0+\lambda q_1\ge0\) on \(\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.title: Failure Without Strict Feasibility

children.title: S-Procedure Certificate Regime
children.top_down_role: Quadratic implication certificates obtained through scalar aggregation.

knowledge_statements.title: S-Procedure Certificate Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonnegative-multiplier certificate for quadratic implications; sufficient generally and exact in the one-constraint S-lemma regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m,n\in\mathbb N\). For \(i=0,1,\ldots,m\), let \(A_i\in\mathbb S^n\), \(b_i\in\mathbb R^n\), \(c_i\in\mathbb R\), and define \(q_i:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) by \(q_i(x)=x^{\mathsf T}A_ix+2b_i^{\mathsf T}x+c_i\). If there exist multipliers \(\lambda_i\ge0\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\) such that \[q_0(x)+\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_iq_i(x)\ge0\qquad\text{for every }x\in\mathbb R^n,\] then \[q_i(x)\le0\ \text{for all }i=1,\ldots,m\quad\Longrightarrow\quad q_0(x)\ge0.\] The certificate can be checked by positive semidefiniteness of the augmented matrix representing \(q_0+\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_iq_i\). When \(m=1\) and there exists \(\bar x\in\mathbb R^n\) with \(q_1(\bar x)<0\), the S-lemma makes the certificate necessary as well as sufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For finitely many real quadratic premises, a globally nonnegative combination using nonnegative scalar multipliers certifies the implication. The certificate is always sufficient and is also necessary for one strictly feasible quadratic premise.
assumptions_latex: \(m,n\in\mathbb N\)
\(A_i\in\mathbb S^n\), \(b_i\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(c_i\in\mathbb R\) for \(i=0,\ldots,m\)
\(\lambda_i\ge0\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Global nonnegativity of \(q_0+\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_iq_i\) certifies \(\{q_i\le0\}_{i=1}^m\Rightarrow q_0\ge0\).

notation.meaning: Real quadratic premise or conclusion function from R^n to R

review_flags: locator support for the S-procedure remains provisional

children.title: Multiple-Constraint Failure Boundary
children.top_down_role: Loss of exactness as additional quadratic constraints alter the implication structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiple-Constraint Failure Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two quadratic constraints can invalidate necessity of the scalar-multiplier S-procedure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(\mathbb R\), define \(q_1(x)=x\), \(q_2(x)=-x\), and \(q_0(x)=-x^2\). The simultaneous inequalities \(q_1(x)\le0\) and \(q_2(x)\le0\) force \(x=0\), so they imply \(q_0(x)\ge0\). Nevertheless, for every \(\lambda_1,\lambda_2\ge0\), \[q_0(x)+\lambda_1q_1(x)+\lambda_2q_2(x)=-x^2+(\lambda_1-\lambda_2)x\] has negative leading coefficient and cannot be nonnegative on all of \(\mathbb R\). Thus a valid implication with multiple constraints need not possess a scalar S-procedure certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two opposing affine constraints force x to zero and imply a quadratic conclusion, yet no nonnegative scalar multipliers produce a globally nonnegative certificate.
assumptions_latex: The S-procedure uses constant nonnegative scalar multipliers
The implication is interpreted over \(\mathbb R\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q_1\le0,\ q_2\le0\Rightarrow q_0\ge0\), but no \(\lambda_1,\lambda_2\ge0\) make \(q_0+\lambda_1q_1+\lambda_2q_2\ge0\) globally.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample is algebraically correct and is an appropriate witness for the multiple-constraint failure boundary, but no authoritative source locator is supplied.

children.title: Trust-Region Exactness Regimes
children.top_down_role: Structured quadratic regimes where conic or semidefinite relaxation is exact.

knowledge_statements.title: Trust-Region Exactness Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact Shor SDP relaxation for the classical Euclidean trust-region subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\), \(q\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(\Delta>0\). For the trust-region problem \[p^*=\min_{\lVert x\rVert_2\le\Delta}\ x^{\mathsf T}Qx+2q^{\mathsf T}x,\] possibly with indefinite \(Q\), the Shor relaxation \[p_{\mathrm{SDP}}=\min\ \langle Q,X\rangle+2q^{\mathsf T}x\quad\text{subject to}\quad \operatorname{tr}(X)\le\Delta^2,\ \begin{pmatrix}1&x^{\mathsf T}\\x&X\end{pmatrix}\succeq0\] is value-exact: \(p_{\mathrm{SDP}}=p^*\). An optimal solution of the original trust-region problem exists, and its rank-one lift attains the SDP optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For one Euclidean ball constraint, the Shor semidefinite relaxation of an indefinite quadratic minimization problem has exactly the original optimal value.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\) and \(q\in\mathbb R^n\)
\(\Delta>0\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_{\mathrm{SDP}}=p^*\), with an optimal rank-one lift \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\).
review_flags: trust-region specialization should be confirmed at locator

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral solution route for the classical trust-region subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(Q\succeq0\) and an unconstrained solution of \(Qx=-q\) lies in the ball, it is optimal. Otherwise seek \(\lambda\ge\max\{0,-\lambda_{\min}(Q)\}\). When \(Q+\lambda I\succ0\), set \(x(\lambda)=-(Q+\lambda I)^{-1}q\) and solve \(\|x(\lambda)\|_2=\Delta\). In the hard case, where \(Q+\lambda I\succeq0\) is singular and \(q\in\operatorname{range}(Q+\lambda I)\), take \(x=-(Q+\lambda I)^\dagger q+z\), with \(z\in\ker(Q+\lambda I)\) chosen so that \(\|x\|_2=\Delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The classical trust-region problem reduces to a monotone secular equation, with a nullspace correction in the singular hard case.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\)
\(q\in\mathbb R^n\)
\(\Delta>0\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stated regular or hard-case construction yields a global minimizer.

notation.meaning: Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse of the shifted Hessian

knowledge_statements.title: Secular-Equation and Hard-Case Solution

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient multiplier conditions for a global trust-region minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A vector \(x^*\) globally minimizes \(x^{\mathsf T}Qx+2q^{\mathsf T}x\) over \(\|x\|_2\le\Delta\) if and only if there exists \(\lambda^*\ge0\) such that \[(Q+\lambda^*I)x^*=-q,\qquad Q+\lambda^*I\succeq0,\qquad \lambda^*(\|x^*\|_2^2-\Delta^2)=0,\qquad \|x^*\|_2\le\Delta.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stationarity, a positive-semidefinite shifted Hessian, feasibility, and complementary slackness are necessary and sufficient for global trust-region optimality.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\)
\(q\in\mathbb R^n\)
\(\Delta>0\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed system is equivalent to global optimality of \(x^*\).
knowledge_statements.title: Trust-Region Global Optimality Conditions

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Semidefinite Dual of the Trust-Region Problem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Attained one-multiplier LMI dual for the classical trust-region problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(p^*=\min_{\|x\|_2\le\Delta}x^{\mathsf T}Qx+2q^{\mathsf T}x\), \[p^*=\max_{\lambda\ge0,\,\gamma\in\mathbb R}\left\{\gamma:\begin{pmatrix}Q+\lambda I&q\\q^{\mathsf T}&-\lambda\Delta^2-\gamma\end{pmatrix}\succeq0\right\}.\] The maximum is attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The classical trust-region problem has an attained one-multiplier semidefinite dual with no value gap.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\)
\(q\in\mathbb R^n\)
\(\Delta>0\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p^*=d^*\), and the displayed dual maximum is attained.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Semidefinite Dual of the Trust-Region Problem

children.title: Multiple-Quadratic-Constraint Gaps
children.top_down_role: Limits of single-constraint exactness mechanisms in broader QCQP geometry.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit value gap for a homogeneous QCQP with several quadratic equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\max\{\frac12\sum_{1\le i<j\le3}(1-x_ix_j):x_i^2=1\ (i=1,2,3)\}\). Its optimum is \(2\). The Shor relaxation is \[\max\ \frac12\sum_{i<j}(1-X_{ij})\quad\text{s.t.}\quad X\succeq0,\ X_{ii}=1.\] The matrix with \(X_{ij}=-\tfrac12\) for \(i\ne j\) is positive semidefinite and attains \(9/4\), which is also the relaxation optimum. Hence the relaxation gap is \(1/4\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Triangle Max-Cut has QCQP value 2 but Shor-relaxation value 9/4, exhibiting a strict gap with multiple quadratic constraints.
assumptions_latex: The Shor relaxation drops \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\) while retaining \(X\succeq0\) and \(X_{ii}=1\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_{\mathrm{SDP}}=9/4>2=p_{\mathrm{QCQP}}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Triangle Max-Cut Shor Relaxation Gap
Multiple-Quadratic-Constraint Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A concrete failure of lossless scalar-multiplier aggregation for two quadratic constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x=(x_1,x_2)\in\mathbb R^2\), \(q_1(x)=x_1^2\), \(q_2(x)=x_2^2\), and \(f(x)=x_1\). The implications \(q_1(x)\le 0\) and \(q_2(x)\le 0\Rightarrow f(x)\le 0\) hold because the quadratic constraints force \(x=0\). Nevertheless, there are no multipliers \(\lambda_1,\lambda_2\ge 0\) such that \(f(x)\le\lambda_1q_1(x)+\lambda_2q_2(x)\) for every \(x\): setting \(x_2=0\) and \(0<x_1<1/\max\{1,\lambda_1\}\) contradicts that inequality. Thus single-constraint S-lemma exactness does not extend automatically to multiple quadratic constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two quadratic constraints can imply a target inequality even though no nonnegative scalar aggregation certifies it, so single-constraint S-lemma exactness does not extend automatically.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q_1\le0,\ q_2\le0\Rightarrow f\le0\), but \(f\le\lambda_1q_1+\lambda_2q_2\) fails globally for every \(\lambda_1,\lambda_2\ge0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex QCQP and its epigraph form
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition of a convex quadratically constrained quadratic program with positive-semidefinite quadratic forms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let n,m\in\mathbb{N}. For i=0,\ldots,m, let q_i(x)=\alpha_i+\langle a_i,x\rangle+\tfrac12\langle A_i x,x\rangle on \mathbb{R}^n, where \alpha_i\in\mathbb{R}, a_i\in\mathbb{R}^n, and A_i\succeq0. Given \beta_i\in\mathbb{R} for i=1,\ldots,m, the convex QCQP is \min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\{q_0(x):q_i(x)\le\beta_i,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}. It is equivalent to the epigraph problem \min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n,\tau\in\mathbb{R}}\{\tau:q_0(x)\le\tau,\ q_i(x)\le\beta_i,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex QCQP minimizes a convex quadratic function subject to finitely many convex quadratic inequalities. Introducing an epigraph variable for the objective gives an equivalent problem that minimizes that variable subject to the original constraints and an objective-epigraph inequality.
assumptions_latex: n,m\in\mathbb{N}
q_i(x)=\alpha_i+\langle a_i,x\rangle+\tfrac12\langle A_i x,x\rangle\quad(i=0,\ldots,m)
\alpha_i\in\mathbb{R},\ a_i\in\mathbb{R}^n,\ A_i\succeq0\quad(i=0,\ldots,m)
\beta_i\in\mathbb{R}\quad(i=1,\ldots,m)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_x\{q_0(x):q_i(x)\le\beta_i,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\ \equiv\ \min_{x,\tau}\{\tau:q_0(x)\le\tau,\ q_i(x)\le\beta_i,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}

knowledge_statements.title: LP–SOC–SDP Dominance Patterns
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional strength ordering for relaxations constructed on a common variable space and objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a minimization problem with feasible set \(F\), objective \(c^Tx\), and LP, SOC, and SDP relaxation projections \(P_{\mathrm{LP}},P_{\mathrm{SOC}},P_{\mathrm{SDP}}\). If \(F\subseteq P_{\mathrm{SDP}}\subseteq P_{\mathrm{SOC}}\subseteq P_{\mathrm{LP}}\), then their optimal lower bounds satisfy \[v_{\mathrm{LP}}\le v_{\mathrm{SOC}}\le v_{\mathrm{SDP}}\le v_F.\] Equality or strict inequality may occur at any adjacent pair. The ordering is not implied merely by the cone names; it requires the displayed nesting after auxiliary variables are projected onto the common original-variable space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested LP, SOC, and SDP feasible projections give increasingly strong minimization bounds. Cone labels alone do not establish this ordering.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq P_{\mathrm{SDP}}\subseteq P_{\mathrm{SOC}}\subseteq P_{\mathrm{LP}}\)
All four problems minimize the same objective \(c^Tx\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_{\mathrm{LP}}\le v_{\mathrm{SOC}}\le v_{\mathrm{SDP}}\le v_F\).

children.title: Dual-Bound Quality
children.top_down_role: Assessment of relaxation strength through dual objective information.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Bound Quality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual-feasible lower bounds and their measurable gap from a primal incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the conic minimization problem \(p^*=\inf\{\langle c,x\rangle:Ax=b,\ x\in K\}\), let \((y,s)\) satisfy \(A^*y+s=c\) and \(s\in K^*\). Weak duality gives the certified lower bound \(\langle b,y\rangle\le p^*\). If \(\bar x\) is feasible, then \[0\le p^*-\langle b,y\rangle\le\langle c,\bar x\rangle-\langle b,y\rangle.\] Hence the computable primal-dual gap on the right certifies dual-bound quality; a zero gap certifies optimality of both feasible points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any dual-feasible point gives a rigorous lower bound. Its gap from a feasible primal incumbent bounds suboptimality, and a zero gap certifies optimality.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a closed convex cone.
\(Ax=b,\ x\in K\) and \(A^*y+s=c,\ s\in K^*\) are feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\langle b,y\rangle\le p^*\le\langle c,\bar x\rangle\), with zero primal-dual gap certifying optimality.

source_refs.locator: 2.4.2 Consequences of the conic duality theorem p. 61

source_witnesses.locator: 2.4.2 Consequences of the conic duality theorem p. 61

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute and dimensionless reporting of separation between a feasible incumbent and a certified conic lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L\le p^*\le U\), where \(L\) is a certified lower bound and \(U\) is a finite feasible-incumbent value for a minimization problem. The absolute certified gap is \(g_{\mathrm{abs}}=U-L\). For a declared scale \(\sigma>0\), the normalized gap is \(g_{\mathrm{rel}}=(U-L)/\sigma\); any convention such as \(\sigma=\max\{1,|U|,|L|\}\) must be stated. A ratio \(U/L\) has a multiplicative-quality interpretation only under compatible sign conditions such as \(0<L\le p^*\le U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual-bound quality may be reported by an absolute or declared scale-normalized gap; multiplicative ratios require positive compatible bounds.
assumptions_latex: \(L\) is a valid finite lower bound and \(U\) is the finite objective value of a feasible incumbent.
Any normalization scale is positive and explicitly declared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0\le p^*-L\le g_{\mathrm{abs}},\qquad g_{\mathrm{rel}}=g_{\mathrm{abs}}/\sigma.

notation.meaning: Certified lower bound and feasible-incumbent upper bound

children.title: Rank-Recovery Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Assessment of exactness through matrix rank or recoverable primal structure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative diagnostics for distance of a nonzero positive-semidefinite lift from rank one.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y\succeq0\) be nonzero with eigenvalues \(\lambda_1\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_m\ge0\). Its best rank-at-most-one approximation in Frobenius norm is \(Y_1=\lambda_1u_1u_1^{\mathsf T}\), and \[\min_{\operatorname{rank}(Z)\le1}\|Y-Z\|_F=\left(\sum_{i=2}^m\lambda_i^2\right)^{1/2}.\] Hence \(\operatorname{rank}(Y)=1\) exactly when the eigenvalue tail is zero. A small tail, \(\lambda_2/\lambda_1\), or \((\operatorname{tr}Y-\lambda_1)/\operatorname{tr}Y\) measures near-rank-one structure but does not certify feasibility or objective preservation after factor recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Trailing eigenvalues quantify distance from rank one; only an exactly zero tail gives exact rank one, and faithful recovery checks remain necessary.
assumptions_latex: \(Y\) is a nonzero real symmetric positive-semidefinite matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{rank}(Y)=1\iff\sum_{i=2}^m\lambda_i^2=0.

notation.meaning: Ordered eigenvalues of the lifted matrix

knowledge_statements.title: Spectral Rank-One Residual Diagnostics
Rank-Recovery Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact recovery from a rank-one moment or lifted SDP solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an SDP relaxation uses \(Y=\begin{pmatrix}1&x^T\\x&X\end{pmatrix}\succeq0\) to relax \(X=xx^T\). If an optimal solution \(Y^*\) satisfies \(Y^*_{00}=1\) and \(\operatorname{rank}(Y^*)=1\), then there is an \(x^*\in\mathbb R^n\) such that \(Y^*=(1,(x^*)^T)^T(1,(x^*)^T)\), and hence \(X^*=x^*(x^*)^T\). If, under this factorization, every lifted constraint reduces to the corresponding original constraint and the lifted objective equals the original objective at \(x^*\), then \(x^*\) is feasible for the original problem and attains the SDP value. Thus rank one is an exact recovery certificate under faithful constraint and objective lifting; a small eigenvalue ratio is only a numerical diagnostic, not an exact certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normalized rank-one optimal lift certifies exact recovery when its factor satisfies the original constraints and preserves the original objective. Near-rank-one spectra provide only numerical evidence.
assumptions_latex: \(Y^*\) is optimal and satisfies \(Y^*\succeq0\) and \(Y^*_{00}=1\).
Under \(X=xx^T\), the lifted constraints reduce to the original constraints and the lifted objective equals the original objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}(Y^*)=1\) implies \(X^*=x^*(x^*)^T\), and faithful constraint and objective lifting imply that \(x^*\) is feasible and attains the relaxation value.

children.title: Certificate Agreement Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes where dual evidence and rank evidence support compatible conclusions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Logical Independence of Bound and Recovery Evidence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-sided regimes in which only dual-bound or rank-recovery evidence is available.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a valid minimization relaxation with value \(v_r\le v_o\), zero primal-dual gap for the relaxation proves that its feasible primal and dual values equal \(v_r\), but does not imply \(v_r=v_o\) or rank-one recoverability. Conversely, a rank-one lifted point that faithfully recovers \(x\in F_o\) proves only that \(x\) is original-feasible unless that lifted point is certified optimal or a valid lower bound equals \(f(x)\). Thus dual-bound and rank-recovery evidence are logically independent until they meet at a common certified objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A solved relaxation need not be exact, and a recoverable feasible factor need not be globally optimal; equality with a certified bound joins the two certificates.
assumptions_latex: The relaxation is a valid outer relaxation of an original minimization problem.
Any claimed rank-one factor faithfully recovers an original-feasible point and its objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: [\operatorname{gap}_r=0]\not\Rightarrow[v_r=v_o],\qquad [x\in F_o]\not\Rightarrow[f(x)=v_o].
knowledge_statements.title: Logical Independence of Bound and Recovery Evidence
Certificate Agreement Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Agreement of dual-bound and rank-one recovery certificates for a lifted minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y^*\) be primal feasible for a lifted conic minimization relaxation, let \((y^*,s^*)\) be dual feasible, and suppose \(\langle C,Y^*\rangle=\langle b,y^*\rangle\). If \(Y^*\) is normalized rank one and its factor yields an original feasible point \(x^*\) with the same objective value, then weak duality gives \[\langle b,y^*\rangle=v_{\mathrm{relax}}=f(x^*)=v_{\mathrm{original}}.\] Thus the zero duality gap and rank-recovery certificates agree and jointly certify relaxation exactness and global optimality of \(x^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero conic duality gap plus faithful rank-one recovery makes the dual bound, relaxation value, and original objective coincide, certifying global optimality.
assumptions_latex: Primal and dual lifted solutions are feasible with equal objectives.
The normalized rank-one primal factor is feasible for the original problem and preserves its objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\langle b,y^*\rangle=v_{\mathrm{relax}}=f(x^*)=v_{\mathrm{original}}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Facial Degeneracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Facial reduction sense of degeneracy for a conic feasible region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\) be a closed convex cone in a finite-dimensional space and let \(F=\{x\in K:Ax=b\}\ne\varnothing\). Define the minimal face of \(K\) containing the feasible set by \[\operatorname{face}_K(F)=\bigcap\{G:G\text{ is a face of }K,\ F\subseteq G\}.\] The conic system is facially degenerate relative to the declared cone \(K\) when \(\operatorname{face}_K(F)\subsetneq K\). Equivalently, \(F\cap\operatorname{ri}K=\varnothing\). Replacing \(K\) by \(\operatorname{face}_K(F)\) identifies the smaller cone containing all feasible solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible conic system is facially degenerate relative to its declared cone when its feasible set lies in a proper face, equivalently when it contains no point in the cone's relative interior.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a finite-dimensional closed convex cone.
\(F=\{x\in K:Ax=b\}\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Facial degeneracy means \(\operatorname{face}_K(F)\subsetneq K\), equivalently \(F\cap\operatorname{ri}K=\varnothing\).

children.title: Strict-Feasibility Loss

knowledge_statements.title: Strict-Feasibility Loss
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of relative primal Slater feasibility in a finite-dimensional conic system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\) be a convex cone in a finite-dimensional space and let \(F=\{x\in K:Ax=b\}\). Relative primal strict feasibility is the predicate \[\exists x\in\operatorname{ri}K\quad Ax=b.\] Strict-feasibility loss occurs when the system is feasible but this predicate is false: \[F\ne\varnothing,\qquad F\cap\operatorname{ri}K=\varnothing.\] If \(K\) is full-dimensional, then \(\operatorname{ri}K=\operatorname{int}K\), so this reduces to the usual ambient-interior Slater condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relative strict feasibility is lost when feasible conic points exist but none lies in the cone's relative interior; for a full-dimensional cone this is the usual interior condition.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a convex cone in a finite-dimensional space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Strict-feasibility loss is \(F\ne\varnothing\) together with \(F\cap\operatorname{ri}K=\varnothing\).

children.title: Duality-Gap Risk
children.top_down_role: Dual attainment or gap consequences associated with defective feasibility geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Duality-Gap Risk
knowledge_statements.scope_note: What ceases to be guaranteed when conic constraint qualifications fail.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a primal-dual conic pair, weak duality remains valid without strict feasibility. However, if the applicable primal and dual Slater conditions both fail, the standard conic strong-duality theorem no longer guarantees equality of optimal values or attainment. Consequently, one cannot infer \(p^*=d^*\), existence of optimal certificates, or complementary-slackness witnesses solely from primal and dual feasibility. The failure of Slater conditions is a risk boundary, not proof that a positive gap must occur; strong duality may still hold through facial reduction or another constraint qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without a suitable Slater condition, weak duality survives but zero gap and attainment are no longer guaranteed; failure does not itself prove a gap.
assumptions_latex: A primal-dual pair is posed over closed convex cones.
Neither available side satisfies the applicable Slater condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasibility alone does not imply \(p^*=d^*\) or attainment when the relevant constraint qualifications fail.

children.title: Numerical Stability Consequences

knowledge_statements.title: Numerical Stability Consequences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Barrier-curvature deterioration near a singular semidefinite face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
On \(\mathbb S_{++}^n\), let \(\phi(X)=-\log\det X\). Its Hessian acts as \[
abla^2\phi(X)[H]=X^{-1}HX^{-1}.\] Under the Frobenius-induced operator norm, \[\|
abla^2\phi(X)\|=\lambda_{\min}(X)^{-2}.\] Hence, if \(X_k\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\) and \(\lambda_{\min}(X_k)\downarrow0\), then \(\|
abla^2\phi(X_k)\|	o\infty\). Moreover, the Hessian condition number is \[\kappa(
abla^2\phi(X))=\left( rac{\lambda_{\max}(X)}{\lambda_{\min}(X)}ight)^2.\] Thus approaching a singular face produces unbounded barrier curvature, and it produces increasingly ill-conditioned barrier Hessians when the eigenvalue ratio diverges. Scaling, regularization, or facial reduction can address the vanishing-eigenvalue directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near a singular semidefinite face, log-determinant barrier curvature diverges. The barrier Hessian becomes increasingly ill-conditioned when the largest-to-smallest eigenvalue ratio also diverges.
assumptions_latex: \(X\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\).
Matrix-space norms are Frobenius-induced operator norms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda_{\min}(X_k)\downarrow0\) implies \(\|\nabla^2\phi(X_k)\|\to\infty\); if also \(\lambda_{\max}(X_k)/\lambda_{\min}(X_k)\to\infty\), then \(\kappa(\nabla^2\phi(X_k))\to\infty\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of the declared-cone barrier formulation when a feasible affine slice has no relatively interior point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\) be a finite-dimensional closed convex cone and let \(\Phi\) be a barrier with relative domain \(\operatorname{ri}K\). If \(S=\{x\in K:Ax=b\}\ne\varnothing\) but \(S\cap\operatorname{ri}K=\varnothing\), then for every \(\mu>0\) the barrier subproblem \[\inf\{\langle c,x\rangle+\mu\Phi(x):Ax=b,\ x\in\operatorname{ri}K\}\] has empty feasible domain, so the corresponding primal central path in the declared cone is undefined. If \(G=\operatorname{face}_K(S)\), then \(S\cap\operatorname{ri}G\ne\varnothing\); replacing \(K\) by \(G\) permits an intrinsic barrier formulation on \(\operatorname{ri}G\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a feasible conic slice misses the relative interior of its declared cone, the declared-cone barrier path is undefined. Passing to the minimal feasible face restores an intrinsic barrier domain.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a finite-dimensional closed convex cone.
\(\operatorname{dom}\Phi=\operatorname{ri}K\) relative to \(\operatorname{span}K\).
\(S\ne\varnothing\) and \(S\cap\operatorname{ri}K=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The declared-cone barrier subproblem has empty feasible domain, while the minimal face \(G\) satisfies \(S\cap\operatorname{ri}G\ne\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: minimal face of K containing S

children.title: Positive-Scale Perspectives
children.top_down_role: Perspective structure away from the zero-scale boundary.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scaling law intrinsic to the strictly positive activity region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the positive-scale perspective \(p_f(x,t)=t f(x/t)\), every \(\lambda>0\) satisfies \[p_f(\lambda x,\lambda t)=\lambda p_f(x,t).\] Conversely, every \((x,t)\) with \(t>0\) has the unique activity-one representative \((x/t,1)\) on its positive ray, and \[p_f(x,t)=t\,p_f(x/t,1)=t f(x/t).\] Thus its epigraph is invariant under positive conic scaling, although the zero-scale boundary need not be present before closure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The positive perspective is one-homogeneous, and division by activity uniquely recovers the activity-one representative on each positive ray.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is proper and convex.
\(t>0\) and \(\lambda>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p_f(\lambda x,\lambda t)=\lambda p_f(x,t),\qquad p_f(x,t)=t p_f(x/t,1).
knowledge_statements.title: Positive Homogeneity and Ray Dehomogenization
Positive-Scale Perspectives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Perspective transformation restricted to strictly positive scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper and convex. Its positive-scale perspective is the function \(p_f:\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R_{++}\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) defined by \[p_f(x,t)=t f(x/t),\qquad t>0.\] The function \(p_f\) is convex on its domain. Its epigraph satisfies \[\operatorname{epi}p_f=\{(x,t,r):t>0,\ (x/t,r/t)\in\operatorname{epi}f\},\] exhibiting the perspective as the positive conic homogenization of the epigraph of \(f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For positive scale, the perspective is t times f evaluated at x/t; it is convex and homogenizes the epigraph of f.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is proper and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_f(x,t)=t f(x/t)\) is convex on \(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R_{++}\).

children.title: Zero-Activity Closure

knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Activity Closure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed value of a convex perspective on the zero-scale boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper, closed, and convex, and let \(f^\infty\) be its recession function. The closed perspective \(\bar p_f\) is \[\bar p_f(x,t)=\begin{cases}t f(x/t),&t>0,\\ f^\infty(x),&t=0,\\ +\infty,&t<0.\end{cases}\] In particular, zero activity at \((x,t)=(0,0)\) has value \(\bar p_f(0,0)=f^\infty(0)=0\). This boundary assignment is the lower-semicontinuous closure of the positive-scale perspective, rather than an arbitrary convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The closed perspective assigns the recession value at zero scale; at zero activity its value is zero, yielding the lower-semicontinuous closure.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, closed, and convex.
\(f^\infty\) denotes the recession function of f.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar p_f(x,0)=f^\infty(x)\), and specifically \(\bar p_f(0,0)=0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual Support Representation of Recession Values
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent dual characterization of the zero-scale value along a recession direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every proper closed convex \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), \[f^\infty(d)=\sigma_{\operatorname{dom}f^*}(d)=\sup_{y\in\operatorname{dom}f^*}\langle y,d\rangle.\] Hence the closed-perspective boundary value is \(p_f(d,0)=\sigma_{\operatorname{dom}f^*}(d)\), and it is finite exactly when this support supremum is finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero-scale recession value is the support function of the effective domain of the Fenchel conjugate.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, closed, and convex.
\(f^*\) is the Fenchel conjugate of \(f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p_f(d,0)=f^\infty(d)=\sup_{y\in\operatorname{dom}f^*}\langle y,d\rangle.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual Support Representation of Recession Values
Recession-Direction Extension
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary representation of the closed perspective in nonzero recession directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a proper closed convex function \(f\), choose any \(x_0\in\operatorname{dom}f\). Its recession function is \[f^\infty(d)=\sup_{\alpha>0}\frac{f(x_0+\alpha d)-f(x_0)}{\alpha},\] independently of the chosen \(x_0\). The closed perspective extends the positive-scale formula to the zero-scale boundary by \[\bar p_f(d,0)=f^\infty(d).\] Therefore a nonzero direction \(d\) has finite zero-scale perspective value exactly when \(d\in\operatorname{dom}f^\infty\); otherwise the boundary value is \(+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At zero scale, the closed perspective equals the recession function, so precisely the finite recession directions remain admissible.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is proper, closed, and convex.
\(x_0\in\operatorname{dom}f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar p_f(d,0)=f^\infty(d)\), finite exactly for \(d\in\operatorname{dom}f^\infty\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact boundary for extending a positive-scale perspective by only the inactive origin.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper, closed, and convex, and define \(q_f(x,t)=t f(x/t)\) for \(t>0\), \(q_f(0,0)=0\), and \(q_f(x,t)=+\infty\) otherwise. knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fenchel conjugate with the activity variable paired with \(\mu\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \((y,\mu)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\), the Fenchel conjugate of the closed perspective is
\[p_f^*(y,\mu)=\sup_{(x,t)}\{\langle y,x\rangle+\mu t-p_f(x,t)\}=\begin{cases}0,&f^*(y)+\mu\le0,\\+\infty,&f^*(y)+\mu>0.\end{cases}\]
Thus \(p_f^*=\delta_D\), where \(D=\{(y,\mu):f^*(y)+\mu\le0\}\). Consequently, the closed perspective is the support function \(p_f=\sigma_D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The perspective conjugate is the indicator of the hypograph-like set defined by the inequality between the dual activity coefficient and the conjugate of the base function.

children.title: Primal–Dual Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Structural links between perspective epigraphs and conjugate representations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subgradient characterization at a finite zero-scale perspective point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) be proper, closed, and convex, and suppose \(f^\infty(d)<+\infty\). For its closed perspective \(p_f\), \[(y,\mu)\in\partial p_f(d,0)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad f^*(y)+\mu\le0\ \text{ and }\ \langle y,d\rangle=f^\infty(d).\] Thus a dual point supports the perspective at zero activity exactly when its spatial component attains the support representation of the recession value. Unlike the positive-activity case, \(f^*(y)+\mu\le0\) need not be tight.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At zero activity, a perspective subgradient is a dual-feasible pair whose spatial component exposes the recession value; the activity inequality may have slack.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is proper, closed, and convex.
\(p_f\) is its closed perspective.
\(f^\infty(d)<+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (y,\mu)\in\partial p_f(d,0)\iff f^*(y)+\mu\le0\ \land\ \langle y,d\rangle=f^\infty(d).

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((y,\mu)\in\partial p_f(x,t)\iff y\in\partial f(u)\ \text{and}\ \mu=-f^*(y)=f(u)-\langle y,u\rangle\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-activity subgradient correspondence for scalar perspectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(u=x/t\). A pair \((y,\mu)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\) is a subgradient of \(p_f\) at \((x,t)\) if and only if
\[y\in\partial f(u),\qquad \mu=f(u)-\langle y,u\rangle=-f^*(y).\]
Equivalently, primal and dual points correspond through simultaneous tightness of the Fenchel relation \(f(u)+f^*(y)=\langle y,u\rangle\) and the dual perspective constraint \(f^*(y)+\mu\le0\). In particular, every positive-activity perspective subgradient lies on the boundary \(f^*(y)+\mu=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At positive activity, perspective subgradients correspond exactly to base-function subgradients, with the activity multiplier equal to minus the conjugate value.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Correspondence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The positive-activity subgradient correspondence is correctly quantified and has the correct multiplier sign, but no inspectable source supports it.

children.title: Scalar Perspective Families

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fenchel Dual Representation of the Closed Perspective
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conjugate and support-function characterization of a scalar closed perspective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper, closed, and convex, and let \(p_f\) be its closed perspective. For \(t\ge0\), \[p_f(x,t)=\sup_{u\in\operatorname{dom}f^*}\bigl(u^{\mathsf T}x-tf^*(u)\bigr).\] Equivalently, with \(C=\{(u,v):f^*(u)+v\le0\}\), \[p_f=\sigma_C,\qquad p_f^*=\delta_C.\] In particular, \(p_f(x,0)=\sigma_{\operatorname{dom}f^*}(x)=f^\infty(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The closed scalar perspective is a support function, and its conjugate is the indicator of the corresponding conjugate hypograph.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p_f=\sigma_C\quad\text{and}\quad p_f^*=\delta_C.
knowledge_statements.title: Fenchel Dual Representation of the Closed Perspective

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is proper and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x,t)\mapsto t f(x/t)\) is convex on \(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R_{++}\); its lower-semicontinuous extension is closed convex when \(f\) is closed.
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional scalar-valued convex functions with an extended-real closure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define \(P_f(x,t)=t f(x/t)\) for \(t>0\). Then \(P_f\) is convex on \(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R_{++}\) and is positively homogeneous: \(P_f(\lambda x,\lambda t)=\lambda P_f(x,t)\) for every \(\lambda>0\). If \(f\) is also closed, the extension
\[p_f(x,t)=\begin{cases}t f(x/t),&t>0,\\f^\infty(x),&t=0,\\+\infty,&t<0\end{cases}\]
is proper, closed, convex, and positively homogeneous.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scaling a convex function by a positive activity variable preserves convexity; recession values provide the closed extension at zero activity.
knowledge_statements.title: Scalar Perspective Families

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scalar perspective convexity and closed recession extension are correct finite-dimensional principles and fit the topic, but the record has no source.

children.title: Set Perspective Constructions
children.top_down_role: Perspective scaling of convex-set representations.

assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C^{\mathrm p}=\{(x,t):t>0,\ x/t\in C\}\cup\{(d,0):d\in\operatorname{rec}C\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed homogenization of a nonempty closed convex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The closed set perspective of \(C\) is
\[C^{\mathrm p}:=\operatorname{cl}\{(t u,t):u\in C,\ t>0\}.\]
It admits the slice representation
\[C^{\mathrm p}=\{(x,t):t>0,\ x/t\in C\}\cup\{(d,0):d\in\operatorname{rec}C\}.\]
Moreover, \(C^{\mathrm p}\) is a closed convex cone, its activity-one slice is \(\{(u,1):u\in C\}\), and its zero-activity slice is \(\operatorname{rec}C\times\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A set perspective is its closed homogenization: positive slices are scaled copies of the set, and the zero slice is its recession cone.
knowledge_statements.title: Set Perspective Constructions

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polar of a Set Perspective Cone
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intrinsic dual characterization of a set's closed homogenization cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let \(C^{\mathrm p}=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{cone}(C\times\{1\})\). Under the convention \(D^\circ=\{q:\langle q,d\rangle\le0\ \forall d\in D\}\), \[(C^{\mathrm p})^\circ=\{(z,s):\sigma_C(z)+s\le0\},\qquad \sigma_C(z)=\sup_{u\in C}\langle z,u\rangle.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The polar of a set perspective cone is described exactly by the support function of the original set.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
The nonpositive polar convention is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (C^{\mathrm p})^\circ=\{(z,s):\sigma_C(z)+s\le0\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Polar of a Set Perspective Cone

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Homogenization of an affine conic epigraph lift over finite-dimensional spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X,W,Y\) be finite-dimensional real vector spaces, let \(K\subseteq Y\) be a closed convex cone, let \(A:X\to Y\), \(B:\mathbb R\to Y\), and \(C:W\to Y\) be linear, and let \(d\in Y\). Suppose \(f:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) has the affine conic epigraph lift \(f(x)\le r\) if and only if \(\exists w\in W:\ Ax+Br+Cw+d\in K\). For every \(t>0\), its positive-activity perspective slice has the representation \[t f(x/t)\le r\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \exists v\in W:\ Ax+Br+Cv+td\in K.\] The epigraph of the closed perspective is the closure of the positive-activity lifted projection; exact inclusion of the zero-activity slice requires the projected homogenized lift to be closed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine conic epigraph lift is perspectivized at positive activity by multiplying its constant term by activity and rescaling its auxiliary variable; closure determines exactness at zero activity.
knowledge_statements.title: Conic Perspective Representations

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polyhedral source cone makes the projected homogenized lift polyhedral and closed, hence exact for the closed perspective epigraph.
assumptions_latex: The finite-dimensional homogenized lift \(H\) is as defined in the immutable seed.
\(K\) is a polyhedral convex cone.

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Exactness of Homogenized Perspective Lifts

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A perspective-specific example showing that a closed nonpolyhedral cone does not ensure exactness before closure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) be \(f(x)=0\), represented by \[f(x)\le r\iff\exists w:\ \left(r,\begin{bmatrix}1&x\\x&w\end{bmatrix}\right)\in\mathbb R_+\times\mathbb S_+^2.\] Its projected homogenized lift is \[H=\left\{(x,t,r):t\ge0,\ r\ge0,\ \exists v:\begin{bmatrix}t&x\\x&v\end{bmatrix}\succeq0\right\}=\{(x,t,r):t>0,\ r\ge0\}\cup\{(0,0,r):r\ge0\}.\] Thus \(H\) is not closed, while \[\operatorname{epi}p_f=\operatorname{cl}H=\{(x,t,r):t\ge0,\ r\ge0\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even an exact lift over a closed semidefinite cone can yield a nonclosed homogenized projection that omits all nonzero zero-activity recession points.
assumptions_latex: \(f(x)=0\) on \(\mathbb R\).
The displayed epigraph lift uses \(\mathbb R_+\times\mathbb S_+^2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: H\ne\operatorname{epi}p_f\quad\text{and}\quad\operatorname{epi}p_f=\operatorname{cl}H.

assumptions_latex: \(X,W,Y\) are finite-dimensional real vector spaces, \(K\subseteq Y\) is a closed convex cone, \(A:X\to Y\), \(B:\mathbb R\to Y\), and \(C:W\to Y\) are linear, and \(d\in Y\).
\(f:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) has the epigraph lift \(f(x)\le r\iff\exists w\in W:\ Ax+Br+Cw+d\in K\), and \(H=\{(x,t,r):t\ge0,\ \exists v\in W,\ Ax+Br+Cv+td\in K\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{epi}p_f=\operatorname{cl}H\), and \(H=\operatorname{epi}p_f\) if and only if \(H\) is closed.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exactness boundary for projected homogenized conic lifts over finite-dimensional spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X,W,Y\) be finite-dimensional real vector spaces, let \(K\subseteq Y\) be a closed convex cone, and let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) have the epigraph lift \(f(x)\le r\) if and only if \(\exists w\in W:\ Ax+Br+Cw+d\in K\), where \(A:X\to Y\), \(B:\mathbb R\to Y\), and \(C:W\to Y\) are linear and \(d\in Y\). Define \[H:=\{(x,t,r)\in X\times\mathbb R\times\mathbb R:t\ge0,\ \exists v\in W,\ Ax+Br+Cv+td\in K\}.\] For the closed perspective \(p_f\), \(\operatorname{epi}p_f=\operatorname{cl}H\). Hence the homogenized lift represents \(\operatorname{epi}p_f\) exactly if and only if \(H\) is closed. Closedness of \(K\) alone does not imply closedness of \(H\), and nonclosedness can omit zero-activity recession points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The projected homogenized conic lift is dense in the closed perspective epigraph and is exact precisely when that projection is closed; a closed underlying cone does not by itself ensure this.
knowledge_statements.title: Perspective Representability Boundaries

\(A,B\in\mathbb H^m\), \(B\succ0\), and the spectrum of \(B^{-1/2}AB^{-1/2}\) is contained in \(I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal P_f(A,B)=B^{1/2}f(B^{-1/2}AB^{-1/2})B^{1/2}\) is jointly matrix convex on its admissible domain.

notation.meaning: Real vector space of m-by-m Hermitian matrices

review_flags: operator-convex perspective theorem locator requires confirmation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional noncommutative perspective on positive-definite activity matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\subseteq\mathbb R\) be an interval, let \(f:I\to\mathbb R\) be operator convex, and let \(A,B\in\mathbb H^m\) satisfy \(B\succ0\) and \(\operatorname{spec}(B^{-1/2}AB^{-1/2})\subseteq I\). Define the matrix perspective by \[\mathcal P_f(A,B):=B^{1/2}f\!\left(B^{-1/2}AB^{-1/2}\right)B^{1/2}.\] For admissible pairs \((A_1,B_1)\), \((A_2,B_2)\) and every \(\theta\in[0,1]\), \[\mathcal P_f(\theta A_1+(1-\theta)A_2,\theta B_1+(1-\theta)B_2)\preceq\theta\mathcal P_f(A_1,B_1)+(1-\theta)\mathcal P_f(A_2,B_2).\] For commuting, simultaneously diagonalizable \(A\) and \(B\), the construction acts entrywise as the scalar perspective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an operator-convex function, the matrix perspective on Hermitian matrices with a positive-definite activity matrix is jointly convex in the Löwner order.
knowledge_statements.title: Matrix Perspective Interface

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Converse boundary for joint convexity of the matrix perspective at all matrix sizes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\mathcal P_f(A,B)\) is jointly matrix convex for all admissible positive-definite \(B\) at every relevant matrix size, then \(f\) is operator convex on its spectral interval. Consequently, scalar convexity alone is insufficient for joint matrix convexity of \(\mathcal P_f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Joint matrix convexity of the perspective requires operator convexity, not merely scalar convexity.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal P_f\) is jointly matrix convex at every relevant matrix size.
The spectra of the tested Hermitian matrices lie in the domain interval of \(f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal P_f\text{ jointly matrix convex}\Longrightarrow f\text{ operator convex}.
knowledge_statements.title: Operator-Convexity Necessity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Singular Activity Requires a Closed Extension
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Domain boundary of the positive-definite matrix-perspective formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The formula \(B^{1/2}f(B^{-1/2}AB^{-1/2})B^{1/2}\) is defined directly only for \(B\succ0\). At a singular activity matrix \(B\succeq0\), a matrix perspective must be interpreted through an explicitly specified lower-semicontinuous closure or limiting extension. Its finiteness can depend on \(f\) and on compatibility of \(A\) with the support and kernel of \(B\); direct substitution of a generalized inverse is not valid without those qualifications.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive-definite activity is essential to the displayed formula; singular activity needs a function-dependent closed extension and support compatibility.
assumptions_latex: \(B\succeq0\) may be singular.
No singular extension of \(\mathcal P_f\) has been specified separately.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: B\not\succ0\Longrightarrow B^{-1/2}\text{ is unavailable and the positive-definite formula alone does not define }\mathcal P_f(A,B).
knowledge_statements.title: Singular Activity Requires a Closed Extension

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural invariances of the finite-dimensional noncommutative perspective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every invertible \(C\) and admissible Hermitian pair \((A,B)\) with \(B\succ0\), \[\mathcal P_f(C^*AC,C^*BC)=C^*\mathcal P_f(A,B)C.\] For admissible pairs \((A_i,B_i)\), \[\mathcal P_f(A_1\oplus A_2,B_1\oplus B_2)=\mathcal P_f(A_1,B_1)\oplus\mathcal P_f(A_2,B_2).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matrix perspectives commute with invertible congruences and block direct sums.
assumptions_latex: Functional calculus for \(f\) is defined on the relevant spectral interval.
\(C\) is invertible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal P_f\text{ is congruence covariant and direct-sum preserving}.
knowledge_statements.title: Congruence and Direct-Sum Compatibility

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Matrix Fractional Perspective and Schur-Complement Epigraph
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix perspective of inversion and its semidefinite epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(t)=t^{-1}\) on \((0,\infty)\), the matrix perspective satisfies \[\mathcal P_f(A,B)=BA^{-1}B\qquad(A\succ0,\ B\succ0).\] More generally, for compatible Hermitian \(B,T\) and \(A\succ0\), \[T\succeq BA^{-1}B\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\begin{bmatrix}A&B\\B&T\end{bmatrix}\succeq0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The perspective of inversion is the matrix-fractional map, whose Löwner epigraph is a block positive-semidefinite constraint.
assumptions_latex: \(A\succ0\).
\(B\) and \(T\) are Hermitian and dimension-compatible.
For interpretation as the original matrix perspective, \(B\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T\succeq BA^{-1}B\iff\begin{bmatrix}A&B\\B&T\end{bmatrix}\succeq0.
knowledge_statements.title: Matrix Fractional Perspective and Schur-Complement Epigraph

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}S=\{(x,z,r):0\le z\le1,\ r\ge p_g(x,z)\}\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed convex hull of one binary-controlled convex epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[S=\{(0,0,r):r\ge0\}\cup\{(x,1,r):r\ge g(x)\}.\]
Then its closed convex hull is
\[\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}S=\{(x,z,r):0\le z\le1,\ r\ge p_g(x,z)\},\]
where \(p_g(x,z)=z g(x/z)\) for \(z>0\) and \(p_g(x,0)=g^\infty(x)\). If the active domain of \(g\) is bounded, then \(g^\infty(x)=+\infty\) for every \(x\ne0\), so the zero-activity slice forces \(x=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The closed hull of an off point and an active convex epigraph is described by the closed perspective inequality with relaxed activity.
knowledge_statements.title: Single-Indicator Convex-Cost Hulls
