assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex with \(0\in C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(\{(0,0)\}\cup(C\times\{1\}))=\{(x,z):0\le z\le1,\ (x,z)\in C^{\mathrm p}\}\).
review_flags: specialized indicator-hull source required for promotion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One binary indicator controlling membership in a closed convex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define \(S_C=\{(0,0)\}\cup\{(x,1):x\in C\}\). Then
\[\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}S_C=\{(x,z):0\le z\le1,\ (x,z)\in C^{\mathrm p}\}.\]
For \(0<z\le1\), this is equivalent to \(x\in zC\). At \(z=0\), closed-hull points satisfy \(x\in\operatorname{rec}C\). In particular, when \(C\) is bounded, \(\operatorname{rec}C=\{0\}\), and the formulation reduces to \(0\le z\le1\), \(x\in zC\), with \(x=0\) at zero activity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relaxing a binary-controlled convex set yields scaled copies of the active set; closure adds its recession directions at zero activity.
knowledge_statements.title: Indicator-Controlled Convex Sets

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Support-Inequality Representation for Compact Active Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent half-space and polyhedral forms of a bounded indicator-controlled convex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, compact, and convex with \(0\in C\), and let \(\sigma_C(a)=\sup_{y\in C}a^{\mathsf T}y\). For \(z\ge0\), \[x\in zC\iff a^{\mathsf T}x\le z\sigma_C(a)\quad\text{for every }a\in\mathbb R^n.\] Hence the indicator hull is \[0\le z\le1,\qquad a^{\mathsf T}x\le z\sigma_C(a)\quad(\forall a).\] If \(C=\{x:Ax\le b\}\) is a bounded polyhedron with \(0\in C\), this specializes to \(0\le z\le1\) and \(Ax\le bz\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A compact active set can be scaled through all its support inequalities; for a bounded polyhedral active set, every right-hand side is scaled by the activity.
assumptions_latex: C\text{ is nonempty, compact, and convex.}
0\in C
z\ge0
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x\in zC\iff \forall a,\ a^{\mathsf T}x\le z\sigma_C(a).

knowledge_statements.title: Bounded Active Ranges
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact hull of a scalar variable that is zero when inactive and interval-bounded when active.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\ell<u\) and \(D=\{(0,0)\}\cup\{(x,1):\ell\le x\le u\}\). Its convex hull is
\[
\operatorname{conv}(D)=\{(x,z)\in\mathbb R\times[0,1]:\ell z\le x\le uz\}.
\]
Consequently, imposing binary \(z\) recovers the original on/off domain, while relaxing \(z\) to \([0,1]\) gives its exact continuous convex hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A variable active on an interval and otherwise zero has the exact relaxation lz ≤ x ≤ uz with 0 ≤ z ≤ 1.

knowledge_statements.title: Shared-Indicator Activation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact activation hull when one indicator jointly switches an entire vector domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, compact, and convex. For
\[
D=\{(0,0)\}\cup\{(x,1):x\in C\},
\]
the shared-indicator convex hull is
\[
\operatorname{conv}(D)=\{(x,z):0\le z\le1,\ x\in zC\},
\]
where \(0C=\{0\}\). Hence a fractional indicator scales the entire vector set by one common factor; it does not independently scale its coordinates or component constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One common indicator scales the whole active vector set: at fractional z, the feasible vector belongs to zC, and at z = 0 it is zero.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, compact, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{conv}(D)=\{(x,z):0\le z\le1,\ x\in zC\}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Nonseparable Convex Costs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Perspective hull for a vector cost governed jointly by one activation indicator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, compact, and convex, and let \(f:C\to\mathbb R\) be closed and convex. For the union of the inactive epigraph \(\{(0,0,t):t\ge0\}\) and active epigraph \(\{(x,1,t):x\in C,\ t\ge f(x)\}\), the closed convex hull is
\[
0\le z\le1,\qquad x\in zC,\qquad t\ge zf(x/z)\quad(z>0),
\]
with the boundary convention \(x=0\) and \(t\ge0\) at \(z=0\). The perspective is applied to \(f\) jointly, including all cross-coordinate coupling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The exact hull applies one vector perspective to the entire nonseparable cost; separate coordinate perspectives generally do not preserve cross-coordinate coupling.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, compact, and convex.
\(f:C\to\mathbb R\) is closed and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The hull epigraph is \(\{(x,z,t):0\le z\le1,\ x\in zC,\ t\ge zf(x/z)\}\) with its stated closure at \(z=0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Coupling-Induced Hull Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete gap caused by omitting shared-indicator scaling from a coupled quadratic cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Take \(C=[0,1]^2\), \(f(x)=(x_1-x_2)^2\), and one shared indicator \(z\). The exact perspective epigraph for \(z>0\) requires
\[
t\ge \frac{(x_1-x_2)^2}{z},\qquad 0\le x_i\le z.
\]
The convex but unscaled relaxation \(t\ge(x_1-x_2)^2\) is strictly weaker. At \(z=1/2\), \(x=(1/2,0)\), it permits \(t=1/4\), whereas the exact shared-indicator hull requires \(t\ge1/2\). Thus preserving convexity alone does not close the coupling-induced hull gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a coupled quadratic, omitting the shared perspective admits a fractional point with cost 1/4 although the exact hull requires cost 1/2.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The relaxation \(t\ge(x_1-x_2)^2\) strictly contains the shared-indicator perspective epigraph.

children.title: Direct Nonlinear Perspective Formulations

knowledge_statements.title: Direct Nonlinear Perspective Formulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Native closed nonlinear formulation of a convex perspective epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a proper closed convex function \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), define its closed perspective by
\[
f^\pi(x,z)=
\begin{cases}
zf(x/z),&z>0,\\
f^\infty(x),&z=0,\\
+\infty,&z<0,
\end{cases}
\]
where \(f^\infty\) is the recession function. A direct nonlinear perspective formulation retains the native convex constraint \(t\ge f^\pi(x,z)\), together with \(0\le z\le1\). If \(z\) is binary, its active slice is the epigraph of \(f\), while its zero slice is governed by recession behavior.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A direct formulation keeps the closed perspective inequality as a native convex constraint, including its recession-defined boundary at zero activation.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{epi}(f^\pi)=\{(x,z,t):t\ge f^\pi(x,z)\}\) is a closed convex perspective epigraph.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard closed-perspective construction from convex analysis
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The recession-function boundary is the standard closed perspective construction, and the representation matches the direct nonlinear formulation container. An authoritative convex-analysis source with a specific definition or section locator is absent.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Behavior of degree-one norm terms under scalar perspective scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every norm \(\|\cdot\|\) and \(z>0\), \[z\|x/z\|=\|x\|.\] Its closed perspective therefore remains \(\|x\|\) at \(z=0\) and supplies no coupling between \(x\) and \(z\). For the Euclidean norm its epigraph is SOC-representable, but forcing \(x=0\) at inactivity requires a separate activation-domain constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A degree-one norm is unchanged by perspective scaling, so its perspective alone does not impose on/off activation.
assumptions_latex: \(\|\cdot\|\) is a norm.
\(z\ge0\) for the closed perspective.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: SOC representation of a shifted affine quadratic perspective.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The perspective of a squared affine residual is one SOC constraint after homogenizing its offset.
assumptions_latex: \(z\ge0\) and \(t\ge0\).
\(A\) and \(b\) are fixed.

SOC Perspective Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rotated second-order-cone representation of a convex quadratic perspective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Q\succeq0\) and choose \(L\) with \(Q=L^{\mathsf T}L\). For \(z\ge0\) and \(t\ge0\), the quadratic perspective inequality
\[
x^{\mathsf T}Qx\le tz
\]
is equivalent to the second-order-cone constraint
\[
\left\|(2Lx,\ t-z)\right\|_2\le t+z.
\]
For \(z>0\), this is \(t\ge x^{\mathsf T}Qx/z\); at \(z=0\), it enforces \(Lx=0\), and it enforces \(x=0\) when \(Q\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic perspective is exactly representable by one rotated second-order cone after factoring its positive-semidefinite quadratic form.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\) and \(Q=L^{\mathsf T}L\).
\(z\ge0\) and \(t\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^{\mathsf T}Qx\le tz\iff\|(2Lx,t-z)\|_2\le t+z\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Explicit Zero-Scale Face of the Exponential Cone
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closure behavior of exponential perspectives at zero activation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K_{\exp}=\operatorname{cl}\{(u,v,w):v>0,\ v\exp(u/v)\le w\}\), \[K_{\exp}\cap\{v=0\}=\{(u,0,w):u\le0,\ w\ge0\}.\] Hence \((x,0,t)\in K_{\exp}\) enforces \(x\le0\) and \(t\ge0\), not necessarily \(x=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At zero scale, the exponential cone permits a nonpositive exponential coordinate and nonnegative epigraph coordinate.
assumptions_latex: \(K_{\exp}\) is the closed exponential cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x,0,t)\in K_{\exp}\iff x\le0\text{ and }t\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Explicit Zero-Scale Face of the Exponential Cone

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exponential-cone representation of scaled logarithmic structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(z>0\) and \(x>0\), \[t\le z\log(x/z)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad(t,z,x)\in K_{\exp}.\] The closed cone supplies the closed hypograph at zero-coordinate boundary points.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The scalar relative-entropy epigraph is represented by one exponential-cone constraint.
assumptions_latex: \(x\ge0\) and \(z\ge0\).

Exponential-Cone Perspective Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exponential-cone representation of the exponential perspective epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the closed exponential cone by
\[
K_{\exp}=\operatorname{cl}\{(u,v,w)\in\mathbb R^3:v>0,\ v\exp(u/v)\le w\}.
\]
Then the closed perspective epigraph of \(f(u)=\exp(u)\) is represented exactly by
\[
t\ge z\exp(x/z)\quad(z>0),
\qquad\text{with closure at }z=0,
\]
if and only if \((x,z,t)\in K_{\exp}\). Thus the activation variable occupies the scaling coordinate of the cone rather than appearing through division in the conic model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The exponential perspective is represented exactly by placing the argument, activation variable, and epigraph variable in the closed exponential cone.
assumptions_latex: \(x,z,t\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x,z,t)\in K_{\exp}\iff t\ge z\exp(x/z)\) for \(z>0\), together with the closed boundary at \(z=0\).

children.title: Power-Cone Perspective Reformulations
children.top_down_role: Perspective representations for power-law or geometric-mean structure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Power-cone representation of a two-factor weighted geometric mean.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(0<\alpha<1\). For \(u,v,w\ge0\), \[w\le u^\alpha v^{1-\alpha}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad(u,v,w)\in K_{\mathrm{pow}}^\alpha.\] For \(v>0\), this is \(w\le v(u/v)^\alpha\); closure forces \(w=0\) when either positively weighted factor is zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weighted geometric-mean or concave-power perspective hypograph is one power-cone membership.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: w\le u^\alpha v^{1-\alpha}\iff(u,v,w)\in K_{\mathrm{pow}}^\alpha.
knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Geometric-Mean Perspective Hypograph
Power-Cone Perspective Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Power-cone representation of the perspective of an absolute power.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(p>1\), set \(\alpha=1/p\) and define
\[
K_{\mathrm{pow}}^\alpha=\{(u,v,w):u\ge0,\ v\ge0,\ u^\alpha v^{1-\alpha}\ge|w|\}.
\]
For \(z\ge0\) and \(t\ge0\), membership
\[
(t,z,x)\in K_{\mathrm{pow}}^{1/p}
\]
is equivalent to \(|x|^p\le tz^{p-1}\). For \(z>0\), this becomes the perspective epigraph inequality \(t\ge z|x/z|^p\); its conic closure enforces \(x=0\) when \(z=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The perspective of |x| raised to p is exactly one power-cone constraint with exponent 1/p.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((t,z,x)\in K_{\mathrm{pow}}^{1/p}\iff |x|^p\le tz^{p-1}\).

children.title: Cone-Specific Representability Limits
children.top_down_role: Structural limits arising when a perspective lacks the selected cone representation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Irrational Power Cones Have No Finite Semialgebraic Cone Lift
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representability obstruction for power cones with irrational exponent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(0<\alpha<1\) be irrational. The three-dimensional power cone \[K_{\mathrm{pow}}^\alpha=\{(u,v,w):u\ge0,\ v\ge0,\ u^\alpha v^{1-\alpha}\ge |w|\}\] is not semialgebraic. Since projections of finite affine slices of products of second-order or positive-semidefinite cones are semialgebraic, \(K_{\mathrm{pow}}^\alpha\) has no exact finite SOC or SDP extended formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An irrational-exponent power cone cannot have an exact finite SOC or SDP lift because it is not semialgebraic.
assumptions_latex: \(0<\alpha<1\) is irrational.
Only finite-dimensional affine lifts and projections are permitted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K_{\mathrm{pow}}^\alpha\text{ has no exact finite SOC or SDP lift}.

notation.meaning: Three-dimensional power cone with exponent alpha.

knowledge_statements.title: Irrational Power Cones Have No Finite Semialgebraic Cone Lift
Cone-Specific Representability Limits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sharp obstruction to replacing exponential perspectives by finite SOC lifts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Finite-dimensional sets obtained as projections of affine slices of finite products of second-order cones are semialgebraic. The epigraph
\[
E=\{(x,z,t):z>0,\ t\ge z\exp(x/z)\}
\]
has a boundary containing the transcendental graph \(t=z\exp(x/z)\) and is not semialgebraic. Consequently, its closure has no exact finite second-order-cone extended formulation, although it has the single exponential-cone representation \((x,z,t)\in K_{\exp}\). Convexity of a perspective therefore does not imply representability by an arbitrarily chosen cone family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exponential perspectives are convex but not finitely SOC-representable; exact conic representability depends on the chosen cone family.
assumptions_latex: Extended formulations use finitely many second-order cones and affine equations.
Representability permits affine lifting and projection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{cl}(E)\) is exponential-cone representable but has no exact finite SOC lift.
review_flags: exact nonrepresentability claim requires an authoritative semialgebraic-geometry source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Failure boundary is the correct content kind, and the semialgebraicity argument is plausible, but the exact claim that the closed exponential-perspective epigraph admits no finite SOC lift is nontrivial. It requires authoritative sources specifically supporting semialgebraicity of finite SOC projections and nonsemialgebraicity of this epigraph; the generic local inventory entries do not provide that evidence.

children.title: Polyhedral Perspective Outer Approximations
children.top_down_role: Linear outer approximations and extended polyhedral representations of perspective epigraphs.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary-safe cutting-plane construction for a perspective epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain a finite set \(Y\subset\operatorname{dom}f^*\) and impose \(t\ge\langle y,x\rangle-zf^*(y)\) for every \(y\in Y\). After solving the relaxation, call a perspective-separation oracle at \((\bar x,\bar z,\bar t)\). If it returns \(y\in\operatorname{dom}f^*\) with \(\langle y,\bar x\rangle-\bar zf^*(y)>\bar t+\varepsilon\), add that cut and repeat. Stop when the oracle certifies \(\sup_y\{\langle y,\bar x\rangle-\bar zf^*(y)\}\le\bar t+\varepsilon\). The same procedure applies at \(\bar z=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Generate violated Fenchel cuts until an oracle certifies perspective-epigraph feasibility to tolerance, including at zero activity.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, closed, and convex.
An oracle can find a violated Fenchel cut or certify the conjugate supremum within \(\varepsilon\).
\(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bar t\ge f^\pi(\bar x,\bar z)-\varepsilon\text{ at termination}.

notation.meaning: Current finite set of conjugate cut parameters.

knowledge_statements.title: Fenchel-Cut Separation Algorithm

knowledge_statements.statement_title: No Finite Exact Linearization for Nonpolyhedral Epigraphs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between exact finite polyhedral perspectives and genuine outer approximations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A projection of a finite linear system is polyhedral. Therefore, if \(\operatorname{epi}(f^\pi)\) is nonpolyhedral, it has no exact finite LP extended formulation. In particular, \(\{(x,z,t):z\ge0,\ x^2\le tz\}\) is nonpolyhedral, so no finite family of its supporting perspective cuts is exact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonpolyhedral perspective epigraphs cannot be represented exactly by finitely many linear cuts or a finite LP lift.
assumptions_latex: Only finitely many continuous auxiliary variables and linear constraints are permitted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{epi}(f^\pi)\text{ nonpolyhedral}\Rightarrow\text{no exact finite LP extended formulation}.
knowledge_statements.title: No Finite Exact Linearization for Nonpolyhedral Epigraphs

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform Convergence Away from Zero Activity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convergence of dense tangent approximations on compact positive-activity regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\Subset\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f)\), with \(f\in C^1\) on a neighborhood of \(K\). If finite sets \(A_k\subset K\) have fill distance tending to zero and \[\widehat f_k(u)=\max_{a\in A_k}\{f(a)+\nabla f(a)^{\mathsf T}(u-a)\},\] then \(\widehat f_k\to f\) uniformly on \(K\). Consequently, for every \(\delta>0\), \(z\widehat f_k(x/z)\to zf(x/z)\) uniformly where \(\delta\le z\le1\) and \(x/z\in K\). If the sets \(A_k\) are nested, the convergence is monotone from below.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dense tangent sets converge uniformly to a smooth convex perspective on compact regions bounded away from zero activity.
assumptions_latex: \(K\Subset\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f)\).
\(f\in C^1\) near \(K\).
The fill distance of \(A_k\) in \(K\) tends to zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sup_{\delta\le z\le1,\,x/z\in K}|zf(x/z)-z\widehat f_k(x/z)|\to0.

notation.meaning: Finite tangent-point set at stage k.

knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Convergence Away from Zero Activity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact infinite linear description underlying perspective outer approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a proper closed convex \(f\), \[f^\pi(x,z)=\sup_{y\in\operatorname{dom}f^*}\{\langle y,x\rangle-zf^*(y)\},\qquad z\ge0.\] Hence \[t\ge f^\pi(x,z)\iff t\ge\langle y,x\rangle-zf^*(y)\quad\forall y\in\operatorname{dom}f^*.\] Every finite subfamily is a valid polyhedral outer approximation, and the formula remains valid at \(z=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A perspective epigraph is the intersection of its linear Fenchel cuts; finite subfamilies give outer approximations.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{epi}(f^\pi)=\bigcap_{y\in\operatorname{dom}f^*}\{(x,z,t):t\ge\langle y,x\rangle-zf^*(y)\}.

notation.meaning: Fenchel conjugate of the base function.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Exactness for Polyhedral Base Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite perspective formulation when the base function is finite max-affine.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(f(x)=\max_{1\le k\le m}\{a_k^{\mathsf T}x+b_k\}\), then for \(z\ge0\), \[t\ge f^\pi(x,z)\iff t\ge a_k^{\mathsf T}x+b_kz\quad(k=1,\ldots,m).\] Thus the closed perspective epigraph has an exact finite polyhedral representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite max-affine function yields an exact finite family of perspective cuts.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is finite and max-affine with finitely many pieces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: t\ge f^\pi(x,z)\iff t\ge a_k^{\mathsf T}x+b_kz\ \forall k.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Exactness for Polyhedral Base Functions
Polyhedral Perspective Outer Approximations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cutting-plane construction of finite linear outer approximations to a perspective epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input a proper closed convex \(f\), a finite set \(A\subset\operatorname{dom}f\), and tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\). Initialize the relaxation with \(0\le z\le1\) and, for each \(a\in A\) and \(s_a\in\partial f(a)\), add
\[
t\ge s_a^{\mathsf T}x+\bigl(f(a)-s_a^{\mathsf T}a\bigr)z.
\]
After solving, if \(z>0\), set \(a=x/z\), obtain \(s_a\in\partial f(a)\), and add the displayed cut when its violation exceeds \(\varepsilon\). Stop when no such violation remains; output the current polyhedral outer approximation and incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Build a linear outer approximation from perspective supporting cuts, repeatedly separating the current fractional solution until no cut exceeds the tolerance.

knowledge_statements.title: Auxiliary-Variable Perspective Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extended perspective formulation for a convex function composed with an affine map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be closed and convex, and define \(f(x)=h(Ax+b)\). Introduce \(y=Ax+bz\). The closed perspective epigraph is represented by \[y=Ax+bz,\qquad t\ge z h(y/z)\quad(z>0),\] with its lower-semicontinuous closure at \(z=0\). For any \(a\in\operatorname{dom}h\) and \(g\in\partial h(a)\), the auxiliary-variable inequality \[t\ge h(a)z+g^{\mathsf T}(y-az)\] is valid. Substituting \(y=Ax+bz\) yields a valid perspective cut in the original variables.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closure Boundary for Multi-Indicator Perspective Lifts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closure qualification for the projection of a disaggregated finite-union perspective lift.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U=\bigcup_{i=1}^k\{(x,t,z):z=e_i,\ t\ge f_i(x)\}\), and let \(L\) impose \(z\ge0\), \(\sum_i z_i=1\), \(x=\sum_i x_i\), and \(t\ge\sum_i f_i^\pi(x_i,z_i)\). Then \[\operatorname{cl}\bigl(\operatorname{proj}_{x,t,z}L\bigr)=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}U.\] Equality without the outer closure requires \(\operatorname{proj}_{x,t,z}L\) to be closed; closedness of the individual perspective epigraphs alone does not ensure closedness of their linear image.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The disaggregated lift recovers the closed convex hull after closure; omitting closure requires the projected lift itself to be closed.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i\) is proper, closed, and convex.
The alternatives use unit-vector, exactly-one indicators.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{proj}L=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}U\quad\text{only when the projected lift is closed}.
knowledge_statements.title: Closure Boundary for Multi-Indicator Perspective Lifts

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Disaggregated perspective formulation for a finite union selected by multiple indicators.

children.title: Dynamic Perspective Separation
children.top_down_role: Iterative solver interfaces for detecting and separating violated perspective structure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact separation of a closed scalar perspective at zero activity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p_f\) be the closed perspective of a proper closed convex function \(f\). At \((\bar x,0,\bar t)\), search for \(s\in\operatorname{dom}f^*\) satisfying \(s^{\mathsf T}\bar x>\bar t+\varepsilon\). If found, add \[t\ge s^{\mathsf T}x-f^*(s)z.\] If an exact oracle certifies that no such \(s\) exists, then \(p_f(\bar x,0)=f^\infty(\bar x)\le \bar t+\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zero-activity separation maximizes a linear functional over the conjugate domain; a sufficiently large value supplies a violated perspective cut.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, closed, and convex.
An exact conjugate-domain separation oracle is available.
\(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sup_{s\in\operatorname{dom}f^*}s^{\mathsf T}\bar x\le\bar t+\varepsilon\quad\text{or a violated valid cut is returned}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Termination for a Finite Perspective-Cut Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cut-addition bound when the candidate perspective family is finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the target relaxation is described by a finite family \(\mathcal C\) of \(M\) distinct perspective cuts. If each nonterminal iteration adds a previously absent member of \(\mathcal C\), then at most \(M\) cut-addition iterations occur. With exact reoptimization and separation, the terminal solution satisfies every member of \(\mathcal C\) within tolerance \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite perspective-cut family permits at most one addition per distinct cut.
assumptions_latex: \(|\mathcal C|=M<\infty\).
Each nonterminal iteration adds a previously absent cut.
Reoptimization and separation are exact relative to \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{add}}\le M.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Termination for a Finite Perspective-Cut Family

knowledge_statements.statement_title: No General Finite-Termination Guarantee for Infinite Support Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limitation of dynamic separation over nonpolyhedral perspective epigraphs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: When the relevant perspective-support family is infinite, validity of every generated cut does not imply finite termination or a uniform iteration bound. Moreover, failure to find a violation is a global \(\varepsilon\)-feasibility certificate only when the separation oracle optimizes over the entire applicable support family to the required accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An infinite support family can require indefinitely many distinct cuts, and an incomplete oracle provides only a family-relative stopping test.
assumptions_latex: The perspective epigraph need not be polyhedral.
The generated cuts may range over infinitely many supports.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |\mathcal C|=\infty\;\not\Longrightarrow\;N_{\mathrm{add}}<\infty.
knowledge_statements.title: No General Finite-Termination Guarantee for Infinite Support Families
Dynamic Perspective Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cutting-plane separation for differentiable or subdifferentiable closed perspectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a relaxation containing \(0\le z\le1\), an epigraph variable \(t\), and activation linkage, together with a proper closed convex function \(f\). Initialize with no perspective support cuts. At an incumbent \((\bar x,\bar z,\bar t)\) with \(\bar z>0\), set \(a=\bar x/\bar z\), choose \(g\in\partial f(a)\), and test \[\bar t\ge f(a)\bar z+g^{\mathsf T}(\bar x-a\bar z).\] If violated beyond tolerance \(\varepsilon\), add \(t\ge f(a)z+g^{\mathsf T}(x-az)\) and reoptimize. Stop when no tested perspective cut is violated by more than \(\varepsilon\); return the current relaxation solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly linearize the perspective at the incumbent ratio, add any violated supporting cut, and stop when violations fall within tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, closed, and convex with an available subgradient oracle.
Activation linkage handles incumbents with \(\bar z=0\).
\(\varepsilon\ge0\) is the separation tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every generated inequality is valid, and termination yields no detected violation exceeding \(\varepsilon\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Validity and Strength Depend on a Valid Tight Capacity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Big-M validity and relaxation-strength boundary for capacity coupling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le Uz\), \(U\) must upper-bound \(a^{\mathsf T}x\) throughout the active feasible region. If \(U\) is smaller than the true active maximum, feasible active points are removed. If \(U\) is valid but unnecessarily large, the binary feasible set is unchanged while the relaxation \(0\le z\le1\) is weaker; replacing it by a smaller valid bound strengthens the relaxation.

\(z\in\{0,1\}\) in the discrete model.

Capacity-Coupled Activation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear activation linkage coupling usable capacity to an on/off decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z_i\in\{0,1\}\) activate resource \(i\), let \(x_{ij}\ge0\) denote quantities using that resource, and let \(U_i>0\) be its capacity. Capacity-coupled activation is the condition \[\sum_j a_{ij}x_{ij}\le U_i z_i,\qquad a_{ij}\ge0.\] Consequently, \(z_i=0\) implies \(a_{ij}x_{ij}=0\) for every \(j\); if all \(a_{ij}>0\), then \(x_{ij}=0\) for every \(j\). Under relaxation to \(0\le z_i\le1\), the same inequality scales available capacity proportionally with activity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A resource can carry flow only when activated, and its usable capacity scales with the relaxed activation variable.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_j a_{ij}x_{ij}\le U_i z_i\) enforces zero weighted use at inactivity and bounded use at activity.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Per-Period Hulls Do Not Imply the Intertemporal Hull
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of isolated periodwise perspective convexification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S_t\) denote each period's binary commitment-production-cost set, and let \(H\) be a convex set of intertemporal constraints. Then \[\operatorname{conv}\left((S_1\times\cdots\times S_T)\cap H\right)\subseteq\left(\operatorname{conv}S_1\times\cdots\times\operatorname{conv}S_T\right)\cap H,\] and the inclusion can be strict. Consequently, exact perspective hulls for individual periods remain valid but need not describe the convex hull after ramping, startup, shutdown, or minimum-up/down coupling is imposed.

Let n\in\mathbb{N}. In period k, suppose a_k^{(i)}>0 and b_k^{(i)}\ge 0 for i=1,\ldots,n. For x\in Q:=\mathbb{R}_+^n, define

\[
\widehat P:=\Delta_n:=\left\{x\in\mathbb{R}_+^n:\sum_{i=1}^n x^{(i)}=1\right\}.
\]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Projection of Bounded Selection Linkage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between bounded cardinality sparsity and the existence of binary selection indicators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\ell_i\le0\le u_i\) be finite and \(k\in\{0,\ldots,n\}\). Then \[\left\{x:\ell_i\le x_i\le u_i,\ \|x\|_0\le k\right\}=\operatorname{proj}_x\left\{(x,z):z\in\{0,1\}^n,\ \ell_i z_i\le x_i\le u_i z_i,\ \sum_i z_i\le k\right\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under finite valid bounds, projecting the binary linkage formulation gives exactly the vectors with at most k nonzero components.
assumptions_latex: \ell_i\le0\le u_i\text{ are finite for every }i.
k\in\{0,\ldots,n\}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{proj}_x\{(x,z):z\in\{0,1\}^n,\ \ell_i z_i\le x_i\le u_i z_i,\ \mathbf1^{\mathsf T}z\le k\}=\{x\in[\ell,u]:\|x\|_0\le k\}.

notation.meaning: number of nonzero components of x

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cardinality-constrained selection with indicator-linked continuous coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) be continuous coefficients and \(z\in\{0,1\}^n\) selection indicators. A cardinality-limited sparse model imposes \[\ell_i z_i\le x_i\le u_i z_i\quad(i=1,\ldots,n),\qquad \sum_{i=1}^n z_i\le k,\] where \(\ell_i\le0\le u_i\). These constraints ensure \(x_i=0\) whenever \(z_i=0\) and permit at most \(k\) nonzero coefficients. If a separable convex cost \(f_i(x_i)\) is present, its activated epigraph is strengthened by \(t_i\ge f_i^{\pi}(x_i,z_i)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binary indicators link coefficients to zero and impose a cardinality budget; separable convex costs can be perspective-strengthened.
assumptions_latex: \(\ell_i\le0\le u_i\) are valid coefficient bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The linkage and cardinality constraint imply \(\lVert x\rVert_0\le k\).

children.title: Indicator-Regularization Models
children.top_down_role: Estimation formulations coupling indicators with convex regularization terms.

knowledge_statements.title: Indicator-Regularization Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Perspective reformulation of separable convex regularizers controlled by selection indicators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z_i\in\{0,1\}\) and impose valid linkage forcing \(x_i=0\) when \(z_i=0\). For proper closed convex regularizers \(r_i\) satisfying \(r_i(0)=0\), the activated regularization epigraph \[t_i\ge r_i(x_i),\qquad z_i\in\{0,1\}\] has the perspective-strengthened relaxation \[0\le z_i\le1,\qquad t_i\ge r_i^{\pi}(x_i,z_i).\] In particular, if \(r_i(x_i)=\lambda_i x_i^2\) with \(\lambda_i>0\), its closed perspective epigraph is represented by \[t_i\ge0,\qquad t_i z_i\ge\lambda_i x_i^2,\qquad 0\le z_i\le1.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An indicator-linked convex regularizer is strengthened by its closed perspective; quadratic regularization yields a rotated-conic inequality together with nonnegativity of the epigraph variable.
assumptions_latex: Each \(r_i\) is proper, closed, and convex with \(r_i(0)=0\).
The linkage forces \(x_i=0\) at \(z_i=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(t_i\ge r_i^{\pi}(x_i,z_i)\) gives the isolated on/off regularizer's closed convex hull; for \(r_i(x_i)=\lambda_i x_i^2\), this requires \(t_i\ge0\) and \(t_i z_i\ge\lambda_i x_i^2\).

notation.meaning: closed perspective of the component regularizer

children.title: Risk-Coupled Selection Models
children.top_down_role: Sparse selection formulations containing convex loss or risk coupling.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selecting a diagonal positive-semidefinite component of a quadratic risk matrix for separable perspective strengthening.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Q\succeq0\), define \[\mathcal D(Q)=\{d\in\mathbb R_+^n:Q-\operatorname{Diag}(d)\succeq0\}.\] Given \(w\in\mathbb R_+^n\), an eligible diagonal can be selected by \[\max\{w^{\mathsf T}d:d\in\mathcal D(Q)\}.\] If \(d',d\in\mathcal D(Q)\) and \(d'\ge d\) componentwise, then for \(0<z_i\le1\), the right-hand side generated by \(d'\) dominates that generated by \(d\): \[x^{\mathsf T}(Q-\operatorname{Diag}(d'))x+\sum_i\frac{d'_i x_i^2}{z_i}\ge x^{\mathsf T}(Q-\operatorname{Diag}(d))x+\sum_i\frac{d_i x_i^2}{z_i}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An eligible diagonal risk component can be selected by a semidefinite program, and a componentwise larger eligible diagonal gives a stronger perspective relaxation.
assumptions_latex: Q\succeq0
w\in\mathbb R_+^n
d,d'\in\mathcal D(Q)
0<z_i\le1\quad(i=1,\ldots,n)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d'\ge d\Longrightarrow x^{\mathsf T}(Q-\operatorname{Diag}(d'))x+\sum_i d'_i x_i^2/z_i\ge x^{\mathsf T}(Q-\operatorname{Diag}(d))x+\sum_i d_i x_i^2/z_i.

notation.meaning: eligible nonnegative diagonal extractions preserving a positive-semidefinite residual

knowledge_statements.title: Diagonal Perspective-Strengthening Selection
Risk-Coupled Selection Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sparse selection with a positive-semidefinite quadratic risk term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\succeq0\), let \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), and link each \(x_i\) to an indicator \(z_i\in\{0,1\}\). A risk-coupled selection model may impose \(\sum_{i=1}^n z_i\le k\) and \(t\ge x^{\mathsf T}Qx\). Suppose \(Q=R+D\), where \(R\succeq0\) and \(D=\operatorname{Diag}(d)\succeq0\). Then the valid perspective strengthening is \[t\ge x^{\mathsf T}Rx+\sum_{i=1}^n \phi_i^{\pi}(x_i,z_i),\qquad \phi_i(s)=d_i s^2,\] where, for \(z_i>0\), \(\phi_i^{\pi}(x_i,z_i)=d_i x_i^2/z_i\), and its lower-semicontinuous closure is used at \(z_i=0\). Thus the term is zero at \((x_i,z_i)=(0,0)\); it is infinite when \(z_i=0\), \(x_i\ne0\), and \(d_i>0\); and it is zero for all \(x_i\) when \(d_i=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-semidefinite risk term couples selected variables; each positive diagonal component can be strengthened by its closed scalar perspective, while a zero-weight component contributes zero.
assumptions_latex: \(Q=R+D\), \(R\succeq0\), and \(D=\operatorname{Diag}(d)\succeq0\).
Valid linkage forces \(x_i=0\) whenever \(z_i=0\).
\(0\le z_i\le1\) in the continuous relaxation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(t\ge x^{\mathsf T}Rx+\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_i^{\pi}(x_i,z_i)\) is valid and dominates \(t\ge x^{\mathsf T}Qx\) whenever \(0<z_i\le1\) for every index with \(d_i>0\).

children.title: Missing or Incomplete Activation Linkage

knowledge_statements.title: Missing or Incomplete Activation Linkage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Perspective invalidity when inactivity does not force the continuous variable to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the binary model \[z\in\{0,1\},\qquad x\in\mathbb R,\qquad t\ge x^2,\] with no constraint linking \(x\) to \(z\). The feasible point \((x,z,t)=(1,0,1)\) is allowed. Replacing the quadratic epigraph by the closed perspective condition \(t\ge x^2/z\) would exclude this point because the closed perspective is infinite at \((x,z)=(1,0)\). Hence a perspective reformulation is not valid unless the modeled inactive disjunct actually requires \(x=0\), or an equivalent complete activation linkage enforces that condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without linkage forcing the continuous variable to zero when inactive, a perspective constraint can cut off feasible points and is invalid.
assumptions_latex: The original model permits \(z=0\) with \(x\ne0\).
The proposed reformulation uses the closed perspective of \(x^2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The point \((1,0,1)\) proves that the perspective replacement is invalid without complete activation linkage.

children.title: Nonconvex Active Terms
children.top_down_role: Activated terms requiring additional convexification beyond the convex perspective.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit demonstration that activation scaling does not convexify a nonconvex active epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=[-1,1]\) and \(f(x)=-x^2\). The active epigraph \(E=\{(x,t):x\in D,\ t\ge -x^2\}\) is nonconvex: \((-1,-1)\) and \((1,-1)\) belong to \(E\), but their midpoint \((0,-1)\) does not. Consequently, the positive-activity perspective set \(P=\{(x,z,t):z>0,\ x/z\in D,\ t\ge -x^2/z\}\) is nonconvex because its \(z=1\) slice is \(E\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The concave quadratic active cost has a nonconvex epigraph, and its perspective remains nonconvex because the unit-activity slice reproduces that epigraph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The active epigraph \(E\) and its positive-activity perspective set \(P\) are nonconvex.

notation.meaning: Active epigraph of the nonconvex cost

knowledge_statements.title: Concave Active-Cost Perspective Counterexample

assumptions_latex: The activated feasible set is \(S=\{(x,z,t):z\in\{0,1\},\ x=0\text{ if }z=0,\ x\in D\text{ and }t\ge f(x)\text{ if }z=1\}\).
The active epigraph \(E=\{(x,t):x\in D,\ t\ge f(x)\}\) is nonconvex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The ordinary convex perspective formula cannot by itself describe \(\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(S)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: perspective convexification requires a closed convex active epigraph; exact supporting locator unavailable
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary for applying a convex perspective to an intrinsically nonconvex active term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(z>0\), the expression \(z f(x/z)\) is convex in \((x,z)\) only when the extended-valued function \(f\) is convex. If the active epigraph \(E\) is nonconvex, then the set \(\{(x,z,t):z>0,\ x/z\in D,\ t\ge zf(x/z)\}\) is generally nonconvex and is not a convex-hull formulation of \(S\). A valid convexification must instead use a convexification of the active epigraph, such as \(\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(E)\), before taking its perspective, or introduce a stronger extended formulation. Thus activation linkage alone does not repair nonconvexity already present when \(z=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A perspective does not make a nonconvex active epigraph convex. The active term must first be convexified, possibly through an extended formulation.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Active Terms

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role and mathematical direction are appropriate, but the claim about obtaining the closed convex hull by first convexifying the active epigraph requires an authoritative locator and careful closure/recession conditions.

children.title: Zero-Activity Closure Failures
children.top_down_role: Modeling failures caused by incorrect treatment of closure or recession behavior at zero activity.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Opposite Errors from Constant Zero-Activity Branches
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Examples of enlargement and deletion caused by incorrect zero-activity conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f_1(x)=|x|\), the closed perspective satisfies \(p_{f_1}(d,0)=|d|\); assigning value \(0\) to every \((d,0)\) therefore admits spurious epigraph points with height below \(|d|\). For \(f_2=\delta_{[0,\infty)}\), one has \(p_{f_2}(d,0)=\delta_{[0,\infty)}(d)\); assigning \(+\infty\) to every nonzero \((d,0)\) deletes every direction \(d>0\) from the closed perspective domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An all-zero boundary can be too large, while an origin-only finite boundary can be too small.
assumptions_latex: \(p_f\) is the closed perspective of a proper closed convex function \(f\).
\(\delta_C\) is zero on \(C\) and positive infinity outside \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Neither an identically zero branch nor an origin-only finite branch is universally correct at zero activity.
knowledge_statements.title: Opposite Errors from Constant Zero-Activity Branches
Zero-Activity Closure Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed-perspective convention at zero activity, including nontrivial recession directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The closed perspective of \(f\) is
\[f^\pi(x,z)=\begin{cases}z f(x/z),&z>0,\\ f^\infty(x),&z=0,\\ +\infty,&z<0.\end{cases}\]
Replacing the branch \(f^\infty(x)\) at \(z=0\) by \(0\) for every \(x\), or by \(+\infty\) for every nonzero \(x\), is valid only when that replacement agrees with the actual recession function and all activation linkages. Otherwise the modeled epigraph differs from the closure of the positive-activity perspective: feasible recession points may be deleted or spurious zero-activity points may be admitted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At zero activity, a closed perspective is determined by the active function's recession function. An incorrect zero branch can add or remove feasible limit points.
assumptions_latex: The function \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is proper, closed, and convex.
Its recession function is \(f^\infty(d)=\sup_{x\in\operatorname{dom}f}\bigl(f(x+d)-f(x)\bigr)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The closed perspective has zero-activity value \(f^\infty(x)\), not an arbitrary constant or unconditional infeasibility.

notation.meaning: closed perspective of the active function
recession function of the active function

children.title: Feasibility-Based Bound Tightening
children.top_down_role: Local propagation and feasibility reasoning used to contract domains.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Consistency Need Not Detect Global Infeasibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of constraint-by-constraint propagation to decide global feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let x,y\in\{0,1\} and impose x=y and x=1-y. The combined system is infeasible. Nevertheless, for either constraint considered separately, each value of either variable has support in the other variable's current domain, so ordinary constraint-by-constraint arc propagation deletes no value. Thus a nonempty propagation fixed point does not certify global feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The constraints x=y and x=1-y are jointly infeasible but separately leave both binary domains unchanged.
assumptions_latex: Propagation processes each constraint locally against the current domains.
No rule combines the two constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: B^*\ne\varnothing\centernot\Longrightarrow F\cap B^*\ne\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.title: Local Consistency Need Not Detect Global Infeasibility

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Termination and schedule independence of fair monotone contracting propagation on finite domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \mathcal L be a finite lattice of domain states ordered by inclusion, and let P_1,\ldots,P_m:\mathcal L\to\mathcal L be monotone and contracting. Starting from B^0, repeatedly apply the operators under a fair schedule. After finitely many strict contractions the state stabilizes at the greatest common fixed point of the P_i contained in B^0, independently of the fair order. If every P_i is sound for F, then F\cap B^0\subseteq B^*.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fair iteration of monotone contracting rules on finite domains terminates at an order-independent greatest common fixed point and preserves all feasible points when the rules are sound.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal L is finite.
Every P_i is monotone and contracting.
The schedule is fair; feasible-point preservation additionally requires soundness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P_i(B^*)=B^*\ \forall i,\qquad F\cap B^0\subseteq B^*.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Lattice Propagation Fixpoint

assumptions_latex: A constraint system \(F\) is considered over a current box \(B=\prod_{i=1}^n[\ell_i,u_i]\).
Each propagation rule used is sound: it removes no point of \(F\cap B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Repeated sound propagation produces a contracted box containing every feasible point in the original box.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: sound constraint propagation preserves all feasible points while contracting domains; exact supporting locator unavailable
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixpoint propagation over interval domains; completeness is not asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(B^0=B\). At iteration \(k\), apply a sound local feasibility rule to obtain \(B^{k+1}=P_k(B^k)\subseteq B^k\), where soundness means \(F\cap B^k\subseteq B^{k+1}\). Stop when no rule contracts a bound beyond a prescribed tolerance, or declare infeasibility if some interval becomes empty. The output \(B^*\) satisfies \(F\cap B\subseteq B^*\subseteq B\). Consequently, replacing \(B\) by \(B^*\) preserves all feasible solutions, although \(B^*\) need not equal the interval hull of \(F\cap B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply sound constraint-propagation rules until no bound changes. The resulting smaller box contains every feasible point, but need not be the tightest possible box.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility-Based Bound Tightening

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind and sound-propagation guarantee match feasibility-based bound tightening, but no inspectable citation supports the propagation and infeasibility claims.

children.title: Optimization-Based Bound Tightening
children.top_down_role: Auxiliary optimization relaxations used to contract individual variable domains.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Required Orientation of Inexact Auxiliary Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity requirements for replacing exact auxiliary coordinate extrema by certified bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let m_i=\inf\{x_i:x\in R\cap B\} and M_i=\sup\{x_i:x\in R\cap B\}. A certified lower bound L_i\le m_i yields the valid contraction x_i\ge L_i, while a certified upper bound U_i\ge M_i yields x_i\le U_i. A feasible auxiliary point supplies the opposite objective-bound orientation and alone certifies neither contraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Safe inexact OBBT requires a lower bound on the coordinate-minimization value and an upper bound on the coordinate-maximization value; feasible auxiliary points alone have the wrong orientation.
assumptions_latex: F\subseteq R\cap B.
R\cap B\ne\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L_i\le m_i\Rightarrow F\subseteq\{x:x_i\ge L_i\},\qquad U_i\ge M_i\Rightarrow F\subseteq\{x:x_i\le U_i\}.

notation.meaning: Minimum and maximum of coordinate i over the auxiliary relaxation
Certified outward bounds on the auxiliary extrema

knowledge_statements.title: Required Orientation of Inexact Auxiliary Bounds

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Idempotence of a Full Exact OBBT Sweep
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simultaneous tightening of every coordinate over one fixed closed relaxation and compact box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a closed set R and compact box B with R\cap B\ne\varnothing, let T(B) be the smallest axis-aligned box containing R\cap B. Then R\cap T(B)=R\cap B and consequently T(T(B))=T(B). Thus a full simultaneous exact sweep over a fixed relaxation reaches its coordinate-hull fixed point after one sweep; repeated sweeps can improve bounds only if coordinates are omitted, solves are inexact, or the relaxation itself changes with the bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Computing every exact coordinate extremum over one fixed relaxation is idempotent: a second full sweep cannot tighten the resulting box.
assumptions_latex: R\subseteq\mathbb R^n\text{ is closed}.
B\text{ is compact and }R\cap B\ne\varnothing.
Every coordinate extremum is computed over the same fixed set }R\cap B.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R\cap T(B)=R\cap B,\qquad T(T(B))=T(B).

notation.meaning: Axis-aligned coordinate hull of the relaxed feasible set inside B

review_flags: corrects_builder_claim: finite nontermination is impossible for the stated fixed-relaxation simultaneous operator
knowledge_statements.title: Idempotence of a Full Exact OBBT Sweep

assumptions_latex: A relaxation \(R\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) contains the feasible set \(F\).
The current bounds satisfy \(F\subseteq B=\prod_{i=1}^n[\ell_i,u_i]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Valid auxiliary optimization bounds contract the box without excluding any point of \(F\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: coordinate minimization and maximization over a valid relaxation yield valid variable bounds; exact supporting locator unavailable
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate-wise bound tightening using exact or certified auxiliary relaxation solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each selected coordinate \(i\), solve or validly bound
\[\ell_i'=\inf\{x_i:x\in R\cap B\},\qquad u_i'=\sup\{x_i:x\in R\cap B\}.\]
If an auxiliary solve supplies a certified lower bound \(L_i\le\ell_i'\) or certified upper bound \(U_i\ge u_i'\), use \(\max\{\ell_i,L_i\}\) and \(\min\{u_i,U_i\}\), respectively. Exact optima permit the replacements \(\ell_i\leftarrow\max\{\ell_i,\ell_i'\}\) and \(u_i\leftarrow\min\{u_i,u_i'\}\). Since \(F\subseteq R\cap B\), every retained bound is valid for \(F\); an empty auxiliary relaxation certifies infeasibility of \(F\cap B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize and maximize each selected variable over a valid relaxation. Certified auxiliary bounds safely shrink the variable domain; an empty relaxation proves local infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Optimization-Based Bound Tightening

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The coordinate-wise auxiliary optimization algorithm is mathematically coherent and fits the leaf, but it has no supporting source with a specific locator.

children.title: Dual Reduced-Cost Tightening Certificate System
