children.title: Dual-Certificate Bound Tightening
children.top_down_role: Domain contraction supported by dual relaxation information.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conic Dual Certificate for a Linear Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directly checkable lower- or upper-bound certificate over an affine conic relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let R=\{x\in K:Ax=b\}, where K is a convex cone. If s=q-A^\top y\in K^*, then every x\in R satisfies q^\top x=b^\top y+\langle s,x\rangle\ge b^\top y. Thus y and the verifiable membership s\in K^* certify q^\top x\ge\beta for every \beta\le b^\top y. Taking q=e_i gives a lower bound on x_i; taking q=-e_i gives an upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dual vector with dual-cone slack certifies a bound on any linear functional by weak duality.
assumptions_latex: R=\{x\in K:Ax=b\} with K a convex cone.
q-A^\top y\in K^*.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x\in R\Longrightarrow q^\top x\ge b^\top y.
knowledge_statements.title: Conic Dual Certificate for a Linear Bound

assumptions_latex: A convex relaxation is \(R=\{x:g_j(x)\le0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\), with each \(g_j\) convex.
For a proposed inequality \(a^\top x\ge\beta\), nonnegative multipliers \(\lambda_j\) satisfy \(a^\top x-\beta\ge-\sum_j\lambda_j g_j(x)\) throughout the current domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The multipliers form a directly checkable certificate that \(a^\top x\ge\beta\) is valid on \(R\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: nonnegative multiplier aggregation can certify a valid bound; exact conic-duality version and supporting locator unavailable
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplier certificate for a lower bound; upper bounds follow by changing sign.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(x\in R\), feasibility gives \(g_j(x)\le0\), so \(-\sum_{j=1}^m\lambda_jg_j(x)\ge0\). If the displayed domain-valid inequality
\[a^\top x-\beta\ge-\sum_{j=1}^m\lambda_jg_j(x)\]
holds with \(\lambda_j\ge0\), then \(a^\top x\ge\beta\) holds throughout \(R\). The certificate consists of \(\lambda\) together with a verifiable representation of the displayed inequality. Taking \(a=e_i\) certifies a lower bound on \(x_i\), while \(a=-e_i\) certifies an upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative dual multipliers can aggregate relaxation constraints into a checkable variable-bound inequality. Changing the sign of the objective certifies an upper rather than lower bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Certificate Bound Tightening

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind fits, but the domain-valid multiplier inequality is itself the substantive certificate condition and its verifiable representation is unspecified. An authoritative duality or certificate source is required.

children.title: Reduced-Cost Bound Tightening
children.top_down_role: Domain contraction supported by reduced-cost implications.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sign-complete reduced-cost contraction for a bounded equality-form minimization LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \min\{c^\top x:Ax=b,\ \ell\le x\le u\} with finite bounds. For any y, define r=c-A^\top y and L(y)=b^\top y+\sum_{r_i\ge0}r_i\ell_i+\sum_{r_i<0}r_i u_i. Every feasible x satisfies c^\top x\ge L(y). If r_j>0, then c^\top x\ge L(y)+r_j(x_j-\ell_j); hence every point satisfying c^\top x\le U obeys x_j\le\ell_j+(U-L(y))/r_j. If r_j<0, then c^\top x\ge L(y)+(-r_j)(u_j-x_j), giving x_j\ge u_j-(U-L(y))/(-r_j). When y is dual optimal, L(y)=z_{LP}; otherwise the same formulas remain valid with the certified lower bound L(y). Integral bounds may be rounded inward.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded-LP reduced-cost decomposition converts the objective gap to a cutoff into an upper or lower variable contraction, with signs determined by the active bound.
assumptions_latex: The relaxation is \min\{c^\top x:Ax=b,\ell\le x\le u\} with finite componentwise bounds.
U is a valid objective cutoff.
L(y) is finite; replacing it by z_{LP} requires a dual-optimal y with L(y)=z_{LP}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r_j>0\Rightarrow x_j\le\ell_j+\frac{U-L(y)}{r_j},\qquad r_j<0\Rightarrow x_j\ge u_j-\frac{U-L(y)}{-r_j}.

notation.meaning: Reduced-cost vector for equality multiplier y.
Certified LP lower bound obtained by minimizing the reduced-cost expression over the box.

knowledge_statements.title: Bounded-Variable LP Reduced-Cost Certificate

assumptions_latex: A minimization LP relaxation has optimal value \(z_{LP}\), and an incumbent cutoff \(U\ge z_{LP}\) is imposed.
A nonbasic variable \(x_j\) is at its lower bound \(\ell_j\) and has reduced cost \(\bar c_j>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every improving solution satisfies \(x_j\le \ell_j+(U-z_{LP})/\bar c_j\).

notation.meaning: reduced cost of the nonbasic variable

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: LP reduced costs bound allowable movement under an incumbent cutoff; exact supporting locator unavailable
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower-bound nonbasic variable in an LP minimization relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An optimal LP dual solution yields the reduced-cost inequality
\[c^\top x\ge z_{LP}+\bar c_j(x_j-\ell_j)\]
for every relaxation-feasible \(x\), after retaining the single nonnegative reduced-cost contribution. Any solution capable of improving the incumbent must satisfy \(c^\top x\le U\). Hence
\[x_j\le \ell_j+\frac{U-z_{LP}}{\bar c_j}.\]
Intersecting this value with the current upper bound is valid. For an integral \(x_j\), the tightened upper bound may be rounded down. Analogous formulas apply to a variable at its upper bound or to maximization after consistent sign changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive reduced cost limits how far a nonbasic variable can move before exhausting the objective gap to the incumbent, yielding a certified tighter bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Cost Bound Tightening

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The reduced-cost conclusion is standard for a bounded-variable LP under a compatible optimal dual solution, but the assumptions do not state the LP form needed to justify dropping all other reduced-cost contributions. A supporting source is needed to fix the exact hypotheses.

children.title: Incumbent-Cutoff Implications
children.top_down_role: Bound consequences obtained by combining certificate information with an objective cutoff.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pruning semantics when a node lower bound equals an incumbent value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For minimization, let U be the value of a verified feasible incumbent and let L bound every feasible objective in a node from below. If L>U, the node contains no solution with objective at most U. If L\ge U, it contains no solution with objective strictly below U. Equality pruning is therefore valid for retaining one optimum or proving the optimal value, but it may discard alternative optimal solutions and is invalid when every solution with value at most U must be preserved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bound above the cutoff excludes all cutoff-feasible solutions; equality excludes strict improvement only and may discard alternative optima.
assumptions_latex: U is the value of a verified feasible incumbent.
L is a valid node lower bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L>U\Rightarrow\nexists x:f(x)\le U,\qquad L\ge U\Rightarrow\nexists x:f(x)<U.
knowledge_statements.title: Strict-Improvement versus Solution-Preserving Cutoffs

assumptions_latex: A minimization relaxation supplies a valid inequality \(c^\top x\ge L+\gamma(x_j-\ell_j)\) with \(\gamma>0\).
Only solutions satisfying the incumbent cutoff \(c^\top x\le U\) are relevant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The cutoff implies \(x_j\le\ell_j+(U-L)/\gamma\), and excludes the node when \(L>U\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: combining a dual lower-bound inequality with an incumbent cutoff yields domain implications; exact supporting locator unavailable
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-cutoff consequences derived from a certified marginal penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Combining \(c^\top x\ge L+\gamma(x_j-\ell_j)\) with \(c^\top x\le U\) gives
\[\gamma(x_j-\ell_j)\le U-L.\]
Therefore every solution that can meet the incumbent cutoff satisfies \(x_j\le\ell_j+(U-L)/\gamma\). If \(x_j\) is integral, the right-hand side may be rounded down. If \(L>U\), no relaxation-feasible point meets the cutoff, so the node may be pruned. If \(L=U\), every cutoff-feasible point must have \(x_j=\ell_j\) whenever \(\gamma>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certified objective penalty and incumbent cutoff imply a tighter variable bound. If the relaxation lower bound already exceeds the cutoff, the node is excluded.
knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent-Cutoff Implications

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cutoff implication follows from the stated marginal-penalty inequality and the property kind fits, but no inspectable source supports this bound-tightening use and pruning convention.

children.title: Conditional-Bound Probing Algorithm Family
children.top_down_role: Conditional contraction based on discrete assignments and logical implications.

children.title: Discrete-Assignment Probing
children.top_down_role: Trial restrictions based on fixed discrete assignments.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Work bound for exhaustive single-variable assignment probing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If every v\in D_y is probed once and its conditional analysis costs T_v, the conditional-analysis work is \sum_{v\in D_y}T_v, plus domain-update overhead. If T_v\le T uniformly, this is O(|D_y|T). Simultaneously probing tuples instead of single values replaces |D_y| by the size of the tested Cartesian product.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exhaustive single-variable probing performs one conditional analysis per listed value; tuple probing can grow combinatorially.
assumptions_latex: D_y is explicitly enumerated.
Each selected assignment is analyzed once.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_{\mathrm{probe}}=\sum_{v\in D_y}T_v+T_{\mathrm{update}},\qquad T_v\le T\Longrightarrow T_{\mathrm{probe}}=O(|D_y|T+T_{\mathrm{update}}).
knowledge_statements.title: Probe-Enumeration Cost

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Soundness versus Completeness of Assignment Probing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Completeness boundary for finite-domain deletion decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For v\in D_y, let F_v=F\cap\{x:y=v\}. A sound probe may delete v only after certifying F_v=\varnothing. If its conditional feasibility test is complete, it deletes v if and only if F_v=\varnothing. With a merely sound but incomplete test, failure to delete v does not establish F_v\ne\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complete probing removes exactly the infeasible values; survival after incomplete propagation is inconclusive.
assumptions_latex: D_y is finite.
The conditional test is sound; the biconditional additionally requires completeness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{complete conditional testing}\Longrightarrow\bigl(v\text{ survives}\iff F_v\ne\varnothing\bigr).
knowledge_statements.title: Soundness versus Completeness of Assignment Probing

assumptions_latex: A discrete variable \(y\) has a finite current domain \(D_y\).
For each probed value \(v\in D_y\), a sound propagation or relaxation procedure analyzes the system augmented by \(y=v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The probe may validly remove infeasible values and record bounds that hold conditionally on feasible assignments.

notation.meaning: current finite domain of the probed variable
conditional domain obtained under a probe

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: probing fixes a discrete assignment and applies sound conditional inference; exact supporting locator unavailable
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-domain probing with sound conditional propagation or relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each selected \(v\in D_y\), temporarily impose \(y=v\), initialize the remaining domains from the current box \(B\), and run a sound feasibility or bound-tightening procedure. If the augmented system is certified infeasible, delete \(v\) from \(D_y\). Otherwise store the resulting conditional box \(B^{(v)}\), which must contain every feasible point satisfying \(y=v\). After all selected probes, restore the unconditional system and output the reduced domain together with the conditional bounds. Stop early if \(D_y\) becomes empty; this certifies infeasibility of the current node.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Temporarily fix a discrete variable to each selected value, propagate or solve a relaxation, remove certified-infeasible values, and retain sound conditional bounds from feasible probes.
knowledge_statements.title: Discrete-Assignment Probing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-domain probing algorithm is precise and appropriately scoped, but the record provides no source with a section, theorem, or page locator.

children.title: Implication-Based Conditional Bounds
children.top_down_role: Domain contractions associated with logical implications.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simultaneous representation of assignment-specific intervals for an exhaustive discrete partition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let z_v\in\{0,1\} satisfy \sum_{v\in D_y}z_v=1, with z_v=1 exactly when y=v. If every feasible point under assignment v satisfies \ell_i^{(v)}\le x_i\le u_i^{(v)}, then x_i\ge\sum_v\ell_i^{(v)}z_v and x_i\le\sum_vu_i^{(v)}z_v are valid. Integral one-hot indicators select the stored interval for the active assignment; relaxing z to the simplex yields the corresponding convex interpolation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exhaustive one-hot indicators aggregate all assignment-specific intervals into two linear inequalities.
assumptions_latex: z_v\in\{0,1\} and \sum_vz_v=1 encode an exhaustive partition.
Every conditional interval is sound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_v\ell_i^{(v)}z_v\le x_i\le\sum_vu_i^{(v)}z_v.
knowledge_statements.title: One-Hot Aggregation of Conditional Bounds

assumptions_latex: For a discrete assignment \(y=v\), sound probing establishes \(x_i\in[\ell_i^{(v)},u_i^{(v)}]\).
The assignment indicator \(z_v\) equals one exactly when \(y=v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The conditional bounds yield valid indicator implications and corresponding linear inequalities.

notation.meaning: unconditional bounds on the affected variable

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: sound probe bounds define valid indicator implications and big-M interpolation inequalities; exact supporting locator unavailable
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear encoding of bounds conditional on one discrete assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The probe result gives the implications
\[z_v=1\ \Longrightarrow\ \ell_i^{(v)}\le x_i\le u_i^{(v)}.\]
When unconditional valid bounds \(\ell_i\le x_i\le u_i\) are available, these implications admit the valid linear inequalities
\[x_i\ge \ell_i+(\ell_i^{(v)}-\ell_i)z_v,\qquad x_i\le u_i+(u_i^{(v)}-u_i)z_v.\]
At \(z_v=1\) they impose the conditional interval, while at \(z_v=0\) they reduce to the unconditional bounds. The formulation is valid only if the recorded conditional bounds were obtained by sound inference.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sound bound found under a discrete assignment becomes an indicator implication. With global bounds, it can be written as two valid linear interpolation inequalities.
knowledge_statements.title: Implication-Based Conditional Bounds

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The indicator representation correctly interpolates between unconditional and conditional bounds, assuming sound probe bounds, but lacks an inspectable supporting citation.

children.title: Infeasible Probe Exclusion
children.top_down_role: Branch exclusions exposed by contradictory probe outcomes.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Numerical-evidence boundary for deleting a discrete assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A solver failure status or positive numerical residual does not by itself justify excluding y=v. Exclusion requires an exact certificate that F\cap\{x:y=v\}=\varnothing, or verified error bounds showing that a strict certificate margin dominates all residual and data-perturbation errors. Otherwise the probe is inconclusive and v must remain in the domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Numerical failure alone cannot delete an assignment; exact certification or a rigorously protected margin is required.
assumptions_latex: The conditional analysis uses approximate or finite-precision computations.
Deletion must preserve every exactly feasible point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{uncertified approximate failure}\not\Longrightarrow F\cap\{x:y=v\}=\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.title: Tolerance-Qualified Probe Exclusion

assumptions_latex: The current model has feasible set \(F\), and a probe fixes a discrete assignment \(y=v\).
A sound procedure certifies \(F\cap\{x:y=v\}=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The assignment \(y=v\) may be excluded without removing a feasible solution.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: infeasibility of a conditional subproblem certifies exclusion of that assignment; exact supporting locator unavailable
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exclusion certificate produced by an infeasible conditional probe.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A verifiable infeasibility certificate for the conditional system \(F\cap\{x:y=v\}\) proves the implication \(x\in F\Rightarrow y\ne v\). Hence \(v\) may be removed from the current domain of \(y\). If the assignment is represented by an indicator \(z_v\), the valid fixing is \(z_v=0\). For a binary variable \(y\in\{0,1\}\), infeasibility under \(y=0\) fixes \(y=1\), and infeasibility under \(y=1\) fixes \(y=0\). If every value in the current finite domain is excluded, the current node is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certified-infeasible probe proves that its discrete assignment cannot occur. The value can be deleted, and excluding every available value certifies node infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Infeasible Probe Exclusion

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exclusion-certificate role fits the terminal container and the logical implication is precise, but no source or locator supports the probing certificate claim.

children.title: Partition-Based Convexification
children.top_down_role: Strengthening by subdividing variable domains and applying local convexifications.

children.title: Piecewise McCormick Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Partitioned product and factorable envelopes.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst one-sided vertical error on a rectangle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(w=xy\) on \([a,b]\times[c,d]\), let \(\underline m\) and \(\overline m\) be the McCormick convex and concave envelopes. Then \(0\le xy-\underline m(x,y)\le (b-a)(d-c)/4\) and \(0\le\overline m(x,y)-xy\le(b-a)(d-c)/4\). Both maxima occur at the rectangle midpoint. Thus maximum cell widths \(h_x,h_y\) give one-sided error at most \(h_xh_y/4\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The sharp one-sided McCormick error is one quarter of the product of the cell widths.
assumptions_latex: a<b
c<d
\underline m,\overline m\text{ are the standard McCormick envelopes.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \max(xy-\underline m)=\max(\overline m-xy)=\frac{(b-a)(d-c)}4.

notation.meaning: Maximum cell widths for the two factors

knowledge_statements.title: Sharp Cellwise McCormick Deviation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cellwise Hull Strength Does Not Ensure Encoding Ideality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between exact local hulls and a relaxed union encoding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Even if every cell uses the exact McCormick hull, a nonideal big-\(M\) or other union formulation need not project, after relaxing selectors, to \(\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_{p,q}R_{pq})\). Cellwise exactness alone therefore implies neither ideality nor dominance over the global McCormick relaxation; the latter requires an ideal union formulation or explicit retention of the global inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact local envelopes do not make a weak cell-selection formulation ideal.
assumptions_latex: R_{pq}\text{ is the exact local McCormick hull.}
\text{Cell selectors are relaxed continuously.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{proj}(R_{\mathrm{encoding}})\supsetneq\operatorname{conv}\!\left(\bigcup_{p,q}R_{pq}\right)\text{ is possible.}
knowledge_statements.title: Cellwise Hull Strength Does Not Ensure Encoding Ideality
Piecewise McCormick Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite rectangular partition of a bilinear graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
On each cell \(I_p\times J_q=[a_p,b_p]\times[c_q,d_q]\), impose the four local McCormick inequalities
\[w\ge a_py+c_qx-a_pc_q,\qquad w\ge b_py+d_qx-b_pd_q,\]
\[w\le b_py+c_qx-b_pc_q,\qquad w\le a_py+d_qx-a_pd_q.\]
Model the union of these cell relaxations with an ideal convex-hull disjunctive formulation using selectors \(z_{pq}\in\{0,1\}\) satisfying \(\sum_{p,q}z_{pq}=1\). Its projected continuous relaxation is valid for \(w=xy\) and is contained in the global McCormick relaxation. If a nonideal disjunctive formulation is used instead, the global McCormick inequalities must be retained to guarantee this dominance. Refining the partition and using the corresponding ideal formulation cannot weaken the projected relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply the four McCormick inequalities on each partition cell and use an ideal convex-hull disjunctive formulation. Its projection is valid and at least as strong as the global McCormick envelope; a nonideal formulation needs the global inequalities retained to guarantee that comparison.
assumptions_latex: The bilinear relation is \(w=xy\) over \([\ell_x,u_x]\times[\ell_y,u_y]\).
Finite interval partitions \(\{I_p\}_p\) and \(\{J_q\}_q\) cover the domains of \(x\) and \(y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An ideal disjunctive formulation of the local McCormick systems is a valid piecewise relaxation that dominates the global McCormick relaxation.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: McCormick inequalities describe the bilinear convex hull on a rectangle, and an ideal partition disjunction strengthens the global envelope

children.title: Piecewise Univariate Envelopes
children.top_down_role: Local envelope families for nonlinear atoms over interval partitions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform rate under bounded second derivative.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(f\in C^2([a,b])\) and \(|f''|\le M\), then its endpoint secant satisfies \(\max_{x\in[a,b]}|f(x)-s_{a,b}(x)|\le M(b-a)^2/8\). A tangent at the interval midpoint also differs from \(f\) by at most \(M(b-a)^2/8\). Consequently, for a curvature-stable atom, using these estimators on cells of maximum width \(h\) gives two-sided envelope width at most \(Mh^2/4\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounded curvature gives quadratic convergence of secant-and-tangent local envelopes.
assumptions_latex: f\in C^2([\ell,u])
|f''(x)|\le M
\text{The curvature sign is fixed on each cell.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Maximum two-sided local width}\le Mh^2/4.
knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Local Envelope Error

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of unqualified tangent or secant estimators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(f\) is neither convex nor concave on an interval, endpoint secants and tangents need not remain on a fixed side of its graph. The curvature-stable construction is therefore invalid across such an interval unless separate range or curvature analysis certifies every estimator; subdivision at certified curvature changes is one remedy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Secants and tangents cannot be assigned fixed envelope roles across changing curvature without additional certification.
assumptions_latex: \text{No fixed curvature or separate estimator-validity certificate is available.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{An unqualified secant or tangent inequality may cut graph points.}
knowledge_statements.title: Curvature Changes Require Local Certification

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Secant and Tangent Envelopes for Curvature-Stable Atoms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical local envelopes for differentiable convex or concave atoms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(f\) is differentiable and convex on \([a,b]\), its endpoint secant \(s_{a,b}(x)=\frac{b-x}{b-a}f(a)+\frac{x-a}{b-a}f(b)\) satisfies \(f(x)\le s_{a,b}(x)\), while every tangent \(t_\xi(x)=f(\xi)+f'(\xi)(x-\xi)\) satisfies \(t_\xi(x)\le f(x)\). Hence \(\max_{\xi\in T}t_\xi(x)\le y\le s_{a,b}(x)\) is a valid polyhedral graph relaxation for finite \(T\subseteq[a,b]\). For concave \(f\), the inequalities reverse.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tangents underestimate and endpoint secants overestimate a convex atom; their roles reverse for concave atoms.
assumptions_latex: a<b
f\text{ is differentiable and convex or concave on }[a,b].
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \max_{\xi\in T}t_\xi(x)\le f(x)\le s_{a,b}(x)\text{ in the convex case.}
knowledge_statements.title: Secant and Tangent Envelopes for Curvature-Stable Atoms

assumptions_latex: A continuous function \(f:[\ell,u]\to\mathbb R\) is considered on a finite partition \(\ell=t_0<t_1<\cdots<t_K=u\).
For every interval \(I_k=[t_{k-1},t_k]\), functions \(\underline f_k\) and \(\overline f_k\) satisfy \(\underline f_k(x)\le f(x)\le\overline f_k(x)\) on \(I_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The disjunction of local envelopes is a valid piecewise relaxation of the graph of \(f\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: disjunction of valid local underestimators and overestimators yields a valid graph relaxation; exact supporting locator unavailable
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-sided local graph envelopes over a finite interval partition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the graph relation \(y=f(x)\), define each local relaxation
\[R_k=\{(x,y):x\in I_k,\ \underline f_k(x)\le y\le\overline f_k(x)\}.\]
Then \(\{(x,f(x)):x\in[\ell,u]\}\subseteq\bigcup_{k=1}^K R_k\). A valid disjunctive or convex-hull formulation of \(\bigcup_kR_k\) is therefore a relaxation of the graph. If a refined partition replaces each interval by subintervals and uses estimators no weaker than the restrictions of the old estimators, the resulting union is contained in the former relaxation. Exactness holds when both local estimators equal \(f\) on every selected interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bound a univariate function above and below on each partition interval, then model the union of those local envelopes. Valid refinements produce nested, stronger graph relaxations.
knowledge_statements.title: Piecewise Univariate Envelopes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The local-envelope representation matches the leaf and the set inclusions are coherent, but the meaning of a valid formulation is not tied to a specified representable class, and no inspectable source supports the refinement and exactness statements.

children.title: Adaptive Spatial Partitioning
children.top_down_role: Partition refinement driven by relaxation error, incumbent information, or search progress.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Monotone Bounds Do Not Ensure Global Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure without reliable or fair refinement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Monotonicity \(L_{k+1}\ge L_k\) alone does not imply \(L_k\to v^*\). In particular, if refinement stops at a partition whose relaxation has value \(L<v^*\), or indefinitely avoids every cell responsible for that gap, then \(\sup_k L_k<v^*\) is possible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested lower bounds may remain strictly below the optimum if refinement stops too early or persistently ignores relevant inexact cells.
assumptions_latex: L_k\le v^*
L_{k+1}\ge L_k
\text{No reliability or exhaustive-refinement condition is imposed.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sup_k L_k<v^*\text{ is possible.}
knowledge_statements.title: Monotone Bounds Do Not Ensure Global Convergence

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Asymptotic Exactness under Consistent Fair Refinement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient convergence conditions for adaptive partition relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\) be compact and let \(v^*\) be the minimum of a continuous problem. Suppose \(L_k\le v^*\) are values of nested partition relaxations and each has an optimizer \(z_k\) associated with a cell \(Q_k\). Assume \(\operatorname{diam}(Q_k)\to0\), and that every convergent subsequence \(z_{k_j}\to\bar z\) satisfies: \(\bar z\) represents an original-feasible point and \(\liminf_j L_{k_j}\ge f(\bar z)\). Then \(L_k\uparrow v^*\). If feasible incumbent values satisfy \(U_k\to v^*\), then \(U_k-L_k\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lower bounds converge when cells containing relaxation optimizers shrink and the local relaxations are asymptotically consistent; convergent incumbents then close the gap.
assumptions_latex: D\text{ is compact.}
L_k\le v^*\text{ and }L_{k+1}\ge L_k.
\operatorname{diam}(Q_k)\to0.
\text{Shrinking-cell relaxation limits are feasible and objective-consistent.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L_k\uparrow v^*,\qquad U_k\to v^*\Longrightarrow U_k-L_k\to0.

notation.meaning: Cell associated with a relaxation optimizer

knowledge_statements.title: Asymptotic Exactness under Consistent Fair Refinement
Adaptive Spatial Partitioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic adaptive refinement for spatial branch-and-bound or partition-based convexification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a finite partition \(\mathcal P_0\) of \(D\) and choose a tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge 0\). At iteration \(k\), solve \(R(\mathcal P_k)\), obtaining a lower bound \(L_k\), a relaxation solution \(z_k\), and an incumbent value \(U_k\). Assign each active cell \(Q\in\mathcal P_k\) an indicator \(\eta_k(Q)\ge 0\) based on relaxation violation, incumbent relevance, or search progress. If \(U_k-L_k\le\varepsilon\), return the incumbent. If no cell has a positive indicator, terminate with the current partition without claiming gap closure. Otherwise select at least one cell with positive indicator and replace it by finitely many subcells whose union is that cell. Construct \(R(\mathcal P_{k+1})\) so that its feasible set is contained in that of \(R(\mathcal P_k)\). Then \(L_{k+1}\ge L_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly solve the relaxation and refine cells indicated by error or incumbent relevance. Nested relaxations give nondecreasing minimization lower bounds; if no eligible cell exists before the gap closes, the procedure reports that stopping condition.
assumptions_latex: The nonconvex minimization problem has compact domain \(D\subset\mathbb{R}^n\).
For every finite partition \(\mathcal P\) of \(D\), a computable convex relaxation \(R(\mathcal P)\) and cellwise error indicators are available.
The tolerance satisfies \(\varepsilon\ge 0\), and each relaxation solved by the procedure yields the stated lower bound and relaxation solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every performed refinement produces nested partitions and nondecreasing relaxation bounds for minimization.

children.title: Partition Size–Strength Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Representation growth and bound improvement across partition designs.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cell-count growth for tensor-product and selective partitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If coordinate \(x_i\) is divided into \(k_i\ge1\) intervals, the full Cartesian partition has exactly \(M=\prod_{i=1}^d k_i\) cells; a uniform \(k\)-interval partition has \(k^d\) cells. With \(O(1)\) local objects per cell, cellwise formulation size is \(O(M)\), excluding shared linking structure. Partitioning only coordinates in \(S\) reduces the count to \(\prod_{i\in S}k_i\), but need not provide strengthening associated with omitted coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Full grids grow multiplicatively, while selective partitioning reduces size but may produce weaker bounds.
assumptions_latex: k_i\in\mathbb N
\text{All Cartesian products of coordinate intervals are included.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M=\prod_{i=1}^d k_i,\qquad M=k^d\text{ for a uniform grid.}
knowledge_statements.title: Cartesian Partition Growth

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits of cell count as a proxy for quality or runtime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nested relaxations, refinement guarantees only \(L_{m'}\ge L_m\). Equality may hold when the added restrictions are inactive at a coarse optimizer or already implied. Moreover, cell count alone orders neither runtime nor numerical difficulty, which also depend on encoding, symmetry, sparsity, and solver behavior.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: More cells need not improve the bound strictly and do not determine runtime.

\text{Both relaxations use the same minimization objective.}

Partition Size–Strength Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotone nested refinements with fixed-size cell formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal P_{m'}\) be a partition with \(m'\) cells that refines a partition \(\mathcal P_m\) with \(m\) cells, and suppose \(\operatorname{proj}_x R_{m'}\subseteq\operatorname{proj}_x R_m\). For minimization, \(L_{m'}\ge L_m\), and both values remain lower bounds on the original optimum. If each cell contributes at most \(p\) continuous variables, \(q\) binary variables, and \(r\) local constraints, then the cellwise part of the formulation for \(\mathcal P_{m'}\) uses at most \(m'p\) continuous variables, \(m'q\) binary variables, and \(m'r\) local constraints, in addition to shared linking structure. Thus refinement may strengthen the bound while increasing the available cellwise representation in proportion to the refined partition size; equality of bounds or smaller-than-upper-bound formulations remains possible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nested refinement cannot worsen a minimization lower bound. With fixed per-cell formulation limits, the available cellwise variables and constraints grow at most linearly with the number of cells, although neither strict bound improvement nor strict size growth is guaranteed.
assumptions_latex: A compact domain \(D\) is partitioned into \(m\) cells and then refined into \(m'\) cells.
Each cell contributes at most fixed numbers \(p\), \(q\), and \(r\) of continuous variables, binary variables, and local constraints, respectively.
The refined relaxation projects into the coarse relaxation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Refinement preserves relaxation validity and cannot decrease the minimization lower bound, while its cellwise representation has size bounded linearly in \(m'\).

children.title: Valid-Inequality Enrichment
children.top_down_role: Additional linear or convex restrictions introduced before or after lifting.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iterative addition of violated restrictions from a prescribed valid family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal H\) be a family of sets containing \(F\). Starting from \(R_0\supseteq F\), optimize over \(R_k\), query a returned point \(y_k\), and either obtain \(H_k\in\mathcal H\) with \(y_k\notin H_k\) or an oracle certificate that no member of \(\mathcal H\) separates \(y_k\). In the former case set \(R_{k+1}=R_k\cap H_k\). Then \(F\subseteq R_{k+1}\subseteq R_k\); oracle termination certifies only that the returned point satisfies every restriction detectable by that oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimize, separate the returned relaxation point, and add a violated valid restriction; each step preserves the original feasible set and shrinks the relaxation.
assumptions_latex: F\subseteq R_0
F\subseteq H\text{ for every }H\in\mathcal H
The oracle returns only members of \mathcal H
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\subseteq R_{k+1}\subseteq R_k\quad\text{for every enrichment step }k
knowledge_statements.title: Separation-Based Enrichment

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cut-addition bound for a finite valid-inequality pool.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\mathcal H=\{H_1,\ldots,H_m\}\) and every nonterminal iteration adds at least one previously unused member violated by the queried point, then at most \(m\) enrichment iterations occur. If termination means that no member of the full pool separates the returned point, that point lies in \(R_0\cap\bigcap_{i=1}^mH_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pool of m restrictions permits at most m cut-addition iterations when every nonterminal iteration adds a new violated member.
assumptions_latex: |\mathcal H|=m<\infty
No member is added more than once
Every nonterminal iteration adds a violated unused member
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{enrich}}\leq m
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Pool Termination Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of feasibility and bound validity when an added inequality is not valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\{0\}\), \(R=[0,1]\), and minimize \(x\). The inequality \(x\geq\tfrac12\) is not valid for \(F\). Adding it gives \(R^+=[\tfrac12,1]\), so \(F\nsubseteq R^+\), and the enriched value \(\tfrac12\) exceeds the true value \(0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An invalid cut can delete original feasible points and destroy the relaxation-bound guarantee.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\nsubseteq R\cap\{x:x\geq\tfrac12\}

notation.meaning: relaxation after adding the invalid inequality

knowledge_statements.title: Invalid-Cut Failure Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity, redundancy, and convexity preservation in the original or lifted relaxation space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F\subseteq R\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), an inequality \(g(x)\leq0\) is valid for \(F\) when \(F\subseteq H_g:=\{x:g(x)\leq0\}\). It is redundant relative to \(R\) when \(R\subseteq H_g\); otherwise it strengthens \(R\) to \(R\cap H_g\). If \(R\) and \(H_g\) are convex, then the enriched relaxation is convex. For a lifted relaxation \(Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+p}\), an added lifted restriction is valid for the projected feasible set when every \(x\in F\) retains at least one feasible lift.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid restriction preserves every original feasible point, is redundant if already implied by the relaxation, and preserves convexity when its feasible region is convex. In a lift, every original feasible point must retain a representing lift.
assumptions_latex: F\subseteq R\subseteq\mathbb R^n
R\text{ and }H_g\text{ are convex when convexity preservation is asserted}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\subseteq R\cap H_g\subseteq R

notation.meaning: set defined by the added inequality

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dominance and Redundancy Relative to a Relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison of candidate valid inequalities within a fixed relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For valid halfspaces \(H_1,H_2\), the first inequality dominates the second relative to \(R\) when \(R\cap H_1\subseteq R\cap H_2\). The inequalities are equivalent relative to \(R\) when these intersections are equal. The second is redundant after adding the first precisely when \(R\cap H_1\subseteq H_2\), and is redundant before enrichment precisely when \(R\subseteq H_2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dominance, equivalence, and redundancy of valid inequalities are relative to the current relaxation.
assumptions_latex: F\subseteq R
F\subseteq H_1\cap H_2
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: H_1\text{ dominates }H_2\text{ on }R\iff R\cap H_1\subseteq R\cap H_2

Let \(C=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(F)

knowledge_statements.title: Strict Separation by a Valid Linear Inequality

assumptions_latex: The original feasible set is \(F\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), and \(R\supseteq F\) is a convex relaxation.
Every added inequality is valid for all points of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Intersecting the relaxation with valid inequalities preserves all feasible points and can only strengthen its optimization bound.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity and bound monotonicity before or after lifting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g_j:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex functions satisfying \(g_j(x)\le 0\) for every \(x\in F\), for \(j=1,\ldots,s\). Define \(R^+=R\cap\bigcap_{j=1}^s\{x:g_j(x)\le0\}\). Then \(F\subseteq R^+\subseteq R\). Consequently, for any objective \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(\inf_{x\in R}c^\top x\le\inf_{x\in R^+}c^\top x\le\inf_{x\in F}c^\top x\). The same assertion holds in an extended space when validity is imposed on a lift of every point in \(F\) and the enriched formulation is subsequently projected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding convex inequalities valid for every original feasible point preserves validity and can only improve a minimization relaxation bound.

children.title: Redundant Constraint Products
children.top_down_role: Product consequences used to strengthen RLT and polynomial relaxations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combinatorial size of exhaustive bounded-degree product generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With \(m\) nonnegative generators, imposing every distinct square-free product involving at most \(t\) generators produces \(\sum_{s=1}^{t}\binom ms\) candidate product constraints before eliminating duplicates or unsupported degrees. A dense lift containing every monomial in \(n\) variables of total degree at most \(r\) has \(\binom{n+r}{r}\) monomial coordinates, including the constant. Thus exhaustive product generation and dense monomial lifting can grow combinatorially even though a selected subfamily may be much smaller.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exhaustive product cuts and dense monomial lifts have combinatorial size, motivating selective generation.
assumptions_latex: 1\le t\le m
\text{Products are square-free subsets of the }m\text{ generators.}
\text{The dense lift contains all monomials of total degree at most }r.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{products}}=\sum_{s=1}^{t}\binom ms,\qquad N_{\mathrm{monomials}}=\binom{n+r}{r}.

notation.meaning: Maximum monomial degree in the dense lift

knowledge_statements.title: Product and Monomial Count Growth

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lifted equalities obtained from polynomial multiples of exact equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(h(x)=0\) on the feasible set, then \(q(x)h(x)=0\) for every polynomial \(q\). Whenever all monomials of \(qh\) are represented, linearization gives the valid equality \(\mathcal L(qh)=0\). By contrast, a product inequality is justified from sign information only when its factors have a certified sign producing the asserted product sign.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact equalities may be multiplied by any supported polynomial, while inequality products require certified factor signs.
assumptions_latex: h(x)=0\text{ on the original feasible set.}
\mathcal L\text{ represents every monomial of }q(x)h(x).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal L(qh)=0\text{ is valid.}

notation.meaning: Constraint polynomial vanishing on the feasible set

knowledge_statements.title: Products with Equality Constraints

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invalidity of naive truncation or unsupported substitution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A product whose degree exceeds the represented lift cannot generally be converted into a valid affine cut by dropping or independently substituting unrepresented monomials. Any replacement must itself be connected by valid exact identities or correctly directed relaxation inequalities. Product nonnegativity alone therefore does not certify an arbitrary truncated linearization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Missing monomials cannot be discarded or substituted arbitrarily when a product is linearized.
assumptions_latex: \text{At least one monomial in the expanded product lacks a valid represented replacement.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Naively truncated linearization need not be valid.}
knowledge_statements.title: Linearization Requires Supported Monomials

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nested strengthening through richer supported product families.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At order \(r\), linearize selected products of valid nonnegative polynomial constraints whose expanded monomials are represented by the order-\(r\) lift. If order \(r+1\) retains the order-\(r\) variables and restrictions, then \(\operatorname{proj}(R_{r+1})\subseteq R_r\), so minimization lower bounds satisfy \(L_{r+1}\ge L_r\). Strict improvement and finite exactness are not guaranteed without additional assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Richer monomial lifts support nested product relaxations, but higher order need not improve strictly or become finitely exact.
assumptions_latex: g_i(x)\ge0\text{ on the original feasible set.}
\mathcal L_r\text{ represents every selected expanded product.}
R_{r+1}\text{ retains all order-}r\text{ restrictions.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{proj}(R_{r+1})\subseteq R_r,\qquad L_{r+1}\ge L_r.
knowledge_statements.title: Higher-Degree Product Hierarchy

assumptions_latex: The feasible set satisfies affine inequalities \(g_i(x)=a_i^\top x-b_i\ge0\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\).
A lifted relaxation contains variables representing the monomials created by multiplying selected inequalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Linearizing nonnegative constraint products yields valid affine restrictions in the lifted variables.

notation.meaning: Lifted matrix intended to equal the quadratic product matrix

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degree-two RLT consequence of affine inequality products.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each selected pair \((i,j)\), feasibility implies \(g_i(x)g_j(x)\ge0\). Expanding gives \((a_i^\top x-b_i)(a_j^\top x-b_j)\ge0\). With a lifted matrix \(X\) representing \(xx^\top\), linearization yields the affine constraint \(a_i^\top X a_j-b_j a_i^\top x-b_i a_j^\top x+b_i b_j\ge0\). More generally, if a product of known nonnegative constraint polynomials has degree represented by the lift, applying \(\mathcal L\) to that product produces a valid linear constraint. These restrictions are redundant for exact monomial identities but may cut points admitted by their relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Products of nonnegative constraint slacks are nonnegative; replacing represented monomials by lifted variables turns these consequences into valid linear restrictions.
knowledge_statements.title: Redundant Constraint Products

children.title: Implied Conic Constraints
children.top_down_role: Conic consequences used to strengthen lifted relaxations.

assumptions_latex: A lifted feasible set \(F^L\) satisfies an affine conic expression \(A z+b\in K\), where \(K\) is a closed convex cone.
A proposed conic restriction is satisfied by every point of \(F^L\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Adding the implied conic restriction preserves validity and strengthens the lifted relaxation by intersection.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic validity statement for affine conic consequences in a lifted space.

source_refs.locator: 3.3 What can be expressed via conic quadratic constraints? p. 85

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(F^L\subseteq R^L\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) and every \(z\in F^L\) satisfies \(Cz+d\in Q\), where \(Q\) is a closed convex cone. Then \(\widehat R^L=R^L\cap\{z:Cz+d\in Q\}\) obeys \(F^L\subseteq\widehat R^L\subseteq R^L\). Hence the conic consequence is valid and cannot weaken the relaxation. It is genuinely strengthening precisely when some \(\bar z\in R^L\) has \(C\bar z+d\notin Q\). Second-order, rotated second-order, and positive-semidefinite cones are included when the corresponding affine conic implication is valid on \(F^L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any affine conic condition implied by the lifted feasible set may be intersected with its relaxation, and it strengthens the relaxation when it excludes an admitted point.
knowledge_statements.title: Implied Conic Constraints

source_witnesses.locator: 3.3 What can be expressed via conic quadratic constraints? p. 85

children.title: Implied Matrix Constraints
children.top_down_role: Matrix-structured consequences available in lifted spaces.

assumptions_latex: Every lifted feasible point \(z\in F^L\) satisfies a symmetric affine matrix inequality.
The ambient relaxation is \(R^L\supseteq F^L\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The implied positive-semidefinite constraint is valid and can strictly strengthen the relaxation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine positive-semidefinite consequences in lifted formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M(z)=M_0+\sum_{i=1}^d z_iM_i\in\mathbb S^p\), and suppose \(M(z)\succeq0\) for all \(z\in F^L\). The enriched relaxation \(\widehat R^L=R^L\cap\{z:M(z)\succeq0\}\) satisfies \(F^L\subseteq\widehat R^L\subseteq R^L\). Equivalently, the matrix condition enforces \(v^\top M(z)v\ge0\) for every \(v\in\mathbb{R}^p\). It is strictly stronger than \(R^L\) whenever \(R^L\) contains a point \(\bar z\) for which \(M(\bar z)\) has a negative eigenvalue.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-semidefinite matrix inequality holding for every lifted feasible point is valid and removes relaxation points whose matrix pencil has a negative eigenvalue.
knowledge_statements.title: Implied Matrix Constraints

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite scalar cut certifying violation of an implied PSD constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(M(\bar z)\not\succeq0\), any \(v\ne0\) with \(v^\top M(\bar z)v<0\) yields the valid affine inequality \(v^\top M(z)v\ge0\) for every exact lifted feasible \(z\), and separates \(\bar z\). An eigenvector associated with \(\lambda_{\min}(M(\bar z))<0\) supplies such a vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A negative-eigenvalue eigenvector gives a valid scalar affine cut separating a violated implied PSD constraint.
assumptions_latex: M(z)\succeq0\text{ for every exact lifted feasible point }z.
M(\bar z)\not\succeq0.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: v^\top M(z)v\ge0\text{ is valid and }v^\top M(\bar z)v<0.
knowledge_statements.title: Negative-Eigenvector Separation Certificate

children.title: Cross-Representation Strengthening
children.top_down_role: Strength gains obtained by transferring consequences between representations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Separate Projection Witnesses Need Not Be Compatible
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Difference between intersecting projections and linking lifts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Membership \(x\in P_1\cap P_2\) provides possibly independent witnesses \(z_1,z_2\) and does not enforce \(H(z_1,z_2)=0\). Thus a compatible joint lift may project strictly inside \(P_1\cap P_2\). Conversely, a link not satisfiable by lifts of every original feasible point destroys relaxation validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Separate projections do not make their lifted witnesses agree; valid links can strengthen them, while invalid links can remove original points.
assumptions_latex: P_i=\operatorname{proj}_xR_i,\quad i=1,2
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{proj}_xR_\times\subsetneq P_1\cap P_2\text{ is possible, and validity requires compatible lifts of every original point.}
knowledge_statements.title: Separate Projection Witnesses Need Not Be Compatible
Cross-Representation Strengthening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint lifting with exact links between conic, matrix, or algebraic representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(i\in\{1,2\}\), let \(R_i\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times Z_i\) be a relaxation with original variable \(x\), lifted variable \(z_i\), and projection \(P_i=\operatorname{proj}_x R_i\). Define \(R_\times=\{(x,z_1,z_2):(x,z_1)\in R_1,\ (x,z_2)\in R_2,\ H(z_1,z_2)=0\}\), where every original feasible point has lifts satisfying the linking equations. Then the original feasible set is contained in \(\operatorname{proj}_x R_\times\), and \(\operatorname{proj}_x R_\times\subseteq P_1\cap P_2\). Thus jointly enforcing compatible representations cannot weaken either projected relaxation. The inclusion is strict if some \(\bar x\in P_1\cap P_2\) has no pair of lifts \((\bar x,z_1)\in R_1\) and \((\bar x,z_2)\in R_2\) satisfying \(H(z_1,z_2)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linking compatible lifts gives a valid joint relaxation whose projection lies inside the intersection of the two separate projections. It is strictly stronger when a point admitted by both projections has no mutually compatible pair of lifts.
assumptions_latex: For \(i\in\{1,2\}\), the relaxation \(R_i\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times Z_i\) represents the same original variable \(x\in\mathbb R^n\).
Every original feasible point has lifts in both representations that satisfy the linking equations \(H(z_1,z_2)=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The linked joint formulation projects inside \(P_1\cap P_2\), with strict inclusion under the stated absence of compatible lifts.

notation.meaning: Projection of representation i onto the original variables

children.title: Root-Stage Strengthening
children.top_down_role: Strengthening confined to preprocessing or the root relaxation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Root Loop for a Finite Candidate Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iteration bound when root strengthening draws from a fixed finite restriction family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose accepted restrictions come from a finite family \mathcal C, are never deleted, and every nonterminal iteration accepts at least one previously absent member of \mathcal C. Then there are at most |\mathcal C| productive strengthening iterations. Without finiteness or another progress condition, monotone lower bounds alone imply neither finite termination nor convergence to the exact root value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A root loop over a finite persistent cut family has at most one productive iteration per candidate; monotonicity alone gives no general finite-termination guarantee.
assumptions_latex: |\mathcal C|<\infty.
Accepted restrictions are never deleted.
Every nonterminal iteration adds a previously absent member of \mathcal C.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{strengthen}}\le |\mathcal C|.

notation.meaning: Finite universe of candidate root restrictions

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Root Loop for a Finite Candidate Family
Root-Stage Strengthening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cutting and domain-reduction loop executed before tree search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(\varepsilon\ge0\) and set \(k=0\). Solve \(\inf\{c^\top x:x\in R_k\}\) to obtain a finite lower bound \(L_k\) and an optimizer \(x_k\). Invoke separation and domain-reduction oracles using \(x_k\), \(L_k\), and the incumbent upper bound \(U\), producing an accepted set \(C_k\) of restrictions valid for the root feasible set. If \(C_k\) contains no accepted restriction or \(U-L_k\le\varepsilon\), return \(R_k\), \(L_k\), and the restrictions accepted so far. Otherwise set \(R_{k+1}=R_k\cap C_k\), update the incumbent if available, increment \(k\), and repeat. Validity gives \(R_{k+1}\subseteq R_k\), and therefore \(L_{k+1}\ge L_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At the root, repeatedly solve the attained relaxation, generate valid accepted restrictions, and intersect them with the current relaxation. The resulting minimization lower bounds are nondecreasing until the gap, acceptance, or other stated stopping rule is met.
assumptions_latex: A minimization problem has root relaxation \(R_0\), incumbent upper bound \(U\), and separation or domain-reduction oracles.
Every accepted restriction is valid for the root feasible set.
Each relaxation solved by the loop has a finite attained optimum, and the tolerance satisfies \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The root loop produces nested relaxations and nondecreasing lower bounds until its stopping rule is met.

notation.meaning: Set of valid restrictions accepted at iteration k

children.title: Globally Reusable Strengthening
children.top_down_role: Valid strengthening retained throughout the search tree.

assumptions_latex: A root-generated restriction \(g(x,z)\le0\) is valid for every globally feasible lifted point.
Descendant nodes only add branching restrictions to the global model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The restriction is globally reusable exactly when its validity does not depend on root-local artifacts or assumptions absent at descendants.

notation.meaning: Feasible set at tree node t

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Criterion distinguishing globally valid restrictions from node-dependent cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A restriction \(g(x,z)\le0\) is globally reusable if \(g(x,z)\le0\) for every \((x,z)\in F^L\), and all variables and coefficients in the restriction retain the same meaning throughout the tree. Since each descendant feasible set satisfies \(F_t^L\subseteq F^L\), global validity implies \(g(x,z)\le0\) on every \(F_t^L\). A restriction derived using a node bound, local disjunction, temporary linearization, or node-specific lifting is reusable only if its derivation establishes validity after those local assumptions are removed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strengthening is globally reusable when it remains valid for the global feasible set and uses variables whose interpretation is unchanged at every descendant.
knowledge_statements.title: Globally Reusable Strengthening

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The global-validity condition is correct and appropriately distinguishes globally reusable restrictions from node-dependent ones, but no branch-and-cut or global-optimization source with a locator is supplied.

children.title: Root-to-Tree Transfer
children.top_down_role: Conditions governing reuse of root-derived structure during search.

knowledge_statements.title: Root-to-Tree Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer of globally valid root cuts and reductions to descendant relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq R\) be the global feasible set and its base relaxation. Let \(C\) satisfy \(F\subseteq C\), and, for each node \(t\), let \(F_t\subseteq F\) and \(F_t\subseteq B_t\). Define \(R_t=R\cap B_t\) and \(R_t^+=(R\cap C)\cap B_t\). Then \(F_t\subseteq R_t^+\subseteq R_t\). For minimization, \(\inf_{x\in R_t}c^\top x\le\inf_{x\in R_t^+}c^\top x\le\inf_{x\in F_t}c^\top x\). A restriction whose validity uses an ancestor-specific domain may be transferred only to nodes whose feasible sets retain those assumptions, unless global validity is established separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Globally valid root restrictions can be added to every descendant relaxation while preserving node-feasible points and not weakening minimization bounds. Ancestor-local restrictions remain limited to nodes where their assumptions hold.
assumptions_latex: The global feasible set and base relaxation satisfy \(F\subseteq R\).
The root strengthening set satisfies \(F\subseteq C\).
For each descendant node \(t\), its feasible set satisfies \(F_t\subseteq F\cap B_t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The transferred relaxation satisfies \(F_t\subseteq R_t^+\subseteq R_t\) and cannot decrease the node's minimization lower bound.

children.title: Node-Local Strengthening
children.top_down_role: Domain-specific relaxation improvement within a search tree.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Node-Local Validity Does Not Imply Global Validity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal search-tree example separating node-valid from globally valid strengthening.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let F=\{0,1\}. At node t with branching restriction x=0, the inequality x\le0 is valid for F_t=\{0\}; it is invalid for the sibling set F_s=\{1\} and for F. Thus validity under a node assumption does not license global installation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A restriction valid after fixing x to zero fails at the sibling fixing x to one, so node validity alone does not permit global reuse.
assumptions_latex: F_t=\{0\}\text{ and }F_s=\{1\}\text{ are sibling node-feasible sets}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F_t\subseteq\{x:x\le0\},\qquad F_s\nsubseteq\{x:x\le0\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Node-Local Validity Does Not Imply Global Validity

assumptions_latex: At node \(t\), the feasible domain satisfies \(F_t\subseteq R_t\).
A local oracle returns restrictions valid on \(F_t\), possibly using node bounds or the node disjunction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Iterative local enrichment preserves \(F_t\) and yields nested node relaxations with nondecreasing minimization bounds.

notation.meaning: Node relaxation at local iteration k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Node-specific cutting, convexification, and domain reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(R_{t,0}=R_t\). At local iteration \(k\), solve the node relaxation and call a separation, convexification, or domain-reduction oracle on the current node domain. Let \(C_{t,k}\) be accepted restrictions satisfying \(F_t\subseteq C_{t,k}\), and set \(R_{t,k+1}=R_{t,k}\cap C_{t,k}\). Stop when no accepted restriction exists, the node is infeasible, the node bound permits pruning, or a prescribed local budget is exhausted. Then \(F_t\subseteq R_{t,k+1}\subseteq R_{t,k}\), so the minimization bound is nondecreasing. Restrictions based on node-local assumptions are inherited only within the subtree where those assumptions hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Within a node, repeatedly add restrictions valid on its current domain; bounds improve monotonically, while locally derived restrictions remain confined to the valid subtree.
knowledge_statements.title: Node-Local Strengthening

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The local enrichment algorithm is mathematically consistent, distinguishes subtree-local validity, and fits node-local strengthening, but it has no inspectable spatial branch-and-bound or cutting-plane source.

knowledge_statements.title: Reusable Relaxation Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural decomposition supporting incremental relaxation maintenance across a search tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent the relaxation at node \(t\) as \(R_t=R_{\mathrm{core}}\cap C_{\mathrm{glob}}\cap C_t\), where \(R_{\mathrm{core}}\) contains the fixed variables, objective representation, linking equations, and base convex constraints; \(C_{\mathrm{glob}}\) contains globally reusable strengthening; and \(C_t\) contains restrictions valid under the node's ancestor path and current domain. Moving from a parent \(p\) to a child \(t\) retains \(R_{\mathrm{core}}\cap C_{\mathrm{glob}}\), may inherit every restriction from \(C_p\) whose assumptions remain valid, and adds the child's branching and local restrictions. On backtracking outside the supporting subtree, a local restriction must be deactivated unless its validity has been established for the new node. A restriction may be dropped earlier without destroying relaxation validity, but doing so can weaken the relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reusable node relaxation separates an immutable core and global strengthening from path-dependent restrictions. Local restrictions may be inherited while their assumptions remain valid and must not be enforced outside that region; dropping them merely weakens the relaxation.
assumptions_latex: Tree-node relaxations share a fixed lifted-variable space and a common family of globally valid constraints.
Node changes consist of additional bounds, branching rows, and optional locally valid restrictions.
A local restriction is enforced only at nodes whose feasible sets satisfy the assumptions used to derive it.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each node relaxation can be represented as a common core plus global and validity-scoped local modifications.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(R_k=D_k\cap\bigcap_{c\in\mathcal C_k}\{x:a_c^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta_c\}\), preserve the solver state and construct \(R_{k+1}\) incrementally. Set \(\mathcal C_{k+1}=(\mathcal C_k\setminus\mathcal D_k)\cup\Delta\mathcal C_k\), warm-start optimization over \(R_{k+1}\), and stop when the prescribed separation or bound-improvement tolerance is met. Output \(R_{k+1}\) and its relaxation bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Retain valid relaxation structure, remove invalidated constraints, add new cuts, and warm-start the updated model while preserving containment of the target feasible set.

assumptions_latex: The old and new target feasible sets satisfy \(F_k\subseteq D_k\) and \(F_{k+1}\subseteq D_{k+1}\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity-preserving reuse when bounds, parameters, or the modeled domain change.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On replacing \(D_k\) by \(D_{k+1}\), retain every stored inequality known to be valid on \(D_{k+1}\), discard or revalidate all others, update domain-dependent coefficients, and separate additional inequalities until the chosen stopping rule holds. If \(D_{k+1}\subseteq D_k\), every inequality valid throughout \(D_k\) may be retained. If the domain expands, an inequality may be retained without revalidation only when its validity covers the expanded region. The output is \(R_{k+1}=D_{k+1}\cap\bigcap_{c\in\mathcal C_{k+1}}\{x:a_c^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta_c\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Filter reusable constraints by their validity domains; contractions preserve old valid inequalities, while expansions require global validity, revalidation, or new separation.
knowledge_statements.title: Domain-Change Adaptation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dominance and Equality of Lagrangian and Convex-Hull Relaxation Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The comparison concerns a convex objective, linear inequalities, and finite scalar coordinate domains; equality is between the Lagrangian bound and the convex-hull-relaxation bound, not necessarily between either bound and the original discrete optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X_i\subset\mathbb R\) be finite, let \(\widehat X_i=\operatorname{conv}(X_i)\), and define
\[
f^*=\inf\{f(x):a_j^Tx\le b_j\ (j=1,\ldots,r),\ x_i\in X_i\ (i=1,\ldots,n)\}.
\]
For \(L(x,\mu)=f(x)+\sum_{j=1}^r\mu_j(a_j^Tx-b_j)\), set
\[
q^*=\sup_{\mu\ge0}\inf_{x_i\in X_i}L(x,\mu)
\]
and
\[
\widehat f=\inf\{f(x):a_j^Tx\le b_j\ (j=1,\ldots,r),\ x_i\in\widehat X_i\ (i=1,\ldots,n)\}.
\]
If \(f\) is convex and the convexified problem has no duality gap, then \(\widehat f\le q^*\le f^*\). If, in addition, \(L(\cdot,\mu)\) is concave on \(\prod_i\widehat X_i\) for every \(\mu\ge0\), then \(\widehat f=q^*\). In particular, this equality holds when \(f\) is linear.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex objective with linear inequalities and finite coordinate domains, strong duality for the coordinatewise convex-hull relaxation implies that its bound is no larger than the optimized Lagrangian bound, which in turn is no larger than the original discrete optimum. The first two bounds coincide when every fixed-multiplier Lagrangian is concave on the convexified domain, including when the objective is linear. This does not generally assert exactness relative to the original discrete optimum.
assumptions_latex: X_i\subset\mathbb R\text{ is finite for }i=1,\ldots,n
\widehat X_i=\operatorname{conv}(X_i)
f\text{ is convex}
a_j^Tx\le b_j,\quad j=1,\ldots,r
\widehat f=\sup_{\mu\ge0}\inf_{x_i\in\widehat X_i}L(x,\mu)\text{ (no duality gap for the convexified problem)}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat f\le q^*\le f^*;\qquad \left[\forall\mu\ge0,\ L(\cdot,\mu)\text{ is concave on }\prod_i\widehat X_i\right]\Longrightarrow \widehat f=q^*.

children.top_down_role: Relaxations formed by dualizing the full selected constraint family.

assumptions_latex: The primal problem is \(p^*=\inf_{x\in X}\{f(x):g_i(x)\leq0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\).
The infimum defining the Lagrangian dual function is interpreted in the extended-real sense.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: All designated complicating inequalities are transferred from explicit feasibility into the Lagrangian.

source_refs.locator: 5.7.1. Duality Gap in Separable Problems p. 217

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Complete dualization replaces every designated inequality \(g_i(x)\leq0\) by a nonnegative multiplier. Its Lagrangian and dual function are \[L(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i g_i(x),\qquad q(\lambda)=\inf_{x\in X}L(x,\lambda),\quad \lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m.\] The complete Lagrangian dual is \(d^*=\sup_{\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m}q(\lambda)\). Only the base domain \(X\) remains explicit in the inner minimization; feasibility of all dualized inequalities is represented through multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complete dualization moves every designated inequality into the Lagrangian, leaving only the base domain explicit in the inner minimization.

children.title: Partial Dualization
children.top_down_role: Relaxations retaining a selected constraint subset in the primal subproblem.

assumptions_latex: The inequality indices are partitioned into a dualized set \(S\) and an explicit set \(S^c\).
The primal value is \(p^*=\inf_{x\in X}\{f(x):g_i(x)\leq0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The partial dual value \(d_S=\sup_{\lambda_S\geq0}q_S(\lambda_S)\) is a lower bound on \(p^*\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Only a selected constraint block is dualized; the complementary block remains explicit.

source_refs.locator: 5.7.1. Duality Gap in Separable Problems p. 217

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\), partial dualization defines \[q_S(\lambda_S)=\inf\left\{f(x)+\sum_{i\in S}\lambda_i g_i(x):x\in X,\ g_j(x)\leq0\ \text{for all }j\notin S\right\},\qquad \lambda_S\geq0.\] The associated partial dual problem is \(d_S=\sup_{\lambda_S\geq0}q_S(\lambda_S)\). Thus the constraints indexed by \(S^c\) remain explicit in every Lagrangian subproblem, whereas those indexed by \(S\) contribute only through their multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partial dualization relaxes one selected constraint block while enforcing all complementary constraints explicitly in each Lagrangian subproblem.
knowledge_statements.title: Partial Dualization

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal–dual inclusions and exactness for convex composite minimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates unconditional sufficient inclusions from the regularity and feasibility regimes yielding equality and existence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal H,\mathcal K\) be real Hilbert spaces, \(f\in\Gamma_0(\mathcal H)\), \(g\in\Gamma_0(\mathcal K)\), and \(L\in\mathcal B(\mathcal H,\mathcal K)\). Then \[\operatorname{zer}(\partial f+L^*\circ\partial g\circ L)\subset\operatorname{Argmin}(f+g\circ L)\] and \[\operatorname{zer}(-L\circ\partial f^*\circ(-L^*)+\partial g^*)\subset\operatorname{Argmin}(f^*\circ(-L^*)+g^*).\] Moreover, \[\operatorname{Argmin}(f+g\circ L)=\operatorname{zer}(\partial f+L^*\circ\partial g\circ L)
e\varnothing\] if any of the following holds: (a) \(\operatorname{Argmin}(f+g\circ L)
e\varnothing\) and at least one of \(0\in\operatorname{sri}(\operatorname{dom}g-L(\operatorname{dom}f))\); \(\mathcal K\) finite-dimensional with \(\operatorname{ri}\operatorname{dom}g\cap\operatorname{ri}L(\operatorname{dom}f)
e\varnothing\); \(\mathcal K\) finite-dimensional, \(g\) polyhedral, and \(\operatorname{dom}g\cap\operatorname{ri}L(\operatorname{dom}f)
e\varnothing\); or \(\mathcal H,\mathcal K\) finite-dimensional, \(f,g\) polyhedral, and \(\operatorname{dom}g\cap L(\operatorname{dom}f)
e\varnothing\); (b) \(\operatorname{Argmin}(f+g\circ L)\subset\operatorname{Argmin}f\cap\operatorname{Argmin}(g\circ L)
e\varnothing\) and \(0\in\operatorname{sri}(\operatorname{dom}g-\operatorname{ran}L)\); or (c) \(f=\iota_C\), \(g=\iota_D\) for closed convex \(C\subset\mathcal H\), \(D\subset\mathcal K\), with \(C\cap L^{-1}(D)
e\varnothing\) and \(0\in\operatorname{sri}(D-\operatorname{ran}L)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The primal composite subdifferential inclusion and the conjugate-dual inclusion always provide sufficient conditions for minimizing their respective objectives. The primal inclusion is also necessary and has a nonempty zero set under any of the listed qualification-plus-existence, common-minimizer, or convex-feasibility regimes.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal H,\mathcal K\) are real Hilbert spaces, \(f\in\Gamma_0(\mathcal H)\), \(g\in\Gamma_0(\mathcal K)\), and \(L\in\mathcal B(\mathcal H,\mathcal K)\).
The two displayed inclusions require no additional qualification.
Exactness and nonemptiness require one of the complete alternatives (a), (b), or (c) stated in the theorem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Both zero-set inclusions hold, and under any stated exactness regime, \(\operatorname{Argmin}(f+g\circ L)=\operatorname{zer}(\partial f+L^*\circ\partial g\circ L)\ne\varnothing\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose dualization yields \[L(x,\lambda)=\sum_{b=1}^B L_b(x_b,\lambda),\qquad x=(x_1,\ldots,x_B)\in X_1\times\cdots\times X_B.\] Then \[q(\lambda)=\inf_{x\in X}L(x,\lambda)=\sum_{b=1}^B\inf_{x_b\in X_b}L_b(x_b,\lambda)=\sum_{b=1}^B q_b(\lambda).\] Each block may consequently be solved by its native combinatorial, network, scenario, or convex optimization method. The representation is valid provided the extended-real sum is well defined, excluding ambiguous expressions combining \(+\infty\) and \(-\infty\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Parallel Block Evaluation and Dual Supergradient Assembly
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual-oracle interface induced by decomposed Lagrangian subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \[L(x,\lambda)=\sum_{b=1}^B\bigl(F_b(x_b)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}r_b(x_b)\bigr)-\lambda^{\mathsf T}c\] on \(X=\prod_bX_b\), and choose each block minimizer \(x_b(\lambda)\) independently. Then \[h(\lambda)=\sum_{b=1}^B r_b(x_b(\lambda))-c\] is a supergradient of the concave dual function: \[q(\mu)\leq q(\lambda)+h(\lambda)^{\mathsf T}(\mu-\lambda).\] The block solves may therefore run in parallel before residual aggregation and a projected dual-ascent update.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent block minimizers provide the decomposed dual value and an aggregate supergradient for projected dual ascent.

The extended-real block sum is well defined.
\(\Lambda\) is the appropriate multiplier-feasible set.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A decomposed dual evaluation costs the sum of block costs serially or the largest block cost under ideal parallel execution, plus aggregation.
