children.title: Augmented-Lagrangian Interface
children.top_down_role: Penalty-augmented dual reformulations and their relationship to convex relaxation.

assumptions_latex: The primal problem is \(p^*=\inf\{f(x):x\in X,\ Ax=b\}\).
The penalty parameter satisfies \(\rho>0\), and \(X\) is the explicit base domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every multiplier \(\lambda\), \(q_\rho(\lambda)\leq p^*\); thus the augmented dual remains a valid lower-bounding reformulation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic augmentation of an equality-constrained Lagrangian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The quadratic augmented Lagrangian and its dual function are \[L_\rho(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}(Ax-b)+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert Ax-b\rVert_2^2,\qquad q_\rho(\lambda)=\inf_{x\in X}L_\rho(x,\lambda).\] The augmented dual problem is \(\sup_{\lambda\in\mathbb R^m}q_\rho(\lambda)\), and every multiplier satisfies \(q_\rho(\lambda)\leq p^*\). The quadratic penalty changes the inner subproblem and dual geometry while preserving the lower-bound interpretation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive quadratic residual penalty changes the Lagrangian subproblem and dual geometry while preserving every augmented dual value as a primal lower bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Augmented-Lagrangian Interface

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact augmented-Lagrangian multiplier method for affine equality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed \(\rho>0\), \[x^{k+1}\in\arg\min_{x\in X}L_\rho(x,\lambda^k),\qquad \lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+\rho(Ax^{k+1}-b).\] If \(f+\delta_X\) is proper, closed, and convex, the primal is feasible, the dual solution set is nonempty, and each inner problem is attained and solved exactly, then \(\lambda^k\) converges in finite dimensions to a dual solution and \(Ax^{k+1}-b\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact augmented minimization followed by a residual multiplier update is a proximal-point method whose multipliers converge and residuals vanish under standard convex assumptions.
assumptions_latex: \(f+\delta_X\) is proper, closed, and convex.
The primal is feasible and the dual solution set is nonempty.
Each augmented subproblem is attained and solved exactly.
\(\rho>0\) is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lambda^k\to\lambda^\star,\qquad Ax^{k+1}-b\to0.
knowledge_statements.title: Method-of-Multipliers Iteration

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inherited Exactness from an Ordinary Multiplier
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exactness certificate valid for every positive penalty parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(x^*\) is feasible and an ordinary multiplier \(\lambda^*\) satisfies \(q_0(\lambda^*)=f(x^*)=p^*\), then for every \(\rho>0\), \[q_\rho(\lambda^*)=p^*.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact ordinary dual multiplier also attains the exact augmented dual bound for every positive penalty parameter.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: q_\rho(\lambda^*)=p^*.
knowledge_statements.title: Inherited Exactness from an Ordinary Multiplier

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Quadratic Penalties Need Not Enforce Feasibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary for treating one fixed augmented subproblem as an exact primal reformulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\{(x-1)^2:x=0\}\), fixing \(\lambda=0\) and finite \(\rho>0\) gives the augmented subproblem \[\min_x (x-1)^2+\frac{\rho}{2}x^2,\] whose minimizer is \(x_\rho=2/(\rho+2)\neq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed finite quadratic penalty can have an infeasible minimizer even for a one-dimensional convex problem.
assumptions_latex: \(\rho\in(0,\infty)\).
The multiplier is fixed at \(\lambda=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_\rho=2/(\rho+2)\neq0.

notation.meaning: minimizer of the fixed augmented subproblem

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Quadratic Penalties Need Not Enforce Feasibility

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Moreau-Envelope Representation of the Augmented Dual
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical proximal representation of the quadratic augmented dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q_0\) be the ordinary equality-constraint dual function. Under the stated closedness qualification, \[q_\rho(\lambda)=\sup_{\mu\in\mathbb R^m}\left\{q_0(\mu)-\frac{1}{2\rho}\|\mu-\lambda\|_2^2\right\}.\] The maximizer \(P_\rho(\lambda)\) is unique and \[\nabla q_\rho(\lambda)=\frac{P_\rho(\lambda)-\lambda}{\rho}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The augmented dual is the concave Moreau envelope of the ordinary dual and therefore has a proximal multiplier map.
assumptions_latex: \(f+\delta_X\) is proper, closed, and convex.
The residual value function \(r\mapsto\inf\{f(x):x\in X,\ Ax-b=r\}\) is proper, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: q_\rho(\lambda)=\sup_\mu\{q_0(\mu)-(2\rho)^{-1}\|\mu-\lambda\|_2^2\}.

notation.meaning: proximal maximizer of the ordinary concave dual

knowledge_statements.title: Moreau-Envelope Representation of the Augmented Dual

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Augmentation Dominates the Ordinary Dual Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise and optimized comparison of ordinary and quadratically augmented dual functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\rho>0\), \[q_0(\lambda)\leq q_\rho(\lambda)\leq p^*\quad\text{for every }\lambda,\] and hence \[\sup_\lambda q_0(\lambda)\leq\sup_\lambda q_\rho(\lambda)\leq p^*.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quadratic augmentation improves or preserves every ordinary dual lower bound while remaining below the primal value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: q_0(\lambda)\leq q_\rho(\lambda)\leq p^*.
knowledge_statements.title: Augmentation Dominates the Ordinary Dual Bound

children.title: Weak-Duality Bound Certificates
children.top_down_role: Bounds available independently of exact dual recovery.

assumptions_latex: The primal problem minimizes \(f(x)\) over \(x\in X\) subject to \(g(x)\leq0\).
A proposed multiplier satisfies \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The computable value \(q(\lambda)\) certifies \(q(\lambda)\leq p^*\), independently of strong duality or dual attainment.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A lower-bound certificate requiring only multiplier feasibility and valid subproblem evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}g(x)\) and \(q(\lambda)=\inf_{x\in X}L(x,\lambda)\). A weak-duality bound certificate consists of a multiplier \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\) and a certified evaluation of \(q(\lambda)\). Its guarantee is \[q(\lambda)\leq p^*.\] The certificate remains valid without strong duality, dual attainment, or a zero duality gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative multiplier and certified Lagrangian subproblem value provide a valid primal lower bound without requiring strong duality or dual attainment.
knowledge_statements.title: Weak-Duality Bound Certificates

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak-duality certificate when the Lagrangian subproblem is not solved exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a dual-feasible multiplier \(\lambda\), let \(q(\lambda)=\inf_{x\in X}L(x,\lambda)\). If a verifier establishes \(\ell\le L(x,\lambda)\) for every \(x\in X\), then \[\ell\le q(\lambda)\le p^*.\] Evaluating \(L\) at one trial point instead gives an upper bound on \(q(\lambda)\) and is not a valid primal lower-bound certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certified lower bound on a Lagrangian subproblem is a primal lower bound; a trial subproblem value alone is not.
assumptions_latex: The multiplier is dual feasible.
The inequality \(\ell\le L(x,\lambda)\) is certified for every \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \ell\le q(\lambda)\le p^*.

notation.meaning: Certified lower bound on the Lagrangian subproblem

knowledge_statements.title: Certified Inexact Lagrangian Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A posteriori primal suboptimality bound requiring neither strong duality nor dual attainment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\bar x\) is primal feasible and \(\ell\le p^*\) is a certified Lagrangian lower bound, then \[\ell\le p^*\le f(\bar x),\qquad 0\le f(\bar x)-p^*\le f(\bar x)-\ell.\] Thus the computable difference \(f(\bar x)-\ell\) certifies absolute primal suboptimality even when the optimized dual bound is not exact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal-feasible objective and a certified Lagrangian lower bound sandwich the optimum and bound primal suboptimality.
assumptions_latex: \(\bar x\) is primal feasible.
\(\ell\) is a valid lower bound on \(p^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0\le f(\bar x)-p^*\le f(\bar x)-\ell.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Lagrangian Sandwich Certificate

children.title: Primal-Value Recovery Regimes
children.top_down_role: Structural settings where dualization recovers the primal value.

assumptions_latex: The primal infimum and dual supremum are attained at \(x^*\) and \(\lambda^*\), respectively.
The multiplier satisfies \(\lambda^*\geq0\), and \(x^*\) is primal feasible.
The saddle conditions \(x^*\in\arg\min_{x\in X}L(x,\lambda^*)\) and \((\lambda^*)^{\mathsf T}g(x^*)=0\) hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The primal and dual values coincide: \(f(x^*)=q(\lambda^*)=p^*=d^*\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery through an attained Lagrangian saddle point and complementary slackness.

source_refs.locator: 5.3.4. Duality and Existence of Optimal Primal Solutions p. 176

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}g(x)\). If \(x^*\) is primal feasible, \(\lambda^*\in\mathbb R_+^m\), \(x^*\in\arg\min_{x\in X}L(x,\lambda^*)\), and \((\lambda^*)^{\mathsf T}g(x^*)=0\), then \[q(\lambda^*)=L(x^*,\lambda^*)=f(x^*)=p^*=d^*.\] These conditions certify recovery of the primal value and a primal optimizer. Equality of optimal values alone does not certify recovery of a primal point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible Lagrangian minimizer satisfying complementary slackness with a nonnegative multiplier recovers the primal optimum and certifies zero gap; value equality alone does not recover a point.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Value Recovery Regimes

source_witnesses.locator: 5.3.4. Duality and Existence of Optimal Primal Solutions p. 176

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary-and-sufficient certificate for an attained primal-dual pair to recover the primal value and optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x^*\) be primal feasible and \(\lambda^*\geq0\). Then \[x^*\in\arg\min_{x\in X}L(x,\lambda^*),\quad (\lambda^*)^{\mathsf T}g(x^*)=0\] if and only if \(x^*\) is primal optimal, \(\lambda^*\) is dual optimal, and \[f(x^*)=q(\lambda^*)=p^*=d^*.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For feasible attained witnesses, Lagrangian minimization and complementary slackness are equivalent to joint primal-dual optimality with zero gap.
assumptions_latex: \(x^*\in X\) satisfies \(g(x^*)\leq0\).
\(\lambda^*\in\mathbb R_+^m\).
The displayed objective and dual values are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl[x^*\in\arg\min_XL(\cdot,\lambda^*),\ (\lambda^*)^{\mathsf T}g(x^*)=0\bigr]\iff\bigl[f(x^*)=q(\lambda^*)=p^*=d^*\bigr].
knowledge_statements.title: Equivalent Attained Saddle Certificate

children.title: Convexified-Value Recovery Regimes
children.top_down_role: Settings where the dual value matches an associated convexified problem.

assumptions_latex: The perturbation value is \(v(u)=\inf\{f(x):x\in X,\ g(x)\leq u\}\).
The function \(v\) is proper at the perturbations used in the conjugacy calculation.
Conjugates and closures are taken in the finite-dimensional perturbation space \(\mathbb R^m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The Lagrangian dual value equals \(d^*=v^{**}(0)\), the closed-convexified perturbation value at the origin.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Perturbation-space interpretation of the dual as closed convexification.

source_refs.source_title: Semidefinite Optimization and Convex Algebraic Geometry

source_refs.locator: 5.7.1. Duality Gap in Separable Problems p. 217

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(v(u)=\inf\{f(x):x\in X,\ g(x)\leq u\}\), define \[q(\lambda)=\inf_{x\in X}\bigl(f(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}g(x)\bigr),\qquad \lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m.\] In finite-dimensional perturbation space, the conjugate representation is \[q(\lambda)=-v^*(-\lambda),\qquad d^*=\sup_{\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m}q(\lambda)=v^{**}(0).\] Thus the dual recovers the lower-semicontinuous convexified perturbation value at zero, which need not equal the original nonconvex value \(v(0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Lagrangian dual value equals the lower-semicontinuous convexified perturbation value at zero, which may differ from the original nonconvex value.
knowledge_statements.title: Convexified-Value Recovery Regimes

source_witnesses.source_title: Semidefinite Optimization and Convex Algebraic Geometry

source_witnesses.locator: 5.7.1. Duality Gap in Separable Problems p. 217

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric representation of the convexified perturbation value recovered by the Lagrangian dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a proper function \(v:\mathbb R^m\to\overline{\mathbb R}\), \[\operatorname{epi}v^{**}=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(\operatorname{epi}v),\qquad v^{**}(0)=\inf\{t:(0,t)\in\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(\operatorname{epi}v)\}.\] Thus \(v^{**}(0)\) is obtained as a limit of finite convex combinations of epigraph points whose averaged perturbations converge to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The recovered value is the height of the closed convex hull of the perturbation epigraph above the origin.
assumptions_latex: \(v:\mathbb R^m\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) is proper.
The perturbation space is finite-dimensional.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: v^{**}(0)=\inf\{t:(0,t)\in\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(\operatorname{epi}v)\}.

notation.meaning: epigraph of the perturbation value function

knowledge_statements.title: Closed-Convex-Epigraph Representation

children.title: Zero-Gap Recovery Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Structural limits beyond which value recovery is not available.

assumptions_latex: The primal value is \(p^*=v(0)\) for a proper perturbation function \(v\).
The associated Lagrangian dual value satisfies \(d^*=v^{**}(0)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Zero duality gap holds exactly when \(v(0)=v^{**}(0)\); failure of this equality is the recovery boundary.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact boundary between original-value and merely convexified-value recovery.

source_refs.locator: 5.7.1. Duality Gap in Separable Problems p. 217
5.7.2. Duality Gap in Minimax Problems p. 226

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the perturbation identities \(p^*=v(0)\) and \(d^*=v^{**}(0)\), the primal-dual gap is \[p^*-d^*=v(0)-v^{**}(0)\geq0.\] Exact primal-value recovery holds if and only if \(v(0)=v^{**}(0)\). If \(v(0)>v^{**}(0)\), the same Lagrangian dual recovers only the convexified value and has a positive duality gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zero gap occurs exactly when the perturbation value equals its closed convex envelope at zero; otherwise the Lagrangian dual recovers only the convexified value.
knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Gap Recovery Boundaries

source_witnesses.locator: 5.7.1. Duality Gap in Separable Problems p. 217
5.7.2. Duality Gap in Minimax Problems p. 226

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Zero Gap Does Not Imply Attainment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed attainment examples are mathematically sound but are not primarily owned by the boundary between original-value and convexified-value recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Zero duality gap alone need not imply primal or dual attainment. For example, \(\inf_{x\in\mathbb R}e^x=0\) is unattained, while \(\min\{x:x^2\leq0\}\) has \(p^*=d^*=0\) but its Lagrangian dual supremum is not attained by any finite multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zero value gap need not provide primal or dual attaining witnesses.
assumptions_latex: Optimal values are interpreted as extended-real infima and suprema.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p^*=d^*\not\Rightarrow\text{primal and dual attainment}.
knowledge_statements.title: Zero Gap Does Not Imply Attainment

intermediate_metadata.reason: The seed exhausts the exact boundary between original-value and merely convexified-value recovery. The proposed nonattainment examples are deferred because attainment and optimizer recovery belong primarily to the primal-recovery or a dedicated attainment scope; convexified-value geometry remains in the other sibling.

children.title: Nonconvex Duality Gaps
children.top_down_role: Persistent gaps limiting dual convexification of nonconvex models.

assumptions_latex: The base domain is the nonconvex set \(X=\{0,1\}\).
The problem is \(p^*=\min\{x:x\in X,\ \tfrac12-x\leq0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The primal value is \(p^*=1\), whereas the Lagrangian dual value is \(d^*=\tfrac12\), producing the positive gap \(p^*-d^*=\tfrac12\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the concrete finite example is certified by direct evaluation of its two feasible binary points and the resulting piecewise-affine dual function; the cited locator supports the general nonconvex duality-gap phenomenon.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A finite binary example exhibiting a strict Lagrangian duality gap.

source_refs.locator: 5.7.1. Duality Gap in Separable Problems p. 217

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the nonconvex binary problem \[p^*=\min\left\{x:x\in\{0,1\},\ \frac12-x\leq0\right\}=1.\] Its Lagrangian dual function and optimized dual value are \[q(\lambda)=\min\left\{\frac{\lambda}{2},1-\frac{\lambda}{2}\right\},\qquad \lambda\in\mathbb R_+,\qquad d^*=\sup_{\lambda\in\mathbb R_+}q(\lambda)=\frac12.\] Therefore this example has the strict gap \(p^*-d^*=\tfrac12>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This one-variable binary problem has primal value one and Lagrangian dual value one-half, giving a strict nonconvex duality gap.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Duality Gaps

source_witnesses.locator: 5.7.1. Duality Gap in Separable Problems p. 217

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value-level definition for a minimization problem and its Lagrangian dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For primal value \(p^*\) and Lagrangian dual value \(d^*=\sup_{\lambda\ge0}q(\lambda)\), the duality gap is \(p^*-d^*\) whenever that extended-real subtraction is defined. Weak duality gives \(d^*\le p^*\); a positive finite gap means \(-\infty<d^*<p^*<+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Lagrangian duality gap is the nonnegative difference between the primal infimum and dual supremum when defined.
assumptions_latex: The primal is a minimization problem.
Multipliers obey the signs required by the relaxed constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d^*\le p^*,\qquad \operatorname{gap}=p^*-d^*\ge0.
knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian Duality Gap

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Positive-Gap Obstruction to Exact Lagrangian Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-recovery consequences of a strict finite Lagrangian gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(-\infty<d^*<p^*<+\infty\), no primal-feasible \(x^*\) and dual-feasible \(\lambda^*\) can satisfy \(f(x^*)=q(\lambda^*)=p^*\). Hence no multiplier certifies the primal optimum by an exact Lagrangian lower bound, and no primal-dual pair forms a value-matching Lagrangian saddle pair, even if the two optima are separately attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive gap rules out exact multiplier certification and any value-matching Lagrangian saddle pair.
assumptions_latex: The primal and dual values are finite and satisfy \(d^*<p^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d^*<p^*\Longrightarrow\nexists(x^*,\lambda^*)\text{ feasible with }f(x^*)=q(\lambda^*)=p^*.
knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Gap Obstruction to Exact Lagrangian Recovery

children.title: Surrogate-Aggregation Relaxation Family
children.top_down_role: Relaxations formed by weighted aggregation or replacement of constraint systems.

children.title: Surrogate-Constraint Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Weighted aggregation of constraints into tractable surrogate restrictions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convexity of a surrogate set formed from real-valued convex constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be convex, let each \(g_i:X\to\mathbb R\) be convex, and let \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\setminus\{0\}\). Then \[g_\lambda=\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i g_i\] is convex, and its zero-sublevel set \[S(\lambda)=\{x\in X:g_\lambda(x)\le0\}\] is convex. It remains an outer relaxation of the original feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative sum of real-valued convex constraint functions has a convex zero-sublevel surrogate set.
assumptions_latex: X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\text{ is convex}
g_i:X\to\mathbb R\text{ is convex for every }i
\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\setminus\{0\}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: g_\lambda\text{ is convex and }S(\lambda)\text{ is convex}
knowledge_statements.title: Convexity Preservation under Nonnegative Aggregation

assumptions_latex: The original feasible region is \(F=\{x\in X:g_i(x)\le 0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\).
The multiplier satisfies \(\lambda\in\mathbb{R}_+^m\setminus\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\subseteq S(\lambda)\), so minimizing over \(S(\lambda)\) gives a valid lower bound for any minimization problem over \(F\).

notation.meaning: Surrogate feasible region for multiplier lambda

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single nonnegative weighted aggregation of inequality constraints in a minimization model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For functions \(g_i:X\to\mathbb{R}\), define the surrogate-constraint relaxation associated with \(\lambda\in\mathbb{R}_+^m\setminus\{0\}\) by
\[
S(\lambda):=\left\{x\in X:\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i g_i(x)\le 0\right\}.
\]
Every \(x\in F\) satisfies the aggregated inequality because each term \(\lambda_i g_i(x)\) is nonpositive. Hence \(F\subseteq S(\lambda)\). For an objective \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\), it follows that
\[
\inf_{x\in S(\lambda)}f(x)\le \inf_{x\in F}f(x).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative weighted sum of valid inequalities yields one necessary constraint. Replacing all original inequalities by it enlarges the feasible set and gives a valid minimization lower bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Surrogate-Constraint Relaxations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and lower-bound direction are mathematically correct, and the content kind fits the leaf, but no inspectable source supports the surrogate-relaxation terminology and result. The statement also includes a proof sentence rather than only the knowledge statement.

children.title: Aggregation Multiplier-Strength Tradeoff
children.top_down_role: Dependence of relaxation quality on aggregation structure and weights.

children.title: Aggregation-Structure Strength
children.top_down_role: Relaxation quality attributable to the selected aggregation structure.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Partition Refinement Alone Does Not Imply Dominance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incomparability of fine and coarse partitions with incompatible aggregate coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\mathbb R^2\), \(g_1(x,y)=x\), \(g_2(x,y)=y\), and \(g_3(x,y)=0\). For \(\mathcal P=\{\{1,2\},\{3\}\}\), retain \(g_1+g_2\le0\) and \(g_3\le0\), so \[S_{\mathcal P}=\{(x,y):x+y\le0\}.\] For \(\mathcal Q=\{\{1,2,3\}\}\), retain \(g_1+2g_2+g_3\le0\), so \[S_{\mathcal Q}=\{(x,y):x+2y\le0\}.\] Neither set contains the other. Therefore partition refinement without coefficient compatibility does not establish a strength ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fine and coarse aggregation structures can be incomparable when their coefficient patterns are incompatible.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal P\text{ refines }\mathcal Q
\text{All displayed block multipliers are nonnegative and nonzero}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S_{\mathcal P}\nsubseteq S_{\mathcal Q}\quad\text{and}\quad S_{\mathcal Q}\nsubseteq S_{\mathcal P}

notation.meaning: Feasible sets of the retained aggregates

knowledge_statements.title: Partition Refinement Alone Does Not Imply Dominance

assumptions_latex: Let \(g_i(x)\le 0\), \(i=1,\ldots,m\), be the original inequalities.
Let \(\mathcal P\) and \(\mathcal Q\) be partitions of \(\{1,\ldots,m\}\), with \(\mathcal P\) refining \(\mathcal Q\).
Every block multiplier is nonnegative and nonzero on its block.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: When each coarse aggregate is a nonnegative combination of fine aggregates, \(S_{\mathcal P}\subseteq S_{\mathcal Q}\); finer aggregation structure is therefore at least as strong.

notation.meaning: Feasible set retaining one aggregate per partition block

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strength ordering induced by retaining several structured aggregates instead of one global aggregate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each \(B\in\mathcal P\), retain the inequality \(\sum_{i\in B}\lambda_i^B g_i(x)\le 0\), and denote their common feasible set by \(S_{\mathcal P}\). Suppose every \(C\in\mathcal Q\) has a coarse aggregate expressible as
\[
\sum_{i\in C}\mu_i^C g_i(x)=\sum_{B\subseteq C,\,B\in\mathcal P}\alpha_B^C\sum_{i\in B}\lambda_i^B g_i(x),
\qquad \alpha_B^C\ge 0.
\]
Then every point satisfying all fine-block aggregates satisfies every coarse-block aggregate. Consequently,
\[
S_{\mathcal P}\subseteq S_{\mathcal Q}.
\]
Thus preserving more independently enforced aggregation blocks cannot weaken this relaxation under the stated conic-combination compatibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finer family of separately enforced aggregates is at least as strong as a coarser family whenever each coarse aggregate is a nonnegative combination of the finer ones.
knowledge_statements.title: Aggregation-Structure Strength

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditional inclusion is correct under the stated conic-combination compatibility, and property is an appropriate kind. An authoritative source is required for this aggregation-structure strength formulation.

children.title: Multiplier Selection Regimes
children.top_down_role: Structural regimes for choosing aggregation weights.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Attainment conditions for normalized best-bound selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Lambda\) be a nonempty compact normalized multiplier set. If \(v:\Lambda\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) is upper semicontinuous and \(\sup_{\lambda\in\Lambda}v(\lambda)<+\infty\), then some \(\lambda^\star\in\Lambda\) satisfies \[v(\lambda^\star)=\max_{\lambda\in\Lambda}v(\lambda).\] Without compactness or upper semicontinuity, only a maximizing sequence may exist.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compactness and upper semicontinuity guarantee an attained best-bound multiplier; otherwise the supremum may be unattained.
assumptions_latex: \varnothing\ne\Lambda\text{ is compact}
v\text{ is upper semicontinuous on }\Lambda
\sup_{\lambda\in\Lambda}v(\lambda)<+\infty
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname*{argmax}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}v(\lambda)\ne\varnothing
knowledge_statements.title: Existence of a Best-Bound Multiplier

assumptions_latex: For each admissible \(\lambda\), the surrogate problem has value \(v(\lambda)=\inf\{f(x):x\in S(\lambda)\}\).
The admissible multiplier set \(\Lambda\subseteq\mathbb{R}_+^m\setminus\{0\}\) is normalized to remove positive scaling.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Fixed, best-bound, and adaptive regimes respectively use a prescribed multiplier, optimize \(v\) over \(\Lambda\), or update multipliers from information produced by previously solved surrogate problems.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical fixed, bound-optimizing, and adaptive choices for normalized surrogate multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(\Lambda\), multiplier selection may follow one of three precise regimes. In the fixed regime, choose a prescribed \(\bar\lambda\in\Lambda\), solve the corresponding surrogate problem, and output \(v(\bar\lambda)\). In the best-bound regime, solve
\[
\sup_{\lambda\in\Lambda}v(\lambda)
\]
and output an optimizer or a maximizing sequence. In an adaptive regime, initialize \(\lambda^0\in\Lambda\); after solving the surrogate problem at iteration \(k\), form diagnostic information \(d^k\), update
\[
\lambda^{k+1}=T_k(\lambda^k,d^k)\in\Lambda,
\]
and stop when a prescribed bound-improvement, stationarity, or iteration criterion is met.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multipliers may be prescribed, chosen to maximize the surrogate bound, or updated iteratively from earlier surrogate solutions under an explicit normalization and stopping rule.
knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier Selection Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fixed and best-bound regimes are intelligible, but the claimed three-regime taxonomy and generic adaptive update require a source. The leaf describes selection regimes rather than one definite algorithm, so the algorithm kind also needs source-backed justification.

children.title: Strength Sensitivity to Multipliers
children.top_down_role: Variation in relaxation quality across multiplier choices.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Normalized Multipliers Can Produce Incomparable Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonnested surrogate halfspaces from strictly positive normalized multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\mathbb R^2\), \(g_1(x)=x_1\), and \(g_2(x)=x_2\). For \[\lambda=(3/4,1/4),\qquad\mu=(1/4,3/4),\] both multipliers are strictly positive and simplex-normalized. Their surrogate sets are \[S(\lambda)=\{x:3x_1+x_2\le0\},\qquad S(\mu)=\{x:x_1+3x_2\le0\}.\] The point \((-1,1)\) belongs only to \(S(\lambda)\), while \((1,-1)\) belongs only to \(S(\mu)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strictly positive normalized multipliers can generate incomparable surrogate halfspaces.
assumptions_latex: S(\eta)=\{x\in X:\eta_1g_1(x)+\eta_2g_2(x)\le0\}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S(\lambda)\nsubseteq S(\mu)\quad\text{and}\quad S(\mu)\nsubseteq S(\lambda)

notation.meaning: Surrogate feasible set generated by eta

knowledge_statements.title: Normalized Multipliers Can Produce Incomparable Relaxations

assumptions_latex: The surrogate set is \(S(\lambda)=\{x\in X:\lambda^{\mathsf T}g(x)\le 0\}\).
Multipliers lie in \(\mathbb{R}_+^m\setminus\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The surrogate set and its optimization bound are invariant under positive rescaling of \(\lambda\), but need not be monotone under componentwise changes of normalized multipliers.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scale invariance and directional, generally nonmonotone dependence on multiplier ratios.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(t>0\),
\[
S(t\lambda)=\{x\in X:t\lambda^{\mathsf T}g(x)\le 0\}=S(\lambda),
\]
and therefore \(v(t\lambda)=v(\lambda)\) whenever \(v(\lambda):=\inf_{x\in S(\lambda)}f(x)\) is defined. Thus strength depends only on the ray generated by \(\lambda\), permitting a normalization such as \(\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}\lambda=1\). In contrast, for two normalized vectors \(\lambda\) and \(\mu\), neither \(S(\lambda)\subseteq S(\mu)\) nor \(S(\mu)\subseteq S(\lambda)\) follows merely from their components; a change in multiplier ratios rotates the aggregated inequality and can strengthen some directions while weakening others.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Only multiplier ratios matter: positive scaling changes nothing. Changing normalized ratios generally rotates the aggregate, so relaxation strength has no universal componentwise monotonicity.
knowledge_statements.title: Strength Sensitivity to Multipliers

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Positive-scale invariance is correct. The assertion about componentwise changes between normalized multipliers is imprecise because componentwise ordering under a fixed simplex normalization forces equality; a source or a more exact sensitivity formulation is needed.

children.title: Aggregation Information Loss
children.top_down_role: Weakness caused by discarding individual constraint geometry.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Recovery from the Full Aggregate Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: No-loss boundary obtained by retaining all coordinate aggregates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\{x\in X:g_i(x)\le 0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\) and \(S(\lambda)=\{x\in X:\lambda^{\mathsf T}g(x)\le 0\}\). Then \[F=\bigcap_{\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\setminus\{0\}}S(\lambda)=\bigcap_{i=1}^mS(e_i).\] Thus loss arises from discarding aggregates, while the coordinate aggregates recover every original inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: All nonnegative aggregates, or just the coordinate aggregates, recover the original constraint system exactly.
assumptions_latex: g_i:X\to\mathbb R\quad(i=1,\ldots,m)
e_i\text{ is the }i\text{-th coordinate vector}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F=\bigcap_{\lambda\ge0,\lambda\ne0}S(\lambda)=\bigcap_{i=1}^mS(e_i)

notation.meaning: Feasible set defined by one aggregate

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Recovery from the Full Aggregate Family

assumptions_latex: The variable is \(x\in\mathbb{R}\).
The original system is \(x\le 0\) and \(-x\le 0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: With equal positive multipliers, aggregation replaces the singleton feasible set \(\{0\}\) by all of \(\mathbb{R}\), demonstrating complete loss of the opposing constraint geometry.
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete cancellation example showing maximal information loss under one surrogate aggregate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g_1(x)=x\) and \(g_2(x)=-x\). The original feasible set is
\[
F=\{x\in\mathbb{R}:x\le 0,\ -x\le 0\}=\{0\}.
\]
Choose \(\lambda=(1,1)\). The surrogate inequality is
\[
\lambda_1g_1(x)+\lambda_2g_2(x)=x-x=0\le 0,
\]
which holds for every \(x\in\mathbb{R}\). Hence \(S(\lambda)=\mathbb{R}\), strictly containing \(F\). Aggregation has discarded the fact that the two inequalities constrain opposite directions, and their weighted cancellation makes the surrogate constraint vacuous.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The constraints x at most zero and minus x at most zero force x to zero, but equal-weight aggregation cancels them and admits every real number.
knowledge_statements.title: Aggregation Information Loss

children.title: Decomposition Master-Reformulation Interface
children.top_down_role: Placement of separability, pricing, and master formulations without duplicating decomposition algorithms.

children.title: Block-Scenario Decomposition Interface
children.top_down_role: Relaxation structures exposing block, scenario, commodity, or network separability.

children.title: Block Decomposition Interface
children.top_down_role: Relaxation structures exposing separability across model blocks.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational interface supplied by an exactly separable Lagrangian subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed \(\pi\), define \(q_b(\pi)=\inf_{x_b\in X_b}\{f_b(x_b)+\pi^{\mathsf T}A_bx_b\}\). The block values may be evaluated independently and \(q(\pi)=-\pi^{\mathsf T}a+\sum_bq_b(\pi)\). If every infimum is attained at \(x_b(\pi)\), then \(\sum_bA_bx_b(\pi)-a\in\partial^+q(\pi)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent block oracles assemble the dual value, and attained block solutions yield the aggregate residual as a dual supergradient.
assumptions_latex: The retained Lagrangian subproblem is block separable.
Each reported block value is its true infimum; the supergradient assertion additionally requires attainment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: q(\pi)=-\pi^{\mathsf T}a+\sum_bq_b(\pi),\qquad \sum_bA_bx_b(\pi)-a\in\partial^+q(\pi).
knowledge_statements.title: Parallel Block-Oracle Evaluation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sufficient Structural Criterion for Block Separability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A checkable structural condition ensuring that partial dualization exposes independent block subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\prod_{b=1}^B X_b\) and \(L(x,\pi)=\sum_b f_b(x_b)+\pi^{\mathsf T}(\sum_bA_bx_b-a)\). If every retained objective and constraint term is block-local, then \[\inf_{x\in X}L(x,\pi)=-\pi^{\mathsf T}a+\sum_b\inf_{x_b\in X_b}\bigl(f_b(x_b)+\pi^{\mathsf T}A_bx_b\bigr).\] A retained nonredundant cross-block constraint or nonseparable term generally prevents this decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Cartesian retained domain with only block-local terms guarantees independent Lagrangian block subproblems; retained cross-block terms generally destroy that structure.
assumptions_latex: \(X_b\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_b}\) is nonempty for every \(b\).
\(A_b:\mathbb R^{n_b}\to\mathbb R^m\) and \(a,\pi\in\mathbb R^m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \inf_{x\in X}L(x,\pi)=-\pi^{\mathsf T}a+\sum_b\inf_{x_b\in X_b}(f_b(x_b)+\pi^{\mathsf T}A_bx_b).

notation.meaning: Retained feasible set of block b
Block map into the common coupling space

knowledge_statements.title: Sufficient Structural Criterion for Block Separability

assumptions_latex: Variables are partitioned as \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_B)\) with \(x_b\in X_b\).
The objective is separable and the only cross-block restriction is \(\sum_{b=1}^B A_bx_b=a\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dualizing the coupling equation produces a dual function equal to a constant plus a sum of independent block value functions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lagrangian interface exposing independent block subproblems through coupling-row multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider
\[
\inf\left\{\sum_{b=1}^B f_b(x_b):x_b\in X_b,\ \sum_{b=1}^B A_bx_b=a\right\}.
\]
For a multiplier \(\pi\), the Lagrangian is
\[
L(x,\pi)=-\pi^{\mathsf T}a+\sum_{b=1}^B\left(f_b(x_b)+\pi^{\mathsf T}A_bx_b\right).
\]
Consequently its dual function decomposes as
\[
q(\pi)=-\pi^{\mathsf T}a+\sum_{b=1}^B\inf_{x_b\in X_b}\left(f_b(x_b)+\pi^{\mathsf T}A_bx_b\right).
\]
Thus a master mechanism may coordinate the shared multiplier while each block evaluates its contribution independently.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dualizing the sole cross-block equation makes the Lagrangian value a sum of independent block values, with a master mechanism coordinating the common multiplier.
knowledge_statements.title: Block Decomposition Interface

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The separable Lagrangian representation is standard and matches the block interface, but no relevant source is cited. The spaces and compatible dimensions of the block variables, coupling maps, right-hand side, and multiplier are not explicit.

children.title: Scenario Decomposition Interface
children.top_down_role: Relaxation structures exposing separability across scenarios.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical aggregation variants for communicating finite-scenario recourse cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(Q_\omega(x)\ge\alpha_{\omega k}+\beta_{\omega k}^{\mathsf T}x\), a multicut master imposes \(\eta_\omega\ge\alpha_{\omega k}+\beta_{\omega k}^{\mathsf T}x\) separately, whereas a single-cut master imposes \(\eta\ge\sum_\omega p_\omega(\alpha_{\omega k}+\beta_{\omega k}^{\mathsf T}x)\). For identical generated scenario cuts, \[\sum_\omega p_\omega\max_k(\alpha_{\omega k}+\beta_{\omega k}^{\mathsf T}x)\ge\max_k\sum_\omega p_\omega(\alpha_{\omega k}+\beta_{\omega k}^{\mathsf T}x),\] so the multicut lower approximation is at least as strong for minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scenario cuts may be retained separately or aggregated; retaining them separately gives an expected-recourse lower approximation at least as strong.
assumptions_latex: Every scenario cut is a valid global lower bound for \(Q_\omega\).
The master minimizes probability-weighted recourse.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The multicut master bound is at least the corresponding single-cut master bound.}
knowledge_statements.title: Single-Cut and Multicut Scenario Masters

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of simple probability-weighted scenario assembly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The identity \(Q(x)=\sum_\omega p_\omega Q_\omega(x)\) describes fixed probability-weighted expectation with scenario-local recourse. It is not, in general, a complete separable representation when probabilities depend on decisions, admissible probability weights are coupled by ambiguity constraints, a nonlinear risk functional replaces expectation, or retained constraints jointly contain recourse variables from multiple scenarios.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Decision-dependent probabilities, coupled ambiguity, nonlinear risk, or cross-scenario recourse constraints invalidate simple fixed-weight scenario assembly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Cross-scenario coupling or nonlinear aggregation need not equal }\sum_\omega p_\omega Q_\omega(x)\text{ for fixed }p_\omega.
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Expectation Separability Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-scenario two-stage structure underlying independent recourse evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[\min_{x\in X,y_\omega}\left\{c^{\mathsf T}x+\sum_{\omega\in\Omega}p_\omega d_\omega^{\mathsf T}y_\omega:W_\omega y_\omega=h_\omega-T_\omega x,\ y_\omega\in Y_\omega\right\}.\] Once \(x\) is fixed, distinct recourse variables \(y_\omega\) occur in independent feasible sets and objectives. The intended cross-scenario coupling is the common first-stage decision, equivalently nonanticipativity of \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixing the common first-stage decision separates the finite-scenario extensive form into independent recourse problems.
assumptions_latex: \(\Omega\) is finite, \(p_\omega>0\), and \(\sum_\omega p_\omega=1\).
No retained constraint contains recourse variables from two distinct scenarios.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Q(x)=\sum_{\omega\in\Omega}p_\omega Q_\omega(x)\text{ with independently evaluable }Q_\omega(x).
knowledge_statements.title: Extensive-Form Scenario Separability

assumptions_latex: A finite scenario set \(\Omega\) has probabilities \(p_\omega>0\) summing to one.
For fixed first-stage decision \(x\), scenario recourse values \(Q_\omega(x)\) are independently evaluable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The expected recourse value and its valid affine lower approximations are assembled by probability-weighted aggregation of scenario contributions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-scenario interface between independent recourse evaluations and an expected-value master model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the expected recourse function by
\[
Q(x)=\sum_{\omega\in\Omega}p_\omega Q_\omega(x).
\]
If scenario \(\omega\) supplies a valid affine lower bound
\[
Q_\omega(x)\ge \alpha_\omega+\beta_\omega^{\mathsf T}x,
\]
then probability-weighted aggregation gives the valid master inequality
\[
Q(x)\ge \sum_{\omega\in\Omega}p_\omega\alpha_\omega+
\left(\sum_{\omega\in\Omega}p_\omega\beta_\omega\right)^{\mathsf T}x.
\]
Scenario decomposition therefore evaluates or separates each \(Q_\omega\) independently and communicates only weighted values, subgradients, or cuts to the shared first-stage master.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent scenario recourse values and cuts combine through probability weights to form the expected recourse function and valid master inequalities.
knowledge_statements.title: Scenario Decomposition Interface

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Probability-weighted aggregation of valid scenario lower bounds is correct and representation fits the leaf. A stochastic-decomposition source is absent, and the domain and dimension of the first-stage variable and affine coefficients are not introduced explicitly.

children.title: Cross-Block Coupling Interface
children.top_down_role: Residual coupling that links otherwise separable components.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural identification of independent subsystems within a sparse coupling equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Form a bipartite graph with block vertices \(b\), coupling-row vertices \(i\), and edge \((b,i)\) when row \(i\) of \(A_b\) is structurally nonzero. Simultaneous row and block permutation separates \(\sum_bA_bx_b=a\) into one independent subsystem per connected component. A component containing multiple blocks is irreducibly coupled relative to this sparsity pattern.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Connected components of the block-row incidence graph identify the independent coupling subsystems.
assumptions_latex: Cross-block interaction is represented by \(\sum_bA_bx_b=a\).
Edges are determined by structural, rather than accidental numerical, nonzeros.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_bA_bx_b=a\text{ is permutable into one subsystem per connected component.}
knowledge_statements.title: Coupling-Graph Component Decomposition

assumptions_latex: Each block variable satisfies \(x_b\in X_b\).
Cross-block interaction is represented by \(\sum_{b=1}^B A_bx_b=a\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A shared multiplier converts coupling into block-local linear terms, while primal feasibility is recovered only when the aggregate residual vanishes.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual coordination of otherwise independent blocks through a shared coupling residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
r(x):=\sum_{b=1}^B A_bx_b-a.
\]
Attaching multiplier \(\pi\) to \(r(x)=0\) adds
\[
\pi^{\mathsf T}r(x)=-\pi^{\mathsf T}a+
\sum_{b=1}^B\pi^{\mathsf T}A_bx_b
\]
to the separable objective. Hence every block receives the same coordinating price \(\pi\) through its local term \(\pi^{\mathsf T}A_bx_b\). The dualized subproblems may be solved independently, but their combined solution is feasible for the original coupling system exactly when \(r(x)=0\). A nonzero residual is therefore the interface signal requiring master or multiplier adjustment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A common price turns cross-block coupling into local linear terms. Independent block solutions recover original feasibility exactly when their combined coupling residual is zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Block Coupling Interface

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The residual and shared-price interface is mathematically sound, but it lacks a source and explicit compatible vector-space dimensions. The statement is primarily a decomposition representation/property; classifying it as duality requires source-backed justification.

children.title: Column-Generation Dantzig-Wolfe Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Links between Lagrangian pricing, convexification of subproblem sets, and extended master formulations.

children.title: Column-Generation Pricing Interface
children.top_down_role: Connection between relaxation pricing and generated master columns.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Full-master objective guarantee from rigorous block pricing tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an optimal restricted-master dual solution have block pricing minima \(z_b\), and suppose rigorous bounds give \(z_b\ge-\varepsilon_b\). If the full master has one unit convexity equation per block, then \[0\le v_{\mathrm{RMP}}-v_{\mathrm{MP}}\le\sum_b\varepsilon_b.\] Exact nonnegative pricing minima therefore certify exact full-master optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certified pricing lower bounds give an additive full-master optimality guarantee; exact nonnegative reduced costs give exact optimality.
assumptions_latex: The full master has \(\sum_v\theta_{bv}=1\) for each block.
The restricted master is feasible and solved exactly.
Each bound \(z_b\ge-\varepsilon_b\) is rigorous with \(\varepsilon_b\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0\le v_{\mathrm{RMP}}-v_{\mathrm{MP}}\le\sum_b\varepsilon_b.
knowledge_statements.title: Certified Approximate-Pricing Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite termination bound for exact column generation on a finite full master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the full master has finitely many columns, every restricted master and pricing problem is solved exactly, and each nonterminal iteration adds at least one previously absent negative-reduced-cost column, then column generation terminates at a full-master optimum after at most as many strict column-addition iterations as there were initially omitted columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact column generation terminates finitely on a finite column set when each nonterminal iteration adds a new improving column.
assumptions_latex: The full master contains finitely many distinct columns.
Restricted-master and pricing solves are exact.
A previously absent negative-reduced-cost column is added whenever one exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{add}}\le N_{\mathrm{initially\ omitted\ columns}}.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Column-Generation Termination

assumptions_latex: The restricted master is a minimization linear program with dual multipliers \(\pi\) on linking rows and \(\sigma_b\) on block convexity rows.
A candidate block column \(v\in V_b\) has cost \(c_b^{\mathsf T}v\) and linking vector \(A_bv\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A column with negative reduced cost improves the dual feasibility test; if every block pricing minimum is nonnegative, no omitted column violates the current dual solution.

notation.meaning: Convexity-row dual multiplier for block b

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced-cost oracle connecting a restricted master to block column generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given an optimal restricted-master dual pair \((\pi,\sigma_b)\), solve for each block
\[
z_b:=\min_{v\in V_b}\left(c_b^{\mathsf T}v-\pi^{\mathsf T}A_bv-\sigma_b\right).
\]
Initialize with any master-feasible column set. At an iteration, add to the restricted master any minimizing column with \(z_b<0\), reoptimize the master, and repeat. Stop when \(z_b\ge 0\) for every block, subject to the chosen numerical tolerance. At termination, all omitted-column reduced-cost inequalities are satisfied, so the current restricted-master solution is optimal for the full linear master. If artificial columns are used initially, feasibility also requires that their final total weight be zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pricing minimizes reduced cost over each block. Negative reduced cost adds a column; nonnegative minima for all blocks certify optimality of the full linear master.
knowledge_statements.title: Column-Generation Pricing Interface

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The pricing algorithm and nonnegative-reduced-cost optimality test are standard, but no source is supplied. The conclusion's phrase that a negative reduced-cost column improves dual feasibility is inaccurate: such a column exposes violation of the current full-master dual constraints and may improve the primal restricted-master objective.

children.title: Dantzig–Wolfe Master Reformulation
children.top_down_role: Extended master representations built from subproblem-set columns.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exactness boundary for point-and-ray master representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(X_b\) has nonzero lineality, a point-and-one-sided-extreme-ray list need not generate \(X_b\). An exact generator master must also represent a basis of \(\operatorname{lin}(X_b)\) with free coefficients, or represent every lineality direction by two opposite nonnegative rays. Omitting required recession or lineality generators can make the projected master strictly smaller than the original block set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unbounded masters require all recession and lineality generators; omitting them destroys projection equivalence.
assumptions_latex: \(X_b\) is a nonempty polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{lin}(X_b)\ne\{0\}\Longrightarrow\text{an exact generator master must represent lineality.}
knowledge_statements.title: Lineality and Missing-Generator Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unbounded pointed-polyhedral extension of the bounded extreme-point master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X_b=\operatorname{conv}(V_b)+\operatorname{cone}(R_b)\) be a nonempty pointed polyhedron with finite point and recession-ray generators. Then \[x_b=\sum_{v\in V_b}v\theta_{bv}+\sum_{r\in R_b}r\mu_{br},\qquad \theta_{bv},\mu_{br}\ge0,\quad\sum_v\theta_{bv}=1.\] Substitution into a block-angular linear program gives an equivalent master with point columns of convexity weight one and ray columns of convexity weight zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An equivalent master for a pointed unbounded block polyhedron uses both point and recession-ray columns.
assumptions_latex: Each \(X_b\) is a nonempty pointed polyhedron with finite generator sets \(V_b,R_b\).
The objective and linking constraints are linear.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{proj}_x(\text{point-and-ray master})=\{x:x_b\in X_b,\ \sum_bA_bx_b=a\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Point-and-Ray Dantzig–Wolfe Master

assumptions_latex: Each nonempty bounded polyhedron \(X_b\) has extreme-point set \(V_b\).
The original block-angular model has linking equation \(\sum_b A_bx_b=a\) and linear cost \(\sum_b c_b^{\mathsf T}x_b\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Replacing every block point by a convex combination of its extreme points yields an equivalent master linear program.

notation.meaning: Extreme points of block polyhedron b
Weight assigned to extreme point v of block b

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extreme-point form for bounded block polyhedra in a block-angular linear program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Since \(X_b=\operatorname{conv}(V_b)\), every \(x_b\in X_b\) can be written as \(x_b=\sum_{v\in V_b}v\theta_{bv}\), where \(\theta_{bv}\ge 0\) and \(\sum_{v\in V_b}\theta_{bv}=1\). Substitution gives the Dantzig--Wolfe master
\[
\min_{\theta\ge 0}\ \sum_b\sum_{v\in V_b}c_b^{\mathsf T}v\theta_{bv}
\]
subject to
\[
\sum_b\sum_{v\in V_b}A_bv\theta_{bv}=a,
\qquad
\sum_{v\in V_b}\theta_{bv}=1\quad\text{for every }b.
\]
The original and master formulations have identical feasible images in the \(x\)-space and identical objective values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each bounded block point is represented as a convex combination of block extreme points, producing an equivalent linear master with linking and convexity equations.
knowledge_statements.title: Dantzig–Wolfe Master Reformulation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: For nonempty bounded block polyhedra, the extreme-point master representation and equivalence claim are correct, and representation is the appropriate kind. A specific Dantzig–Wolfe source and locator are still required.

children.title: Pricing-to-Convexification Link
children.top_down_role: Relationship between subproblem pricing and convexified master representations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information lost when a nonconvex block is accessed only through linear pricing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Because linear pricing values are closed-convex-hull invariant, an oracle returning only exact linear optimization values identifies at most \(\operatorname{clconv}X\). It cannot distinguish sets with the same closed convex hull, determine which convexified points were originally feasible, or certify recovery of an original nonconvex point from an arbitrary master convex combination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linear pricing exposes the closed convex hull but not the original nonconvex membership information lost by convexification.
assumptions_latex: The oracle returns only values of linear optimization problems.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{clconv}X=\operatorname{clconv}Y\Longrightarrow\inf_Xd^{\mathsf T}x=\inf_Yd^{\mathsf T}x\quad\forall d.
knowledge_statements.title: Pricing-Oracle Information Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric reason that linear pricing operates on the block convexification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every nonempty \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and \(d\in\mathbb R^n\), \[\inf_{x\in X}d^{\mathsf T}x=\inf_{x\in\operatorname{conv}X}d^{\mathsf T}x=\inf_{x\in\operatorname{clconv}X}d^{\mathsf T}x,\] with equality in the extended-real sense. Thus linear pricing values cannot distinguish a set from its closed convex hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linear pricing has the same value over a set, its convex hull, and its closed convex hull.
assumptions_latex: \(X\ne\varnothing\).
Pricing uses a finite-valued linear functional.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \inf_Xd^{\mathsf T}x=\inf_{\operatorname{conv}X}d^{\mathsf T}x=\inf_{\operatorname{clconv}X}d^{\mathsf T}x.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear Pricing Is Closed-Convex-Hull Invariant

assumptions_latex: The block set \(X_b\) is a nonempty polyhedron represented in the master through its extreme points and, when needed, extreme rays.
Pricing optimizes the current reduced-cost linear functional over \(X_b\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Pricing either exposes a missing generator of the block convex hull or certifies that the current master dual inequality is valid over the entire block set.

notation.meaning: Current reduced-cost coefficient for block b

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pricing as separation over the generators of a block convexification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(d_b:=c_b-A_b^{\mathsf T}\pi\). The pricing value is
\[
\phi_b:=\inf_{x_b\in X_b}d_b^{\mathsf T}x_b-\sigma_b.
\]
If \(\phi_b<0\) and the infimum is attained at an extreme point, that point is a generator of \(\operatorname{conv}(X_b)\) whose master column violates the current reduced-cost inequality. If the problem is unbounded below along an extreme ray, the corresponding ray column is missing. If \(\phi_b\ge 0\), then
\[
d_b^{\mathsf T}x_b\ge\sigma_b\quad\text{for every }x_b\in X_b,
\]
which certifies validity over the entire block convexification, including all unenumerated generators.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pricing separates the current dual inequality over a block: it returns a missing extreme point or ray, or certifies validity over the full block convexification.
knowledge_statements.title: Pricing-to-Convexification Link

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The pricing certificate is correct for a polyhedron admitting the stated point-and-ray generator representation, but the treatment of unboundedness and extreme rays needs an authoritative source and careful exclusion or handling of lineality. Certificate is an appropriate content kind.

children.title: Benders Value-Function Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Links between projection, value-function approximation, and master-space reformulation.

children.title: Benders Projection Interface
children.top_down_role: Projection structures supporting master-space reformulation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Benders Feasibility Cuts from Alternative-System Rays
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection certificate when linear recourse may be infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(S(x)=\{y\ge0:Wy\ge h-Tx\}\), the theorem of alternatives gives \[S(x)\ne\varnothing\iff r^{\mathsf T}(h-Tx)\le0\quad\forall r\in R:=\{r\ge0:W^{\mathsf T}r\le0\}.\] Because \(R\) is polyhedral, it suffices to use its extreme rays. If \(r^{\mathsf T}(h-T\bar x)>0\), then \(r\) certifies infeasibility at \(\bar x\) and yields the Benders feasibility cut \(r^{\mathsf T}(h-Tx)\le0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternative-system rays characterize the projected recourse domain and generate Benders feasibility cuts.
assumptions_latex: The recourse constraints are \(Wy\ge h-Tx\) and \(y\ge0\).
All data are finite-dimensional.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S(x)\ne\varnothing\iff r^{\mathsf T}(h-Tx)\le0\ \forall r\in R.
knowledge_statements.title: Benders Feasibility Cuts from Alternative-System Rays

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating domain feasibility from a finite projected value function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Feasibility of \(S(x)\) does not imply finiteness of \(Q(x)=\inf\{q^{\mathsf T}y:y\in S(x)\}\). If \(d\ge0\), \(Wd\ge0\), and \(q^{\mathsf T}d<0\), then every nonempty \(S(x)\) has \(Q(x)=-\infty\). An ordinary finite epigraph master and its optimality cuts therefore require exclusion of such improving recession directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible recourse problem may be unbounded below; ordinary Benders optimality cuts require finite recourse values.
assumptions_latex: \(S(x)\ne\varnothing\) at the master point considered.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d\ge0,\ Wd\ge0,\ q^{\mathsf T}d<0\implies Q(x)=-\infty.
knowledge_statements.title: Unbounded-Recourse Boundary

assumptions_latex: For each master point \(x\in X\), the subproblem value is \(Q(x)=\inf\{q^{\mathsf T}y:Wy\ge h-Tx,\ y\ge 0\}\).
The subproblem is feasible and has a finite value for every \(x\in X\).
Strong linear-programming duality holds for each subproblem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Projecting out \(y\) yields the epigraph of \(Q\), represented by Benders inequalities indexed by dual-feasible multipliers.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear Benders optimality cuts as an exact projected epigraph representation under complete recourse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The dual feasible region is
\[
U:=\{u\ge 0:W^{\mathsf T}u\le q\}.
\]
By strong duality,
\[
Q(x)=\sup_{u\in U}u^{\mathsf T}(h-Tx).
\]
Therefore the projection of
\[
\{(x,y,\eta):x\in X,\ Wy\ge h-Tx,\ y\ge 0,\ \eta\ge q^{\mathsf T}y\}
\]
onto the \((x,\eta)\)-space is
\[
\{(x,\eta):x\in X,\ \eta\ge u^{\mathsf T}(h-Tx)\ \text{for every }u\in U\}.
\]
When \(U\) is polyhedral, it suffices to impose the inequalities associated with its extreme points; these are the Benders optimality cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under feasible finite recourse, eliminating subproblem variables represents the value-function epigraph by all dual-generated Benders optimality cuts in master space.
knowledge_statements.title: Benders Projection Interface

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The LP dual and projected epigraph formulas are correct under the stated feasible finite-recourse and strong-duality assumptions, and representation fits the leaf. A Benders source is absent; the final reduction to extreme points also needs its polyhedral attainment conditions explicitly supported.

children.title: Value-Function Approximation
children.top_down_role: Master representations based on approximating projected value functions.

assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(Y\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m\) are nonempty convex sets, and \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) is proper, closed, and convex.
For each \(y\in Y\), the subproblem is \(v(y)=\inf\{f(x):x\in X,\ Ax+By=b\}\).
Each retained dual solution is feasible for the Lagrange dual of its corresponding subproblem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat v_T(y)\leq v(y)\) for every \(y\in Y\), and equality holds at any sampled point whose subproblem admits strong duality and whose optimal dual solution is retained.

notation.meaning: Finite maximum of dual affine minorants.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite dual-cut approximation of a convex subproblem value function.

source_refs.source_title: Semidefinite Optimization and Convex Algebraic Geometry

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For retained dual-feasible multipliers \(\lambda^1,\ldots,\lambda^T\), define the associated affine dual bounds \(\ell_t(y)=(\lambda^t)^{\mathsf T}(b-By)+\inf_{x\in X}\bigl(f(x)-(\lambda^t)^{\mathsf T}Ax\bigr)\). The Benders value-function approximation is \[\widehat v_T(y)=\max_{1\leq t\leq T}\ell_t(y).\] Weak duality gives \(\ell_t(y)\leq v(y)\), hence \(\widehat v_T\leq v\). If strong duality holds at a sampled \(y^t\) and \(\lambda^t\) is dual-optimal there, then \(\widehat v_T(y^t)=v(y^t)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite maximum of dual affine cuts underestimates the convex subproblem value function and interpolates sampled points whenever an optimal dual multiplier is retained.
knowledge_statements.title: Value-Function Approximation

source_witnesses.source_title: Semidefinite Optimization and Convex Algebraic Geometry

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between a valid minorant and an exact supporting cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A dual-feasible multiplier generates a valid affine minorant \(\ell\le v\), but without dual optimality it need not interpolate the sampled value. If the multiplier is not dual feasible, the affine function need not minorize \(v\) and can invalidate the master lower bound. Thus \[\text{dual feasibility}\Rightarrow\ell\le v,\qquad\text{dual optimality plus strong duality}\Rightarrow\ell(\bar y)=v(\bar y).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual feasibility guarantees cut validity; dual optimality and strong duality are additionally required for interpolation.
assumptions_latex: \(\ell\) is constructed from a candidate dual multiplier at \(\bar y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{dual feasible}\Rightarrow\ell\le v;\quad\text{dual optimal and strong duality}\Rightarrow\ell(\bar y)=v(\bar y).
knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier Validity and Interpolation Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Supporting-hyperplane interpretation of an exact Benders cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(v(y)=\sup_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\{a(\lambda)-\langle B^{\mathsf T}\lambda,y\rangle\}\), strong duality holds at \(\bar y\), and \(\bar\lambda\) attains the supremum there. Then \(-B^{\mathsf T}\bar\lambda\in\partial v(\bar y)\), and \[v(y)\ge v(\bar y)+\langle-B^{\mathsf T}\bar\lambda,y-\bar y\rangle.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An optimal subproblem dual multiplier gives a subgradient and supporting affine cut of the convex value function.
assumptions_latex: The displayed supremum representation is valid.
\(\bar\lambda\) is dual-optimal at \(\bar y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: -B^{\mathsf T}\bar\lambda\in\partial v(\bar y).

notation.meaning: convex subdifferential of v at the sampled point

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Cuts as Value-Function Subgradients

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Monotone Refinement and Finite Polyhedral Cut Generation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convergence interface for exact cut refinement of a polyhedral value function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\widehat v_T=\max_{t\le T}\ell_t\) and \(\ell_{T+1}\le v\), then \[\widehat v_T\le\widehat v_{T+1}\le v.\] Suppose the relevant value function is the maximum of finitely many affine pieces, all master and subproblem solves are exact, and every nonterminal iteration adds a previously absent piece violated at the current master solution. Then only finitely many cut additions are possible. The procedure terminates with an optimal master solution; if all relevant pieces have been added, \(\widehat v_T=v\) on the relevant domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Valid cuts improve the minorant monotonically. With finitely many relevant affine pieces and exact separation, only finitely many new cuts can be generated before optimal termination.
assumptions_latex: Every generated cut is globally valid.
The relevant value function has finitely many affine pieces.
Master and subproblem solves and separation are exact.
Each nonterminal iteration adds a previously absent violated piece.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat v_T\le\widehat v_{T+1}\le v\text{ and only finitely many nonterminal cut additions occur}.

notation.meaning: valid affine minorant added at iteration t

knowledge_statements.title: Monotone Refinement and Finite Polyhedral Cut Generation

children.title: Master-Space Reformulation Link
children.top_down_role: Connection between subproblem information and master-space representations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimality-gap certificate linking a relaxed master to an evaluated feasible solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\widehat v\le v\) on \(Y\) and \(L=\inf_{y\in Y}\{g(y)+\widehat v(y)\}\). Then \(L\le p^*:=\inf_{y\in Y}\{g(y)+v(y)\}\). For any \(\bar y\in Y\) with finite evaluable \(v(\bar y)\), \(U=g(\bar y)+v(\bar y)\) satisfies \(p^*\le U\). Hence \(L\le p^*\le U\), and \(U-L\le\varepsilon\) certifies \(\varepsilon\)-optimality of \(\bar y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut-relaxed master supplies a lower bound and any evaluated feasible master point supplies an upper bound; their gap certifies approximate optimality.
assumptions_latex: \(\widehat v(y)\le v(y)\) for all \(y\in Y\).
\(v(\bar y)<+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L\le p^*\le U,\qquad U-L\le\varepsilon\implies g(\bar y)+v(\bar y)\le p^*+\varepsilon.
knowledge_statements.title: Master Lower–Upper Bound Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary for identifying a lifted projection with a value-function epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v(y)=\inf\{f(x):x\in X,\ Ax+By=b\}\). Without attainment, the projection of \(\{(x,y,\theta):x\in X,\ Ax+By=b,\ f(x)\le\theta\}\) contains every \((y,\theta)\) with \(\theta>v(y)\) but can omit \((y,v(y))\). Equality with \(\operatorname{epi}v\) therefore requires attainment at finite values; identification with a closed epigraph additionally requires the corresponding closedness qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonattainment can remove boundary points from the projected master epigraph, so exact equality needs attainment and, when closure is asserted, closedness.
assumptions_latex: \(v(y)=\inf\{f(x):x\in X,\ Ax+By=b\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{proj}_{y,\theta}\{(x,y,\theta):f(x)\le\theta,\ Ax+By=b\}\subsetneq\operatorname{epi}v\text{ can occur}.

notation.meaning: epigraph of the subproblem value function

knowledge_statements.title: Projection Closure and Attainment Boundary
Master-Space Reformulation Link
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact epigraphic master reformulation before replacing the value function by cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the infimum defining \(v(y)\) is attained whenever \(v(y)<+\infty\). Eliminating \(x\) from the coupled formulation then yields the exact master-space problem \[\inf_{y\in Y}\bigl(g(y)+v(y)\bigr)=\inf_{y\in Y,\,\theta\in\mathbb{R}}\{g(y)+\theta:\theta\geq v(y)\}.\] Moreover, the epigraph of \(v\) is exactly the projection onto the \((y,\theta)\)-space of \[\{(x,y,\theta):x\in X,\ y\in Y,\ Ax+By=b,\ f(x)\leq\theta\}.\] Replacing the epigraph constraint by valid dual cuts gives a relaxation of this exact master representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When each finite subproblem value is attained, projecting out the subproblem variables gives an exact master problem whose value-function epigraph constraint can be relaxed using Benders cuts.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(Y\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m\) are the subproblem- and master-variable domains.
\(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) and \(g:Y\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\), and \(v(y)=\inf\{f(x):x\in X,\ Ax+By=b\}\), with \(v(y)=+\infty\) when the subproblem is infeasible.
Whenever \(v(y)<+\infty\), the infimum defining \(v(y)\) is attained.
The original problem minimizes \(g(y)+f(x)\) over \(x\in X\), \(y\in Y\), and \(Ax+By=b\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The two optimization problems have equal infima, their optimal master-variable sets coincide whenever optima exist, and the displayed projection equals \(\operatorname{epi}v\).

notation.meaning: Epigraph variable for the subproblem value.
